title: Kinetic Profile::brake reverses when the motion's decel exceeds the brake's own amax
description: Found by bd val-1w8's tests (Kinetic 3c85cff, include/kinetic2/profile.hpp Profile::brake). When b0 (the current decel, decel-positive frame) is above L.amax, t1 = (A - b0)/J clamps to 0 and the trapezoid branch holds b0, not A, for t2 = speed/A: the velocity passes zero and the brake accelerates the other way for the rest of t2. Repro through the arbiter: window [92,176], rail 268.11, jog 200 mm/s and 200 mm/s^2, input amax 20 mm/s^2; a jog 134 -> 176 paused while decelerating (at 165 mm, ~61 mm/s): brakeToRest() plans at the input set, the brake reverses and runs to -258 mm at -330 mm/s. Reachable whenever the brake's limits are lower than the ones the motion was planned under: PAUSE after a jog whose amax exceeds the input amax, an input amax lowered mid-motion, the starved-timeline brake after a setConfig. The position backstop (val-1w8) holds the carriage at the window edge, so it no longer reaches a stop, but the brake is wrong: it should ramp the decel down to A first (or brake at b0's own level). Fix belongs in Kinetic (sibling repo), then a pin bump.
notes: Kinetic a9958a0 (pushed): Profile::brake from a deceleration above the brake's amax now ramps the deceleration to amax under jmax, holds it and ramps out, so the entry velocity never changes sign; before, it held the entry deceleration for the hold the ceiling sized (the rig's 200 mm/s jog paused under 20 mm/s^2 ran to -258 mm). Doctest 'a brake under a lower amax than the deceleration in flight never reverses (Nucleus val-9z5)' asserts the rig's entry (v 0.75, a -0.75, amax 0.075, jmax 5e6/268): v never below 0, end ahead by at most v^2/(2 amax) + v amax/(2 jmax) + the ramp-in travel, |a| <= amax after the ramp. Caveat: below b0^2/(2 jmax) of speed a reversal is unavoidable under the jerk ceiling (the overshoot branch, unchanged). Lands in Nucleus with the kinetic.pin bump to a9958a0.
close_reason: Fixed in Kinetic a9958a0 (Profile::brake ramps a deceleration above the brake's amax down under jmax first); pinned in Nucleus since kinetic.pin ace0570, now 2518117 (3db0727). The arbiter repro (window 92..176, jog 134 to 176 paused while decelerating) is in test_motion_arbiter and passes.

title: CANON FLAG: the absolute position backstop's only home is the LP core (a step fence); doctrine says the LP core renders edges and nothing else
description: Operator ruling 2026-10-06: no possible way to leave the window or the rail end under any circumstance (override, homing excepted). bd val-1w8 lands the backstop in MotionArbiter::evaluate(): the demand is clamped to the frame and every steer is wall-bounded over kTickDtCapS (2 ms). That is absolute only while the motion task ticks within 2 ms. Between ticks the LP core renders the last steer open loop, so ANY HP stall carries the carriage v x stall: a window solve on the tick (283 ms measured), a flash write with the cache off (the HP side is unreachable, the LP side is not; ~1 s of every 5 s under the bench flash hammer), a higher-priority task. The only place a fence holds regardless of the HP side is the LP core: two shared words g_lo/g_hi (steps, single writer: the arbiter on the motion task), checked once per edge outside the fine wait, an edge past the fence not emitted (counted). Conflicts: architecture.md section 2 'carries a velocity and flags'; motion-control.md 'renders edges and does nothing else', and the DIG-694 loop-shape evidence needs a re-scope after any loop change. Needs an operator ruling and a C-7 amendment before code.
close_reason: Resolved by operator ruling 2026-10-06 ('there should be absolutely no possible way for the machine to leave the specified window or end of the rail under any circumstance (other than override, homing and cases where it makes sense)'; 'go' on the LP core getting two bounds and nothing else). Doctrine amended in the same commit: motion-control.md and architecture.md section 2 now read 'the LP core renders edges inside its fence while its lease is fresh, and nothing else', citing the ruling. Landed: LP fence (g_fence_lo/g_fence_hi in g_pos's frame, checked once per edge after the coarse wait, outside the fine wait; an edge past it withheld and counted in g_fence_hits, the period unchanged), written by MotionArbiter::syncFence() before every nonzero steer (backstop frame rounded outward by under a step; the home search frame during a cycle), narrowing bound first with memory fences (LpEmitter::fence()); LP lease (g_lease renewed by evaluate() every tick; unrenewed for kLeaseCycles = 4 ms the core stores 0 to g_step_q8 and counts g_lapses; unleased until the first renewal). Census lease_lapses and fence_hits, status line lapses= fence=. Pushback recorded: _p_cmd_mm is NOT re-anchored on a lapse (a stall inside the drain re-anchored steered -600 mm/s against a 223 mm/s plan; without it +195.8 mm/s). Evidence [verified 2026-10-06 -- pinned Kinetic 3c85cff]: test_motion_arbiter 60/60, 3574 assertions; pio test -e native 26/26 suites on a pinned copy; a 3.9 ms stall carries a steer past the window and the count stops exactly on the fence (36716), 13 edges withheld (rig without the fence: 13 steps past); a 283 ms stall moves the carriage 0.896 mm at 223.5 mm/s (4 ms of the held steer) then steers 233 mm/s; the incident stall storm keeps the carriage in [92.0003, 176] with lapses == injected stalls; a home cycle is never fenced; sim scrub p4cfg 501 sent, 0 NACK, pos max 176.00 (was 176.04); flagship_p4_bench builds (RAM 19.1%, flash 31.0%), LP image 8128 B embedded before and after (.text 2428 -> 2584 B); per-edge path +18 instructions (43 -> 61), one of them between the fine wait's exit and the edge store; canon_lint pin findings only. Follow-ups: val-3ty (bench re-scope), val-4rr (flash write vs lease).

title: The window solve leaves the motion tick: a bounded or resumable solve (Kinetic hook) and the planner's own task
description: bd val-1w8 follow-up. The window solve runs on the 1 ms motion tick, unbounded: host measurement of the incident's jog scrub (20 Hz Manual moves, window [92,176], rail 268.11, jog 200/200) is 16 ms average and 21 ms max per solve on x86 with the timeline full at 64 knots; the P4 measured 283 ms. A segments-bundle stream peaks at 4.4 ms on the host. While a solve runs the emitter renders the last steer open loop, so no tick-level rule bounds travel during it. Needs from Kinetic (sibling repo, its own bead): a per-call work budget or a resumable solve (Engine::solveStep(budget) that advances the pending-window solve in bounded slices while stateAt() keeps rendering the committed curve), so a planner task below the tick can own the engine and the tick reads a committed piece. Without a bounded solve, a planner task trades the stall for a hand-off discontinuity (the re-plan origin is react_us ahead of the submit, the publish lands a solve later). Call site: MotionArbiter::sampleEngine().
notes:
2026-10-08 design, after the handle renderer (Kinetic 266b650, 0.1.24): the P4's extension (PIE, csr_pie.h) is 128-bit integer SIMD for neural kernels and does not fit a scalar float solver with branches and divisions; the hardware that fits is the second HP core. Today Motion (prio 6), ValenceHub (5) and Pattern (4) all sit on core 1 and core 0 carries app_main, esp_hosted SDIO, BoardIo, Provision and DriveLink. Plan: a Planner task on core 0 owns the window solve; the motion task never solves, it samples the committed plan. Engine API: solvePending() apart from stateAt(); stateAt samples the last solved window (one solve behind, not one sample behind). Handover: the planner solves from the origin predicted at the reaction horizon (now + react_us, the engine's existing notion), double-buffers Solved and the pieces, and the motion task swaps at the first tick at or past that origin time; a solve that misses its horizon re-solves from the next one. Cost on this host today: a funscript knot 42 us mean / 219 max, a 64-knot bundle 2.3 ms, so on the P4 the plan arrives 1 to 4 ms after a knot and the tick never stalls. Dense sample streams still need kin-j6g.
Operator 2026-10-08: core 0 WILL be busy (the C6 link, the accessory network, BLE, the board services); no planner task there. The way forward is the bead's other option: a resumable solve on core 1, Engine::solveStep(budget) advancing the render in bounded slices (a piece fit, a trim step) while stateAt keeps sampling the last complete render; the budget per tick a machine constant (about 200 us on the P4), the handover at the reaction horizon as noted above.
P4 measured 2026-10-08 on 0.1.26 (Kinetic 1095efd), the hub's own plan_us (EMA over 8 plans): a jog 330 us; a segment stream (the funscript path, 1 Hz sine on a 100 mm window, 10 segments/s) 2.4 ms per knot, last 6.3 ms; a 50 Hz sample stream 12.9 ms per sample; running max 83 ms (inside a sample stream). The P4 runs this code about 50x slower than the bench host, not the 10-20x assumed: funscript knots stall the tick 2 to 6 ms each a few times a second, sample streams starve it. Jogs are fine.
close_reason: Kinetic 38f3bf1 (Engine::peek) and Nucleus 8d6f516: the planner task (prio 5) owns the engine and publishes a 128 ms strip; the steer task (prio 6) steers, fences and renews every tick from it; late plans become residuals; the steer cap follows the jog set. Host-verified only (test_motion_arbiter 69 cases, 68 pass, the one failure from the uncommitted valence_config.h factory-set change; wasm trace byte-identical; flagship_p4_bench builds, no .tbss). Not flashed; kinetic.pin bump to 38f3bf1 is the operator's.

title: Motion backstop: the tick clamps the rendered demand to the active frame, a late tick is a stall never a burst
description: Incident 2026-10-06 (Nucleus 0.1.17, Kinetic 3c85cff): a jog-tape scrub drove the carriage into the end stops twice. 0x1111: plan_us_max 283,030 us (one window solve on the motion task), knot_refused 334, deadline_stretched 426. evaluate() scaled its kick cap and velocity cap with the measured dt (0.283 s -> 14,150 / 15,150 mm/s) and nothing clamped the rendered position to the window or the rail: the window clamp held intent targets only. Build: a position backstop in evaluate() (window, or the asserted rail under override and return; homing bypasses), a dt cap derived from kMotionTickUs with a late tick counted as a stall and re-anchored, a census counter for both on the status line, tests in test_motion_arbiter, the sim scrub, docs.
close_reason: Landed: position backstop in MotionArbiter::evaluate() (demand clamped to the window, or the asserted rail in the rail frame, ratcheted to the previous demand; wall bound from position truth over kTickDtCapS), stall rule (kick and velocity cap priced over kTickDtCapS = 2 x kMotionTickUs; late ticks counted), census stalls/backstops on the status line, plan.flags clamped while held. Evidence [verified 2026-10-06 -- test_motion_arbiter 54/54, 3493 assertions, pinned Kinetic 3c85cff]: a PAUSE brake planned to 241.3 mm held the carriage at 176.000 (HEAD: 241.35); a 283 ms stall with the emitter frozen steers 233 mm/s (HEAD: 2020.6); the incident scrub in a 3 s stall storm stays in [92.0003, 176] (HEAD: [-638.9, 717.7], both rail ends); isolated 283 ms stalls reach [89.0, 185.9], the open-loop hold val-fi5 owns. Sim scrub p4cfg: 323 sent, 0 NACK, pos max 176.04, 0 rail excursions. Firmware flagship_p4_bench builds against pinned Kinetic (RAM 19.1%, flash 30.9%). Follow-ups: val-8rt (solve off the tick), val-fi5 (LP fence flag), val-9z5 (Kinetic brake reversal), val-d11 (jog chain), val-x2o (sim tick cadence).

title: Window drag mid-stream: after a 400 mm/s drag stops, the plan overshoots and reverses at about -336 mm/s (retarget chases moving knots)
description: Found by the val-8es agent 2026-10-09 (test_motion_arbiter val-17u sweep with the window dragged 80 mm in 40 writes; old code does the same). Each window write reseeds the plan with velocity scaled by the span ratio while every pending knot (window shares) moves with the window, so the carriage chases moving targets and overshoots when the drag stops. Operator-visible (dragging the window during playback is the val-17u feature). Investigate: reseed velocity restatement, limits scaling, whether consecutive reseeds should rate-limit (one per planner tick, coalesce writes), or the frame move should be applied as a smooth window transition. Acceptance: same sweep, no reversal after the drag beyond the kin-554 tolerance, no ceiling excursion.
close_reason: Nucleus 2272b8f + Kinetic cdfb47a (Engine::reframe, RFC-105 (bb) on a frame move): drag sweep at every phase, no backward travel (was 4.88 mm, -336 mm/s), live at the kinetic.pin bump

description:

Nucleus implements them at its next valence.pin bump (operator's say; canon_lint pin-mismatch is the reminder) and its next kinetic.pin bump. title: A Manual point move submitted while a plan moves runs the plan away (3 km at 302 m/s at the old defaults), and a census read changes the outcome
description:
Found while landing val-sgj (factory input set 1200 mm/s, 100000 mm/s2, 2e7 mm/s3). Reproduced in the native rig of test_motion_arbiter (Rig, forceHome(500), setWindow(100, 200, 400), run(1000)) at HEAD 59bca46 and on the working tree, with the OLD defaults and the new ones. The carriage is held at the window edge only by the position backstop (backstops 1); the plan itself diverges.

Case F, a Manual point move while a stream plan is moving:
  submit(Stream, 250) ; run(100 ms) ; submit(Manual, 390) ; run 10 s
  old defaults (1000, 50000, 5e6): plan peak 2,978,780 mm, |v| peak 302,457 mm/s, target 2.29e8 mm
  new defaults (1200, 100000, 2e7): plan peak 1,074,850 mm, |v| peak 108,885 mm/s, target 2.96e7 mm
  (Manual alone, Stream alone, Stream then Manual in the same tick: all clean.)

Case G/H, a census read changes the plan:
  submit(Stream, 250) ; run(1 ms) ; submit(Stream, 20) ; census() ; submit(Manual, 390) ; run 10 s
  old: plan runs to 3506.95 mm at up to 1181 mm/s, comes to rest inside 10 s
  new: plan runs to 37260.8 mm (target 55918.1) at up to 4726 mm/s, still moving at 10 s
  Without the census() read the same sequence is clean (plan peak 200 mm). MotionArbiter::snapshot() is not side-effect free.

Visible symptom: test_motion_arbiter "window clamp: every source held in the window; the jog under override reaches the rail" fails at REQUIRE(r->submit(MotionSource::Manual, 390.0f)) after override() under the new factory jerk, because the runaway plan is still moving at 10 s and the jog is refused (jog waits for the pause brake to finish). Under the old defaults it passes only because that runaway comes to rest in time. Do not fix the test by pinning the old limits: the plan divergence is the bug.

On hardware the emitter would drive the carriage at its ceiling into the window edge and the fence would stop it there. P0 candidate: the operator's call.
notes: Root cause (2026-10-08): two layers. Kernel (Kinetic kin-v9z, 06673ee): hardKnot() fell back to the time-fixed render when Profile::point from the live state broke a ceiling or the window; a jog's knot is one tick out, so the render's end state carried a = 20869 window units/s2 (jog amax 2) and the starvation brake from it ramped that out at jmax first (v += a^2/2J), then stopped at the jog amax: the runaway. Arbiter: the Manual branch put the jog set (50 mm/s, 200 mm/s2) on motion planned under the input set (1200 mm/s); no jog profile from that state stops inside the window (3.6 m). Census: snapshot() sampled the engine, which solved a dirty window under the input set and closed the engine's re-plan undo; without the read the solve ran under the jog set and the undo committed the chase whole (clean by accident). Fixed in f7a27ea: Manual over a non-jog plan brakes at the input set first (PAUSE's brake) and jogs from its end; the steer cap takes the jog set when that brake ends (the old cap stepped the emitter 1050 mm/s in one tick); snapshot() reads planStep()'s cached sample, never the engine. Also kernel: a knot submitted during an explicit brake dropped the brake (plan stepped to its end): fixed in 06673ee. Veto-able: a Manual move during a stream/pattern now stops that motion first (as PAUSE does) instead of handing off at the reaction horizon. Host-verified only; bench smoke owed at the flash. Follow-up: Kinetic kin-g1f (HARD knot committed through on its authored time).
close_reason: Fixed: Kinetic 06673ee (kin-v9z) + Nucleus f7a27ea (kinetic.pin 06673ee). Host suites green; bench smoke owed at the flash.

title: max_rail can be raised above the measured stroke after a real home: a config-set key 8 clamps only to the catalog ceiling (500), so the fence and window may be set past the physical stop
description: Found 2026-10-08 on the machine: the home cycle adopts the measured usable rail (267.69 mm) into max_rail (ValenceDevice::adoptMeasuredRail), but applyConfig case 8 clamps a later config-set to ceiling::rail_mm (500), not to census.home_rail_mm, so a client (or tools/aim/hub_config.py's factory defaults, max_rail 500) can push max_rail and with it the window and the LP fence past the stop the home cycle found. title: Position truth drifts from the drive's encoder above about 1600 mm/s cruise (3.9 mm per 600 mm leg; 11.7 mm at 2500-3000)
description: Bench 2026-10-07 (same setup as the emitter-cap bug). Up to 1440 mm/s cruise the hub's quadrature count and the drive's own encoder agree to 0.05 mm over a 600 mm leg. At 1630 mm/s cruise (jog 2000, 0x02=1500) the hub count ends 3.9 mm short of the encoder every fast leg, sign following the direction; at 2500-3000 commanded 11.7 mm. The hub then believes it is short and pushes the carriage past the real target: on the machine a fast script walks the carriage toward an end over many strokes. Not yet known whether the LP quadrature decoder (lp_quad.c) misses edges at 1.3 M edges/s or the drive's encoder OUTPUT drops edges; needs the scope on A/B at 1600 mm/s. Until known, treat 1500 mm/s as the ceiling of trustworthy position truth.
close_reason: Retracted 2026-10-07: measurement artifact. The hub has no encoder input (operator: five wires, A/B out, home interrupt in); its 'pos' is the LP emitter's own edge count. The 3.9/11.7 mm 'drift' came from reading the drive's encoder while the hub was still creeping on legs that never settled. Traced legs show the drive's encoder landing on the hub's emitted count to 0.01 mm at every speed, including 626 kHz bursts.

title: LP emitter sustains about 2200 mm/s (460 kHz), not its 1 MHz floor; a plan above it falls behind and the residual catch-up at amax x 1 ms crawls
description: Bench 2026-10-07, traced (scratchpad tr_unc.json / tr_cap.json, session 44929813): jog 3000 mm/s over 600 mm. The plan finishes in 0.23 s but the LP count reaches only about 450 of 600 mm by then: the emitter averaged about 2200 mm/s (460 kHz edges) against 3000 commanded, so the LP core's real ceiling is near 460 kHz at 40 MHz, far under kMinCyclesPerEdge's 1 MHz. Then the plan's velocity is 0 and the only thing moving the count is the residual kick, capped at inputAmax x dt where dt is the 1 ms tick: 100 mm/s at input_accel 100000, 10 mm/s at 10000, so the last 160 mm take 1.6 s or time out. The DRIVE is not the problem: its encoder lands on the hub's count to 0.01 mm after every burst, including 626 kHz, its own motor speed clamp (0x02 = 1500 rpm = 982 mm/s at 39.27 mm/rev) just makes it catch up later. What to do: (1) the plan's speed ceiling must be the LP emitter's measured rate at this gear (about 2000 mm/s with margin), as a machine constant, so the count never falls behind the plan; (2) decide whether a shortfall should be closed at plan speed rather than amax x 1 ms. Earlier text of this bead (pulse drops at the drive input) was wrong.
notes:
Operator 2026-10-07: the hub has no knowledge of the drive dropping pulses. Refinement: it sees the shortfall (err_mm is what the tracking kick acts on) but cannot tell loss from lag, and the cure for lag (more velocity) is the cause of loss. No detection is needed: the bandwidth is the drive's datasheet number (500 kHz) and the gear is already read from the drive at boot, so the ceiling is computable, v = 500e3 / steps_per_mm (2397 mm/s at 4/1; 2000 with margin). The catalog max of input_speed and jog_speed should follow it instead of MAX_SPEED_MM_S 10000, so clients see the real ceiling. Position truth drifting above 1600 mm/s (val-o8y) argues for the lower number until that is answered.
Implemented 2026-10-07 (uncommitted): MAX_SPEED_MM_S 10000 -> 2000 (valence_config.h) and the catalog's ceiling::speed_max to match, so input_speed, jog_speed and home speed can never ask the LP for more than it sustains; the steer-word floor comment in MotionArbiter.h now states the measured rate. Left open: whether a shortfall should close at plan speed instead of amax x 1 ms (only reachable now through a lapse).

2026-10-08: (1) done: MAX_SPEED_MM_S 2000 in valence_config.h and the catalog ceiling (Nucleus 49052b4, 0.1.23). (2) still open: whether a shortfall closes at plan speed rather than amax x 1 ms is the operator's call; with val-8rt (the solve off the tick) the residual's main cause, a solve stalling the tick, goes away.

title: RFC-087 supersede flush is not implemented: a new segments bundle must replace queued, not-yet-started segments from its first start; Kinetic² refuses a knot that is not after the newest, so a funscript seek or stop waits out the queue or is refused
description: SPEC 'Supersede, the segments flush' (RFC-087, SPEC.md line 333 as of Valence 752b9d1): a newly accepted bundle on a segments channel replaces every scheduled, not-yet-started segment from the same source whose start is at or after the new bundle's first start (t_base); a segment already executing hands off at that start. Found by the Phosphor funscript twin port (ph-82cx, 2026-10-06): the player's seek and stop rely on it. Neither the Valence hub library (hub_impl.hpp handles the RFC-087 horizon and lead cap only) nor MotionArbiter/ValenceDevice implements the replace; kinetic2::Engine::submit refuses a knot that is not after the newest one (kDetailPast), so a seek's fresh segments are refused until the queue drains (up to the 250 ms horizon). Needed: on a c2h segments bundle, the arbiter retires every pending knot of that source with start >= t_base before submitting the bundle (Kinetic² has the timeline; add a truncate-after(t) that keeps the piece in flight and re-plans from the reaction horizon, RFC-105 (bb)), with a motion-arbiter case: queue 250 ms of segments, send a bundle starting 40 ms out, the plan follows the new bundle from its first start and nothing is refused. The library side may need the hook (Valence RFC territory if the wire changes; it should not).
close_reason: RFC-087 supersede flush landed, 0.1.14. ValenceDevice::onStreamBundle marks the first segment a segments bundle hands the motion path (MotionIntent::supersede); MotionArbiter::submitKnots truncates the Kinetic² timeline at that segment's start (Engine::truncateAfter, Kinetic 7e5f5fb, kinetic.pin moved) and chains the bundle from the hand-off, never a rest. Samples never flush. Verified 2026-10-06 -- pio test -e native 26/26 suites: test_motion_arbiter RFC-087 case hands off at 25.8 mm moving 206 mm/s, 100 ms later 23.7 mm on the new bundle, end 20.0 mm at rest, jump at submit 0 mm, per tick beyond velocity 5.2e-5 mm, rejected 0, failures 0, KnotRefused 0; VD-SEG-1 flag on the first taken segment only. title: [bug] CANON FLAG: Kinetic² at e5ab493 is not motor-ready: a spent sample stream jumps (22-68 mm/tick), far samples drop, sweeps diverge and refuse; unspecified segment end velocity breaks SPEC 9.6
description:
CANON FLAG raised 2026-10-06 by the val-klo follow-up agent; pending operator ruling. Blocks running flagship_p4_kinetic2 on a motor and blocks val-2lv's bench A/B.

Measured at kinetic.pin e5ab493 through MotionArbiter (pio test -e native_kinetic2 -f native/test_motion_arbiter; the failing cases are committed, unrelaxed, as the evidence) and on the bare kinetic2::Engine<1> (probe, not committed):

1. Continuity breaks once anything is spent. A 60 Hz sample scrub (a 150 mm/s ramp, a hold, a 1.5 Hz sweep of 60 mm; input set ceilings 1000 mm/s, 50000 mm/s2, 2e6 mm/s3 on a 400 mm window) jumps 22.4 mm in one 1 ms tick beyond its velocity, refuses 41 samples, fails 2 knots (case "Kinetic² continuity", scrub subcase; 29b0083). The ramp-to-hold spend alone turns the plan back (-28 mm/s on a monotone stream) and then steps it 3.37 mm in one tick. Bare kernel, same normalized ceilings (2.5, 125, 5000), no Nucleus code: 68 mm (Stretch) / 61 mm (Blend) in one tick. Segments without spends are continuous (0.0019 mm).
2. A sample 100 mm or more from a carriage at rest is dropped (PlanFailed) and a stream that starts that far away never moves (cases "a power loss mid-move ..." and "a stream sample under PAUSE ... resume does"). Lone 20 mm and 50 mm samples land Blend-trimmed (19.76, 35.4 mm).
3. A feasible sweep (1.5 Hz, 20 or 60 mm; 0.5 Hz, 60 mm) diverges 39 to 207 mm from the stream and refuses 60 to 90 of 300 samples after 2-3 s; 0.25 Hz of 20 mm follows within 1.5 mm.
Hypothesis, NOT verified in the kernel source: a free last knot's velocity is fixed (its secant at the submitted time) before the spend and is not re-derived when Stretch moves the knot, so a stretched knot arrives at a speed its new time cannot honor; the referee calls a turn-back legal (window and ceilings only) and accumulated stretches back the timeline up.

4. SPEC 9.6: "Without a scheduled successor the hub MUST resolve unspecified to rest (0)". At e5ab493 a segment knot with an unspecified end velocity and no successor keeps its secant (RFC-105 (dd)) and the engine brakes past the target: a 50 mm segment ends at 50.707 mm (case "Kinetic² segments: a start past the newest knot holds until it"). The arbiter can only conform by authoring rest at every unspecified knot, the chunky shape val-b8x exists to remove; a kernel knot kind "free, but rest if last" would satisfy both. Related: val-091.60.

Your call: (a) fix 1-3 in Kinetic first (the arbiter port waits for the pin), and (b) for 4, a kernel rest-if-last knot kind, or the arbiter authoring rest for unspecified segments until it exists?

2026-10-06 (Kinetic kernel, uncommitted pin): items 1-3 landed as RFC-105 (ff)-(pp): samples are their own knot kind (never trimmed), persisted priors, eased replay compression, minimum-jerk interior junctions, the ladder from a tenth of a tick, and a joint re-solve of the previous sample before a far stretch. title: Kinetic² in the arbiter behind a build switch; kinetic-wasm and Phosphor's pin follow
description: The path by which Kinetic² reaches the machine and Phosphor's preview (the preview is tools/kinetic-wasm = the arbiter compiled to wasm, so it needs no work of its own). Steps: (1) after the Kinetic symlink dependency lands, add kinetic2 to the dependency (same checkout, include/kinetic2). (2) MotionArbiter: a compile-time switch (Kconfig NUCLEUS_KINETIC2 / CMake option, default OFF until the bench rules) selecting kinetic2::Engine<1> in place of kinetic::Engine. Conversions at the boundary, nowhere else: a 0x2101 segment -> knotFromSegment(target, duration, end_vel, anchor, family); a 0x0084 sample and a jog -> knotFromSample(p, arrival, schedule_latency_us) (one sample behind, RFC-105 promise 1); strokes from the generators -> knots at their half-stroke times with the fray-d end velocities; brake() for pause/e-stop/settle; resetAt/reseedAt on the position truth as today. (3) The census: plan_* fields from Engine::solved()/stateAt (start, end, current, velocity, elapsed, duration, style, flags per RFC-100: shaped = WaveformScaled, stretched = DeadlineStretched, clamped = EndVelClamped, fallback never); anomalies keep their kinds (0..10 Kinetic 1's, 11 KnotRefused appended to the 0x0088 field list and SM_ANOM_KINDS). (4) kinetic_tuning (52 B) maps onto kinetic2::Config: infeasible_policy, amplitude_budget -> amplitude_floor, the chase_* members are accepted and ignored under Kinetic² (document in tools/kinetic-wasm/README), plus new members appended for lookahead_us and corner; kinetic_version() says which kernel. (5) Build both kernels in CI; valencesim gets the same switch so the Mac/Linux benches can A/B. (6) Phosphor: node test/kinetic-pin.mjs --write with the switch ON produces the Kinetic² bytes.js; the funscript analyzer and the RFC-105 tuner read the version string. Acceptance: the native trace suite passes with both kernels (separate fixtures), the P4 compiles both, the bench (val-2lv when the Flagship exists) decides the default.
notes:
Steps 1-4 landed behind NUCLEUS_KINETIC2, default OFF (this commit). Homes: the switch ValenceMotion.h (kKinetic2, kAnomalyKinds 12 under it); Kconfig NUCLEUS_KINETIC2 (P4 env flagship_p4_kinetic2 via the kinetic2.sdkconfig.defaults overlay: custom_sdkconfig is arduino-only on platform 55.03.39), CMake option for valencesim (build-k2) and kinetic-wasm (build-k2), pio env native_kinetic2. Boundary: MotionArbiter.cpp 'the Kinetic² boundary'. Segment = knotFromSegment at start+duration, a start past the newest knot holds at rest until it; Stream sample = knotFromSample at arrival + sampleLatencyUs(tuning) (one home with the hub's grant); Manual (jog, return, homing) = knotFromSample with the park time (RFC-105 (k)) from the newest knot, policy forced Stretch; Pattern/Advanced point = brake; PAUSE/home stall/timeout = brake; a last knot due and still moving = brake from its own time (SettleEngaged). title: RFC-085: PAUSE is the one non-emergency latch; STOP and HOLD retire, RESUME is the only clear

title: Motor switch at runtime: FLT and IMON reads, EN-node drop detection, latch-off re-arm, motion gated on motor power
description:
Board fact (Hardware flagship/SPEC.md 2026-09-22 motor-switch row, 2026-09-23 bus-OVP row, 2026-09-23 board-monitor row, 2026-09-23 24-36 V row): the motor switch controller (U2, TPS48111) takes MOTOR_EN on G21 (INP, 100k pull-down R409) and PRECHARGE_EN on G22 (INP_G, 100k pull-down R410). It reports MSW_FLT_N on G20 (FLT_T and FLT_I tied, 10k pull-up R411; see Hardware hw-3qf) and MSW_IMON on G19 (ADC1). Its EN/UVLO node, the wired-OR every hardware kill pulls (INA ALERT, bus OVP trip Q405, E-stop Q901, board monitor FAULT_N through R1121), reads on G23 (ADC1; ~1.8 V running, ~0 V tripped, 3.31 V at 55 V after the R408 change). Over-current LATCHES OFF and firmware re-arms by toggling MOTOR_EN.

Today: BoardPins.h names every pin; the boot self-check holds G21/G22 low and reads G20 once. Nothing runs after boot.

Owed: (1) the pre-charge then enable sequence (PRECHARGE_EN high, ~75 ms window per design-considerations.md section 4, MOTOR_V+ seen rising on the power monitor, then MOTOR_EN high, IMON sane) once val-091.21's table can pass; (2) EN-node and FLT watch at runtime: a drop reads the board monitor's latched fault code and the INA DIAG_ALRT (powerTakeAlerts) and names the cause over Valence; (3) the re-arm path (powerTakeAlerts then a MOTOR_EN toggle, never one alone, ValencePower.h); (4) the arbiter refuses motion while motor power is off, so the LP emitter never renders into an unpowered drive. Safety-relevant.

title: E-stop inputs at runtime: read NC/NO, latch ESTOP in the arbiter on a hardware stop, never resume on release, bypass policy
description:
Board fact (Hardware flagship/SPEC.md 2026-09-23 external wired E-stop row, amended by the 2026-09-28 pinout rows and the 2026-10-01 NO-closed trip row): the E-stop jack (J9 PH3, and the daughterboard M8 J3 in parallel) cuts motor power in HARDWARE through Q901 on the motor-switch EN node; no firmware is in that path. Firmware reads NC on G39 (ESTOP_NC) and NO on G30 (ESTOP_NO) through 1k series with 2.2k pull-ups: (NC,NO) 0/1 normal, 1/0 pressed, 1/1 unplugged, 0/0 wiring fault. G29 (ESTOP_BYP, 100k pull-down) drives the bypass that masks ONLY an unplugged cable; every reset clears it. SPEC: "Releasing the button restores motor power: firmware must not resume motion by itself."

Today: BoardPins.h names the three pins; the boot self-check (val-091.21) holds the bypass low and decodes the pair once at boot (selfcheck::decodeEStop). Nothing reads them at runtime.

Owed: (1) a runtime reader (edge interrupt, or a poll on a task that is not the motion task) that latches ESTOP through the MotionArbiter when the hardware stop opens, so the plan stops before position truth diverges from a drive that just lost power; (2) never clearing that latch on release (the 0x0005 estop_clear path stays the only door); (3) the bypass as a single-session, configure-gated toggle, off at boot; (4) the 'no E-stop found' warning published over Valence. Safety-relevant: a hardware stop the firmware does not notice leaves the LP emitter rendering into an unpowered drive.

title: Accessory e-stop fan-out over ESP-NOW, both directions (RFC-053)
description:
Accessory e-stop fan-out over ESP-NOW, RFC-053 (ACCEPTED 2026-07-29: opt-out, default ON, NVS-persisted, catalog-exposed setting, plus a build flag that compiles the path out; the ESP-NOW half "remains unimplemented in the reference firmware").

Both directions:
- Hub -> accessories: on e-stop latch, the spoke task sends the RFC-053 ESTOP frame (SPEC section 5.5: E5 E5 E5 E5, cause, origin, seq, CRC-32 over the first 8 pre-COBS bytes) as an ESP-NOW broadcast AHEAD of every queued frame, repeated until the latch clears or N repeats, and does not wait for the next beacon. Every accessory treats it as goodbye: safe state now.
- Accessory -> hub: an Isotope e-stop fob (or any accessory with a stop button) broadcasts the same frame; the hub validates magic + CRC and latches through the same path every other e-stop origin takes (MotionArbiter owns the gate; architecture.md section 2), with the origin recorded.
- The receive side validates in the spoke task and posts one message to the hub; no hub state is touched from the esp_hosted RX callback (T5).
- The ESTOP frame's bytes come from the Valence registry/codec (never a local copy).

Acceptance: hub e-stop reaches every paired accessory's safe state within the V2-measured RTT bound; a fob press latches the machine; the setting off suppresses both directions and is visible in every client.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6 + two ESP32 boards: one stand-in accessory with SAFE_N, one fob sketch with a button + analyzer): 20 hub-side e-stops (Phosphor button) -> SAFE_N falling; 20 fob presses -> P4 census "mot=estop" (analyzer on a P4 debug GPIO toggled at latch in a bench build); 5 of each with the setting off (expect no effect).
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- hub->accessory n=20 max ms, fob->latch n=20 max ms, setting-off 0/10, RFC-053]
acceptance_criteria: Hub e-stop reaches accessory safe state and a fob latches the machine, both measured n=20; setting off suppresses both.

Pause is NOT broadcast: it reaches accessories through the RFC-078 interlock as commanded safe values (val-9u0.13).

title: Join/declaration handling and the userspace accessory store (data partition + PSRAM, StoredState-style codec)
description:
Join and declaration handling, and the userspace accessory store.

Join: during an open pairing window the hub accepts a join request, receives the accessory's declaration (its baked mini-catalog: channels, types, ranges, deadman-safe values), assigns a channel slice in the user channel space, stores it, and adds the peer (20-peer ceiling; typical 3). Outside a window, a known accessory (by MAC and stored identity) re-attaches without pairing; an unknown one is ignored. No encryption (ruling).

Store (extends the StoredState pattern, it does not reuse its blob):
- Hardware-free codec, header-only, [magic u32][version u8], exact-length decode, REJECT WHOLE on any mismatch (StoredState.h rules); the host twin (sim/valencesim) and a native suite run the same codec.
- Flash: a new data partition in the reserved tail of flagship_p4/partitions.csv at the size V5 chose, NOT NVS (24 KB, already holding cfg + presets). A partition-table change needs one serial flash; otadata and the app slots do not move.
- PSRAM: unpacked at boot before the hub is constructed (the catalog must be final before Hub encodes it: ValenceHub.cpp construction order), placement-new into the PSRAM box (T2).
- Writes on the hub task only, held while OTA is in flight (same rule as persistDue()); a join is one write.
- Hub-authored data (names, relationships) is a separate blob from the accessory's declaration: the declaration is the accessory's truth and is replaced whole on a re-join.

Acceptance: join, reboot, accessory re-attaches without pairing and its channels are present; a corrupted store boots with zero accessories and a logged rejection, never a crash; native codec suite exits 0.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp after one serial flash for the partition table + two ESP32 stand-ins with a declaration of 4 and 128 channels): pair both, reboot 10 times, confirm re-attach 10/10 and boot unpack time vs V5; flip one byte of the stored blob with esptool read_flash/write_flash and reboot.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- COM15, pair 2/2, re-attach 10/10, unpack p50/max ms, corrupt blob rejected + boot OK, native <suite> exit 0]
acceptance_criteria: Pair, reboot, re-attach without pairing 10/10; corrupted store rejected whole with a clean boot; native codec suite exits 0.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Rulings 2026-10-01 (RFC-076 rfc-7bq, RFC-077 rfc-cou, RFC-078 rfc-j5f): slices are 32 ids (r=0 session-scoped, r=1 accessory-status, r=2..31 own, 30 channels max) in user space 0x8000-0xBFFF (512 slices, a forgotten slice never reused for the life of a hub); declaration is the accessory's own 8.1 catalog over blob ns0, verified by etag, with a REQUIRED per-field safe value; durable u64 accessory_id; window-free re-join with etag-match skip; hub-side forget only (a forged GOODBYE cannot delete a record); no STORE entries inside a declaration; the hub does not rewrite group strings. The wire surface is the core accessories STORE + roster + accessory-admin INTENT (store verbs per RFC-067, store_id per RFC-070). Capacity refusal is val-9u0.19.

title: Live catalog rebuild on accessory join/leave with the mid-session re-announce (blocked on the Valence live-catalog-growth RFC)
description:
Live catalog rebuild on accessory join/leave, with the mid-session re-announce.

BLOCKED UPSTREAM on the Valence RFC to be drafted as "Live catalog growth: mid-session catalog change and re-announce" (not in RFC-QUEUE.md as of 2026-09-26). Today the catalog is built once in hubBegin() and the Hub constructor encodes it; a changed catalog moves the etag, and nothing in the spec tells a live session the catalog changed under it. Never code against an unaccepted clause.

The RFC must carry CAPACITY as well as growth: valence::Hub binds Catalog32 (48 entries, 200 layout fields, 189 used on this machine) and a 32,768 B encode scratch, both inside Valence's frozen hub.hpp/catalog.hpp (C-6: touching them needs the operator's explicit "yes, break compatibility"). ~128 channels per accessory cannot fit without that. Candidate shapes for the RFC: a hub templated on its catalog type; or accessory channels as a separately encoded, separately etagged catalog segment so the machine's own etag never moves when a pump joins.

Nucleus side once the RFC lands: rebuild on the hub task only (T5), the catalog is PSRAM-resident (T2), no Catalog-sized temporaries on any stack (T1: never `c = Catalog{}`), and the re-announce reaches parked sessions safely (T13: re-check slot.transport on every fan-out send).
Acceptance: join and leave with two Valence clients connected; both receive the re-announce, refetch, and render the new channels; the machine's own channels keep working throughout; back-to-back sessions without reboot (T3).
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6 + stand-in accessory + Phosphor and valence_probe connected at once): join, leave, rejoin 10 cycles; record re-announce -> client refetch complete time, etag before/after, hub stack high-water during a refetch of the grown catalog.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- 10 cycles, 2 clients, refetch p50/max ms, etags, hub stack deepest free N B, RFC-<nnn> at valence.pin <sha>]
acceptance_criteria: Two live clients see join/leave/rejoin x10 via re-announce and refetch; machine channels unaffected; back-to-back sessions without reboot.
notes: 2026-10-09 triage: still valid; stale text: the live-catalog-growth RFC exists and was ACCEPTED (RFC-077, rfc-077, landed 4c0ede7 on 2026-10-01). The library half is Valence rfc-58u; this bead waits on that, not on a draft.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: UNBLOCKED 2026-10-01: RFC-077 (rfc-cou) ACCEPTED. Only the user space changes at runtime (core and device entries byte-identical across a change); the announcement reuses catalog STATE 0x0001 (subscribing to it becomes a MUST for every client); a user-space change does NOT revoke readiness, sessions refetch in the background and send CATALOG_READY with the new etag; withdrawn grants get one unsolicited NACK CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN each; appeared channels deliver nothing until subscribed; in-flight ns0 transfers aborted by the one 8.4 NACK. No base etag; degraded mode is the answer for pinned clients. Capacity is now a build-time parameter (val-9u0.20), so the Catalog32 wall named above goes away with it. The library half (hub re-announce, CHANNEL_WITHDRAWN) is Valence's reference-library live-growth bead.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Upstream library half filed on the Valence board as rfc-58u (2026-10-01); consume it at the valence.pin bump that carries it.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Library side landed (Valence fd36721, rfc-58u): the host must call addCatalogChannel(), markUserSpace() after its own entries, hub.catalogChanged() after every join, replace or forget, and size VALENCE_RETAINED_STATES above the 25 STATE channels it already uses or accessories exhaust the retained-state pool.

title: CustomRpc ESP-NOW shim as a Nucleus component (license checked; PR 17712's three review defects fixed)
description:
The CustomRpc ESP-NOW shim as a Nucleus component (esp_now_* on the P4, forwarded to the C6 over esp_hosted CustomRpc), wire-compatible with the image adopted in the C6-image bead.

Design constraints:
- LICENSE FIRST: ESPHome's C++ runtime is, to my reading, GPLv3 (unverified; check the repo's LICENSE before copying a line). If so, vendoring esp_now_hosted.cpp into Nucleus is a license decision for the operator; the alternative is a clean implementation against the wire contract header esp_now_hosted_rpc.h (whose own license, in esp-hosted-firmware, also needs reading).
- FIX THE THREE PR 17712 REVIEW DEFECTS, or prove V2 did not reproduce them: a lost SEND completion must time out and free the TX slot (never stall forever); the peer mirror must be rebuilt when the C6 restarts (esp_hosted reconnect event); a full peer table must return ESP_ERR_ESPNOW_FULL, not success.
- ONE OWNER TASK (the spoke task in the beacon bead). The shim's receive and send-complete callbacks run on esp_hosted's own RX task (T5): they copy into a fixed-capacity ring and return; they never touch hub state and never allocate.
- Never called from core 1 or from the hub task: an esp_hosted RPC has been measured at 151 ms (ValenceHub.h).
- Fixed-capacity, no per-frame malloc (memory-budget.md "Pools, never per-event malloc"); rings in internal RAM only if a flash-cache-off path can reach them, otherwise PSRAM.

Acceptance: component builds in flagship_p4 with the hub image; the V2 run set A-E passes against the hub image (not the scratch project), with the hub's own WS stream running as the station load.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6 + second ESP32 echo board): rerun V2 A-E on the hub image; in parallel run lag_probe (val-091.13 method) to show the WS motion path is unchanged by ESP-NOW traffic.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- hub image <sha>, V2 A-E RTT/loss, lag_probe sent->pos before/after, E: C6 power-cycle recovered without P4 reboot, 21st peer = ESP_ERR_ESPNOW_FULL]
acceptance_criteria: Builds into the hub image; V2 A-E pass on the hub image; C6 restart recovers without a P4 reboot; 21st peer returns ESP_ERR_ESPNOW_FULL.

title: Spoke task + 1 Hz beacon: core 0, below esp_hosted's tasks, 4 KB internal stack, beacon gated on hub liveness
description:
The spoke task: sole owner of the ESP-NOW shim, and the 1 Hz beacon that is every accessory's deadman.

Placement and why:
- CORE 0. Core 1 carries Motion (prio 6), ValenceHub (prio 5) and Pattern (prio 4), and nothing that can wait on an esp_hosted RPC belongs beside them (151 ms measured). Core 0 already runs app_main and the esp_hosted SDIO service the spoke rides on.
- PRIORITY: above app_main (1), BELOW esp_hosted's own SDIO/RPC tasks, so the spoke can never preempt the transport it depends on. The exact number is read from the esp_hosted Kconfig at implementation and stated on this bead.
- STACK: 4,096 B, internal (task stacks stay internal by ruling; PSRAM is unreachable with the flash cache off). Added to main.cpp's [stack] census; sized by T21 after a join + 50 Hz workload, never down from an idle mark.
- HUB LINK BY MESSAGE, never shared memory (cpp-safety concurrency rule): the hub task posts outbound frames to a fixed queue; received frames go to a fixed ring the hub drains on its tick (T5).
- THE BEACON IS GATED ON HUB LIVENESS: the spoke sends a beacon only while the hub tick counter has advanced since the last beacon (the same proof main.cpp uses for the OTA buy). A hung hub therefore stops the beacon and every accessory goes safe in 5 s; a beacon from a live radio over a dead hub would be the lie.
- Beacon carries the e-stop latch bit and the pairing-window bit; an e-stop does not wait for the next beacon (see the fan-out bead).
- Frame format: blocked on the spoke-wire-format ruling (no code-local wire numbers).

Acceptance: beacon at 1 Hz +/- 10 ms while the hub ticks; a stalled hub stops it; stack census line present.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6 + V4 stand-in accessory + analyzer): rerun V4 steps 1-4 against the hub image; add step 5: halt the hub task from a debug console command (bench build only) and measure BEACON stop -> SAFE_N falling (expect <= 6 s); read the spoke's [stack] high-water after 10 min of V2 run B.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- hub image <sha>, V4 1-5 numbers, spoke stack deepest free N of 4096 B]
acceptance_criteria: Beacon 1 Hz +/- 10 ms while the hub ticks; a stalled hub stops it (accessory safe <= 6 s); stack in the census.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RFC-075 (rfc-2lo) ACCEPTED 2026-10-01 pins the beacon: BEACON 0x17 reused as the 1 Hz heartbeat with the tail-extended payload (hub_instance_id, wifi_channel, accessory_host flag, estop_latched flag). There is NO STOP/pause bit (RFC-085 retires STOP; pause reaches accessories as commanded safe values via the interlock, val-9u0.13). Unicast traffic does NOT refresh an accessory's deadman: the beacon is the only clock. Frame bytes from the generated registry constants, never local.

title: C6 image adoption: ESPHome esp-hosted-firmware is the co-processor image; amend architecture/transport/build-test-deploy/README + pin esp_hosted exactly
description:
Adopt ESPHome's esp-hosted-firmware as the C6 co-processor image. It is a THIRD-PARTY image, not a firmware of ours: the two-chip split (ruling 2026-09-20) stands, the C6 stays a radio co-processor, but "Espressif's stock esp_hosted slave image" stops being true and every doc that says it must change in the same commit (C-3), with a governance.md section 6 amendment (C-7).

Docs that change:
- .claude/rules/architecture.md section 2, "Two-chip split": stock slave -> ESPHome esp-hosted-firmware (release tag pinned), and what it adds (ESP-NOW over CustomRpc, BLE controller if V3 says so).
- .claude/rules/transport.md, "The radio link: the C6 is a NIC, not a peer": image identity, the version pairing with the host lock, the new C-8 evidence line; and the transport-doctrine bullet "ESP-NOW is the peer binding: NOT actively developed" -- the accessory spoke network makes it developed.
- .claude/rules/build-test-deploy.md: a new "C6 co-processor image" section (source URL, pinned tag + sha256, how to flash it -- the path V1 proved --, how to verify: esp_hosted_get_coprocessor_fwversion line in the boot log, and how to revert).
- README.md, "The boards".
- flagship_p4/src/idf_component.yml: pin esp_hosted to the exact version V1 proved (today "^2.9.2" while the lock resolved 2.12.13; a caret lets a component update silently break the pairing).
- governance.md section 6: dated amendment row.

Acceptance: all six edits in one commit, canon_lint zero findings, and the doc's C-8 line matches a fresh boot log.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6, no PCB): clean build (delete .pio) with the pinned component, flash COM15, read the boot log version line against the doc; run valence_probe twice back to back; revert the C6 to stock by the documented procedure and back again.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- COM15 boot log "C6 slave firmware ... X.Y.Z" matches build-test-deploy.md, valence_probe 2x N/N, revert-and-restore done]
acceptance_criteria: Six edits in one commit with a governance.md section 6 amendment; canon_lint zero; the documented C-8 version line matches a fresh boot log.

title: V5: memory -- size the userspace accessory store (N x declaration x 128 channels) against PSRAM, flash partitions and the Catalog32 wall
description:
Question: size the userspace accessory store and the catalog it feeds, before any format is chosen.

Known inputs: PSRAM 32 MB (33.5 MB free steady state, memory-budget.md). Flash 16 MB with 8.5 MB used; the tail 0x820000-0xFFFFFF (~7.9 MB) is unallocated ON PURPOSE for a future data partition (flagship_p4/partitions.csv header). NVS is only 0x6000 (24 KB) and already holds cfg + presets (1,735 B), so the store does NOT go in NVS. A new partition is a partition-table change: one serial flash via `pio run -d flagship_p4 -t upload` (build-test-deploy.md), and otadata/app slots must not move.
The binding constraint is not memory, it is the catalog: Catalog32 caps the hub at 48 entries and 200 layout fields (189 in use today) with a 32,768 B encode scratch, all inside Valence's frozen hub.hpp / catalog.hpp.

BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (desk first, then the P4 stamp; no PCB)
 1. Desk: the declaration record as a hardware-free struct in a native suite (test/native/test_accessory_store); print sizeof for 1, 32 and 128 channels (per channel: id, type, unit, min/max, deadman-safe value, name up to 16 B). Compute totals for N = 3 (typical) and 20 (ceiling).
 2. Desk: in the same suite, build the machine catalog plus 3 x 128-channel accessories into a larger BasicCatalog instantiation and encode it; print entries, layout fields and encoded bytes against 48 / 200 / 32,768.
 3. Bench: scratch build adding a data partition in the tail (proposed 256 KB at 0x820000, veto-able), write 20 synthetic declarations, reboot 10 times, time flash read + decode + PSRAM placement with esp_timer.
Numbers: bytes per accessory at 128 channels, totals at 3 and 20, partition size chosen, boot unpack ms p50/max (proposed pass < 50 ms), encoded catalog bytes and entry/layout counts for 3 x 128 channels.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- native test_accessory_store sizeof + catalog encode, exit 0; COM15 unpack n=10 p50/max ms; partition <offset>/<size>]
acceptance_criteria: Bytes per accessory, totals at 3 and 20, partition offset/size chosen, boot unpack ms, and encoded catalog size/entry/layout counts for 3 x 128 channels, all stamped.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Paper sizing landed in docs/accessory-store-sizing.md, using Isotope's section 16 frame budget (commit 3a02189): worst-case declaration 15,052 B, legal 126-id slice 14,818 B, 63 channels if actuators are mirrored pairs. Per accessory (both slice shapes cost the same 127 entries + 130 field slots): declaration 15,052 + catalog pools 17,040 (127x40 + 130x92, ILP32) + encode scratch ~15,052 + names 4,032 = ~51 KB PSRAM; flash 48 KiB per accessory as A/B records. Catalog32 today [verified 2026-10-01 -- scratch host build of buildValenceCatalog + encodeCatalog]: 42/48 entries, 188/200 layout, 109/160 schema, 164/192 labels, 23,595 B encoded (43 / 192 / 23,982 B with the val-091.22 power channel); 80% scratch floor 26,214 B. VERDICT: PSRAM and flash never bind (N=19 is 2.9% of free PSRAM, 912 KiB of the 7.9 MiB tail); Catalog32 binds at N=0 for a full slice (6 free entries vs 127 needed), so any full-slice N needs a larger catalog type and scratch through the Valence RFC process (alongside val-9u0.12). The proposed 256 KiB partition holds N=5 with A/B; 1 MiB at 0x820000 holds N=19. Soft wall: catalog transfer to clients (~310 KB in ~1,615 BLOB chunks at N=19, unmeasured) and >256 entries vs catalog_max_entries. CANDIDATE N, each for both the 126-channel and the 63-pair slice (same cost): N=3 (typical): 150 KiB PSRAM, 144 KiB flash (256 KiB partition), catalog 429 entries / 590 layout / 349 schema, scratch 86 KB, 361 chunks. N=8: 400 KiB PSRAM, 384 KiB flash (512 KiB partition), 1,064 / 1,240 / 664, scratch 180 KB, 753 chunks. N=19 (ESP-NOW unicast ceiling): 950 KiB PSRAM, 912 KiB flash (1 MiB partition), 2,461 / 2,670 / 1,357, scratch 387 KB, 1,615 chunks; also past the 18-slice id-space count in Isotope DESIGN section 8. Alternative lever: a smaller hub-advertised per-accessory channel budget scales everything by budget/126 (16 ch x N=19 is ~120 KiB PSRAM, ~61 KB catalog). Bench items (unpack ms, measured encode in test_accessory_store) still owed. RULING OWED: pick N from {3, 8, 19} (and whether the per-accessory budget stays 126/63 or drops).

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RULINGS 2026-10-01 (Valence rfc-7bq RFC-076, rfc-cou RFC-077, comments 01:32): slice width narrowed to 32 ids (accessory_slice_ids 0x20): r=0 session-scoped, r=1 accessory-status, r=2..31 the accessory's own, 30 channels at most; worst-case 30-channel declaration ~3.5 KB (19 chunks). Recompute docs/accessory-store-sizing.md at 30 channels per slice (it is written at 126/128 today). RFC-077 item 8: Catalog32 capacities become a build-time parameter of the hub, so the 48/200/32,768 wall is no longer fixed; this bead's output picks the Flagship's parameter, consumed by val-9u0.20. No STORE entries inside a declaration; the hub does not rewrite group strings.

title: Ruling: home of the spoke wire format (Valence ESP-NOW binding RFC vs Isotope spec); passive vs active scan; v1 vs v2 frames
description:
Every frame between hub and accessory is wire-visible: beacon (hub id, seq, e-stop bit, pairing-window bit), probe/answer (if V4 picks active scan), join request, declaration (the mini-catalog), channel-slice assignment, value frames, goodbye. The spec-gap ritual (transport.md) forbids a code-local magic number for anything wire-visible, so the format needs ONE home before the beacon or join code exists.

Options for the operator: (a) a Valence RFC, "ESP-NOW spoke binding: beacon, join and declaration frames", extending the ESP-NOW peer binding transport.md names (and RFC-053's ESP-NOW e-stop path) so the accessory side is a tiny Valence speaker; (b) an Isotope-owned spec in the Isotope repo, with Valence seeing accessories only as catalog channels on the hub. (a) keeps one registry for every number (T20: one vocabulary, one generator); (b) keeps Isotope free to move without the RFC ritual. Orchestrator read: (a), because the declaration IS catalog data and the RFC-053 ESTOP frame already rides ESP-NOW.
Also in the ruling: passive vs active channel scan (V4 measures both), and whether declarations use ESP-NOW v2 1,470 B frames or fragment at the v1 250 B limit (the C6 speaks v2; an ESP32 classic accessory may not).

BENCH VALIDATION PLAN: none for the ruling itself. Its output is checked by the beacon bead's bench plan: the stand-in accessory sketch decodes frames generated from the chosen home's constants, never hand-copied ones.
Stamp: [ruled YYYY-MM-DD -- operator, option (a|b), scan (passive|active), frame size (v1|v2)]
acceptance_criteria: Operator ruling recorded and stamped; the chosen home exists before beacon/join code is written.
notes: 2026-10-09 triage: likely decided: the spoke binding is a Valence RFC (RFC-075, ACCEPTED 2026-10-01, landed 8484552), i.e. option (a). NEEDS THE OPERATOR only for what RFC-075 left open: passive vs active scan and v1 vs v2 frames (see rfc-075's open questions).

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RULED 2026-10-01 through the Valence RFC queue: option (a), the spoke wire format lives in Valence (RFC-075 rfc-2lo ACCEPTED as drafted, RFC-076 rfc-7bq ACCEPTED with 32-id slices). Scan: ACTIVE (DISCOVER_PROBE). Channels 1 to 13 everywhere, a regional accessory may subset. Frames: every spoke frame MUST fit 250 B (v1), declarations ride blob ns0 chunking. Unicast does not refresh the deadman (one clock: the beacon). No STOP bit on the beacon: under RFC-085 pause reaches accessories through the RFC-078 interlock as commanded safe values; only estop_latched is broadcast. Ready to stamp [ruled 2026-10-01 -- operator, option a, scan active, v1 frames].

title: V2: ESP-NOW from the P4 through the CustomRpc shim -- RTT and loss at 1 Hz and 50 Hz, with and without station traffic
description:
Question: does esp_now_* on the P4, forwarded over CustomRpc to the C6 (ESPHome shim, PR 17712), carry a request/response loop at the rates relationships need, with and without station traffic on the same channel? Also: does esp_now_send block the caller for an RPC round trip (an esp_wifi RPC was measured at 151 ms on this board, so assume nothing), and do the PR's known defects reproduce (lost SEND completion stalls TX; peer mirror stale after a C6 restart; full table reports success).

BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp with the V1 image on the C6, plus any second ESP32 dev board; no PCB)
Setup: a scratch pure-IDF project for the P4 under tools/espnow_rtt/ (gitignored instrument, its own project, no ulp/ dir) vendoring the host shim from PR 17712 plus esp_now_hosted_rpc.h. Peer: a ~40-line Arduino ESP-NOW echo sketch on the second board (on receive, send the same bytes back to the sender MAC; the sender MAC is the C6 radio MAC, not the P4's). P4 station associated to the bench AP; peer pinned to the AP's channel.
Runs, each writing a CSV to artifacts/:
 A. 1 Hz x 300 s, 32 B payload, station associated but idle.
 B. 50 Hz x 60 s (3,000 packets), same.
 C. A and B again under station load: from the PC, ping -l 1400 -n 3000 -w 1 <P4 ip> throughout.
 D. B with a 250 B payload (the v1 maximum).
 E. Defect probes: power-cycle the C6 mid-run B and see whether sends resume without a P4 reboot; add 21 peers and read the 21st add's return code.
Numbers: per run RTT p50/p95/max (esp_timer, send call to echo receive), loss % (seq gaps), esp_now_send call duration p50/max on the P4, count of sends with no SEND completion. Proposed pass (operator may veto): loss < 1 % in A-D, p95 RTT < 20 ms at 50 Hz, send call < 1 ms (non-blocking); E either recovers without a reboot or the defect is written onto the shim bead as a requirement.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- tools/espnow_rtt runs A..E, n=<pkts>, RTT p50/p95/max, loss %, send-call max, C6 image <tag>]
acceptance_criteria: Runs A-E stamped with RTT p50/p95/max, loss %, send-call duration; the three PR 17712 defects each marked reproduced or not.

title: V3: BLE over esp_hosted -- P4 advertises and serves GATT through the C6; coexistence with station and ESP-NOW
description:
Question: can the P4 advertise and accept a GATT connection through the C6 (NimBLE host on the P4, controller on the C6, VHCI over SDIO), and does BLE coexist with station + ESP-NOW on the one C6 radio? Config mode and the BLE conformance floor (transport.md) both depend on it. Nucleus has NO BLE today (CONFIG_BT_ENABLED is not set). Settle first: is the ESPHome C6 image built with the BT controller at all? If not, the image choice forks (ESP-NOW image vs BT image) and that is an operator ruling, not a workaround.

BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6 on the V1 image; a phone with nRF Connect; the V2 peer board)
Setup: scratch IDF project tools/ble_hosted/ with CONFIG_BT_ENABLED=y, CONFIG_BT_CONTROLLER_DISABLED=y, CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_ENABLED=y, CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_TRANSPORT_UART=n, CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_ENABLE_BT_NIMBLE=y, CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_NIMBLE_HCI_VHCI=y (esp-hosted-mcu Bluetooth example shape). NimBLE bleprph: one service, one read/write/notify characteristic, name "Nucleus-cfg", a manufacturer-data byte standing in for the pairing-window flag.
 1. Advertise alone: nRF Connect shows the name AND the manufacturer data (T14 in the archived repo: check every adv setter's return).
 2. Connect/disconnect 10 times; per connection write 20 B and read it back 100 times; notify at 10 Hz for 60 s.
 3. Repeat 2 with the station associated, then with station + ESP-NOW run B from V2 in parallel.
 4. Internal heap: int_free and int_max before BT init and with a live connection (the network already costs ~154 KB internal; memory-budget.md).
Numbers: connects 10/10 in each condition, GATT write-read RTT p50/p95, notify loss %, ESP-NOW loss/RTT delta against V2 run B, internal heap cost of the NimBLE host in bytes.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- tools/ble_hosted + nRF Connect, connects 10/10 x3 conditions, GATT RTT p50/p95, ESP-NOW delta, NimBLE internal cost N B, C6 image <tag>, BT controller present yes/no]
acceptance_criteria: Connects 10/10 in three conditions, GATT RTT and ESP-NOW delta recorded, NimBLE internal-heap cost recorded, BT-controller presence in the C6 image answered.

title: V4: beacon + deadman timing end to end with a stand-in accessory; cold join across a forced router channel change
description:
Question: end-to-end fail-safe timing with a stand-in accessory, and cold join time across a forced router channel change.

PUSHBACK TO SETTLE ON THE BENCH: the ruling's "~2 s worst case" join does not follow from a PASSIVE scan for a 1 Hz beacon. To be sure of catching a 1 Hz beacon the accessory must dwell >= 1 s per channel, so 13 channels is ~13 s worst case. ~2 s needs an ACTIVE probe: the accessory broadcasts a short "where is the hub" on each channel and the hub answers at once (13 x ~100 ms dwell, ~1.3 s). Measure both; the operator rules which one the spoke format carries (see the spoke-wire-format ruling bead).

BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp running the V2 scratch project extended with a 1 Hz beacon task and a probe answer; stand-in accessory = any ESP32 dev board; logic analyzer or the scope on two GPIOs)
Stand-in sketch (~40 lines): on boot scan channels 1-13 (passive mode: dwell 1,100 ms; active mode: send a probe, dwell 100 ms); on a beacon, lock the channel, drive SAFE_N HIGH (armed) and note millis of each beacon; no beacon for 5,000 ms, or a goodbye frame, drives SAFE_N LOW at once and rescans (same code path). The P4 toggles a BEACON GPIO on every beacon sent.
 1. Deadman: stop the beacon 20 times (console command), then 5 times by pulling P4 power. Measure last BEACON edge -> SAFE_N falling edge.
 2. Goodbye: 20 times, goodbye send -> SAFE_N falling edge.
 3. Channel change: P4 station on the bench AP; change the AP's 2.4 GHz channel 5 times per mode (passive, active). Measure SAFE_N falling -> rising (rejoined), plus the P4's own re-association time from its log.
 4. Cold join: power the accessory with the hub already up, 20 times per mode; power-on -> SAFE_N rising.
Numbers: deadman 5.0 s +/- 0.1 s (never > 6.0 s after the last beacon SENT), goodbye < 100 ms, cold join p50/max per mode, channel-change outage p50/max per mode.

acceptance_criteria: Deadman within 5.0 +/- 0.1 s (never > 6 s), goodbye < 100 ms, cold join and channel-change outage recorded for passive AND active scan.

title: [epic] Isotope accessory host: ESP-NOW spoke network, config mode, relationships (2026-09-26)
description:
Accessories (Isotope firmware, ESPHome-shaped) join the Nucleus hub over ESP-NOW, hub-and-spoke, through the C6 co-processor. Operator rulings 2026-09-26 (orchestrator scratch RULINGS-2026-09-26.md, Accessories + Provisioning sections): 1 Hz hub beacon, 5 s deadman, goodbye = safe now, no ESP-NOW encryption, 20-peer ceiling, accessories self-describing, stored in userspace (flash, unpacked to PSRAM), channels in the user channel space (~128 per accessory), relationships are hub policy, config mode = boot with PAIR held, BLE only, no softAP ever.

Process ruling: beads, RFCs and validation plans first. Validation children V1-V5 block every implementation child; nothing here is coded until its validations carry a C-4 stamp.

Facts found while planning (read these before any child):
- Host lock: espressif/esp_hosted 2.12.13, esp_wifi_remote 1.6.4 (flagship_p4/dependencies.lock); manifest asks only ^2.9.2 (flagship_p4/src/idf_component.yml). C6 today: stock slave 2.12.1 [transport.md stamp 2026-09-20]. CONFIG_BT_ENABLED is not set.
- ESPHome esp-hosted-firmware: release v2.12.13 (2026-09-25) "Add ESP-NOW slave overlay"; its README says the slave is built from esp_hosted 2.9.3 and the overlay needs >= 2.8.1. Contradiction resolved by V1 on the bench, not by reading. https://github.com/esphome/esp-hosted-firmware , /releases
- esphome PR 17712 (merged 2026-09-06, 2026.9.0): P4-only esp_now_* shim over CustomRpc, fire-and-forget send/add/del, local peer mirror; wire contract esp_now_hosted_rpc.h shared byte-identical with esp-hosted-firmware#17. OPEN REVIEW DEFECTS: a lost SEND completion stalls TX forever; the peer mirror never reconciles after a co-processor restart; a full peer table reports success instead of ESP_ERR_ESPNOW_FULL. https://github.com/esphome/esphome/pull/17712
- ESPHome docs: never run espnow with WiFi in AP mode on the P4; the ESP-NOW source MAC is the C6 radio MAC, not the P4's. https://esphome.io/components/esp32_hosted/ , https://esphome.io/components/espnow/
- ESP-IDF ESP-NOW (C6): v1 payload 250 B (v2 1470 B), 20 peers max, peer channel must equal the station channel, send/recv callbacks run on the WiFi task. https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32c6/api-reference/network/esp_now.html
- esp-hosted-mcu BLE: NimBLE host on the P4, controller on the C6, VHCI over the hosted transport (CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_ENABLE_BT_NIMBLE=y, CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_NIMBLE_HCI_VHCI=y, CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_TRANSPORT_UART=n). https://github.com/espressif/esp-hosted-mcu , https://github.com/espressif/esp-hosted-mcu/issues/6
- CAPACITY WALL: valence::Hub binds Catalog32 = BasicCatalog<48 entries, 200 layout fields, 160, 192, 4> and a 32,768 B catalog scratch (lib/valence hub.hpp, channel/catalog.hpp, both on Valence's frozen list). This machine already uses 189/200 layout fields (ValenceCatalog.h, pattern-presets-roster note). "~128 channels per accessory" cannot land in the current hub at all; the live-catalog RFC must carry capacity, not only mid-session growth.
- An esp_hosted RPC has been measured at 151,008 us (esp_wifi_sta_get_ap_info, ValenceHub.h). Nothing that makes an RPC may run on core 1 or on the hub task.
- hardware/flagship/SPEC.md 2026-09-23 rows: SW2 PAIR on BTN_PAIR G52 (map provisional until layout), and "held at power-on = AP config mode" -- that row contradicts the no-softAP ruling (flagged to the operator; the hardware repo owns the fix).
acceptance_criteria: Every child closed with a C-4 stamp; V1-V5 stamped before any implementation child starts.

title: V1: C6 image swap feasibility -- ESPHome esp-hosted-firmware on the C6, existing P4 host still associates and passes hub traffic
description:
Question: can the C6 run ESPHome's esp-hosted-firmware image (ESP-NOW overlay) while the P4's existing esp_hosted host (lock 2.12.13) still associates and carries the hub's traffic? The risk is the version pairing: the ESPHome release is tagged v2.12.13 but its README says the slave is built from esp_hosted 2.9.3; the P4 host is 2.12.13 and the C6 runs stock 2.12.1 today. A host/slave RPC mismatch is the failure to look for.

Also unresolved and part of this bead: HOW the stamp's C6 add-on gets flashed. Candidates: (a) esp-hosted host-performs-slave-OTA through the P4 (the path tymorton/esp32-p4-c6-espnow-enabler uses; it bypasses the host's version check, which is itself a warning sign); (b) the add-on's own UART/USB pads. Record which one worked.

BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (Stamp-P4 + Stamp-AddOn C6 on COM15; no Flagship PCB needed)
1. Baseline on the current image, unchanged: boot log lines "C6 slave firmware: rc=0 version 2.12.1" and "esp_wifi_init (remoted to the C6): ESP_OK", SDIO timeouts 0; ping -n 100 <ip> (expect 2-5 ms flat, the PS_NONE stamp on val-091.13); Valence probe from the Valence repo, python tools/valence_probe.py --ip <ip> --port 82, twice back to back (T3); note the pass count.
2. Download the ESPHome C6 image named by https://esphome.github.io/esp-hosted-firmware/manifest/esp32c6.json (record the release tag and sha256 into artifacts/). Flash it by path (a) or (b).
3. Boot the SAME P4 image (no rebuild). Repeat step 1 exactly.
4. Reflash stock 2.12.1 and boot once more: the swap must be reversible.
Numbers that must come out: the version line after the swap (X.Y.Z), esp_wifi_init ESP_OK, SDIO timeouts 0 over 10 min, ping p50/max within 2 ms of baseline, probe pass count equal to baseline on both back-to-back runs, one successful revert.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- COM15 boot log "C6 slave firmware ... X.Y.Z" + ping n=100 p50/max + valence_probe 2x N/N; host esp_hosted 2.12.13, slave <tag>/<sha256[:12]>, flash path <a|b>]
acceptance_criteria: Stamped version line after the swap, esp_wifi_init ESP_OK, 0 SDIO timeouts over 10 min, ping and valence_probe (2x back to back) equal to baseline, swap reverted once; host/slave version pairing recorded.

title: Boot self-check gates motor power; every failure is named over Valence
description:
Why: operator ruling (Hardware SPEC 2026-09-23): the motor is never powered until the board proves itself, and any failure is reported rather than silently degraded.

What, in order, motor switch off throughout until step 7: (1) monitor present and on the expected version (else reflash, else block 'monitor missing'); (2) rails in window per the monitor (+5V, +12V; accessory rail = warn only); (3) INA228 answers its ID register and its bus reading matches VIN_RAW minus the ideal-diode drop; (4) input stage passing (VIN_RAW present, bus follows); (5) motor-switch off-state: MOTOR_V+ ~0 (FETs not failed short); (6) regen clamp test pulse (monitor command) seen on CLAMP_MON with ~V/8.33 on the INA228, then trim set and the clamp confirmed idle; (7) E-stop state readable and not faulted; (8) pre-charge: MOTOR_V+ rises through R412; enable: full bus, IMON sane -> motion allowed. Any failure: motor stays off, the step and the reading are published over Valence. At runtime an EN-node drop (G23) triggers a read of the monitor's latched fault code and a report.
acceptance_criteria: Each step demonstrated failing on the bench with the named report arriving over Valence and the motor staying off; a clean board passes and enables within a bounded time.
notes: 2026-10-01 (from val-091.19 design): step 6's '~V/8.33 on the INA228' predates SPEC L92 (INA now after the motor switch, it does not see clamp current) and L117 (load is 7.5 R). title: OTA: A/B app partitions + POST /ota on :80 gated by X-OTA-Token; the archive's C5 route was the last deploy path
description: Today the only way onto the P4 is COM15 (bench act; tonight's lockout fix needed a reflash while a client was live). Design, ruled shape from the S3 era (build-test-deploy.md): raw body POST, not multipart; header X-OTA-Token checked on the hub (secret from git-ignored secrets.h, template updated); esp_ota_ops with two OTA slots + otadata in flagship_p4/partitions.csv (16 MB flash; keep a 4 MB slot each since the image is 1.3 MB and Ruckig grows it); rollback = CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE with esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback only after the hub is up and WiFi joined (a hung image reverts on the next reset; the P4 has no watchdog-buy yet -- add the task watchdog on the hub task before buying). The OTA gate is ONE gate shared with motion (T31: it must keep pumping the transport the bytes arrive on; here the bytes arrive on :80 httpd, the WS on :82 keeps running; stop motion via motionEstop-shaped park, not a second latch). Flash writes disable the cache: nothing ISR/IRAM-sensitive may touch PSRAM during the write (the hub and catalog live in PSRAM: the hub task must not run while a sector is being written, or the write must happen on a task that yields between sectors with the hub paused -- measure, do not assume). Verification C-8: version-verified after reboot via the hub's identity fw_version (VALENCE FIRMWARE_VERSION), and the census line; deploy script tools/ota.py (PowerShell-safe, prints the version before/after). Acceptance: two back-to-back OTAs with version bumps, then a deliberately broken image (bad signature/short file) that is refused before erase, then a hang test only if a watchdog-buy exists.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
LANDED f104db1, fw 0.1.5-p4hub running on 192.168.1.118 [verified 2026-09-21 -- WELCOME identity fw_version + /diag header + COM15 console].

SHAPE
partitions.csv -> otadata(0xf000) + ota_0(0x20000) + ota_1(0x420000), 4 MB each, no factory slot (a factory image is booted whenever otadata is blank, so a rollback would land on a stale third image). nvs keeps 0x9000/0x6000, so the hub instance id and stored config survived the reflash (cfg_gen=160 adopted on the first boot after). POST /ota on the :80 httpd, raw body, X-OTA-Token constant-time vs SECRET_OTA_TOKEN in the git-ignored secrets.h (template updated). The :80 server moved out of ValenceUiTokenMinter into system/ValenceHttp so /uitoken, /ota and /diag share one instance; client sockets 2 -> 3, CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS 16 -> 17, arithmetic rewritten in sdkconfig.defaults.

THE PSRAM QUESTION, MEASURED (the bead said measure, do not assume)
No fault, and the mechanism is that the hub task is NOT RUNNING during a write rather than running blind: IDF's flash driver stalls the other core for the duration of each esp_ota_write. No application-level pause was needed and none was installed. Evidence: an OTA run with a live lag_probe stream left these in the next boot's crash ring, i.e. the PSRAM-resident hub kept logging across the whole 2.7 s write --
  W ota update starting: 1346864 B -> ota_0 at 0x020000, moti
  W motion REJECT: e-stop (suppressed 133)
  W ota 1346864 B written to ota_0 in 2.7 s (481 kB/s), reboo
T31 therefore holds by construction: the hub task and the :82 WS port are never suspended; the :80 task is the one that blocks.

ONE DESIGN CHANGE WORTH VETOING
The buy is gated on the hub's tick counter ADVANCING BETWEEN TWO liveness intervals, not on hubBegin() returning true. hubBegin() returning true says the hub was BUILT; an image whose hub task hangs afterward would otherwise buy itself out of the rollback that exists for it, and at 5 s intervals it was a dead heat with the watchdog. The advance check also pushes the buy one interval LATER than the task watchdog's window, which is what makes the hang test deterministic. Cost: the buy lands ~15 s after boot instead of ~10 s.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Serial flash of the new table over COM15 (the table only goes on by serial), board up, nvs intact.
2. Back-to-back OTAs, version-verified each: 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 -> 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4 -> 0.1.5, slots alternating ota_0/ota_1 each time. 2.5-2.8 s on device per 1,346,976 B image (~480 kB/s), 3.0-4.6 s wall including the HTTP hop. The 0.1.2 deploy ran with a live motion stream on purpose.
3. Refusals, running slot intact after each (still answering 0.1.2-p4hub): bad token -> 401 in 0.1 s; 300 kB truncation of a real image -> 400 ESP_ERR_OTA_VALIDATE_FAILED at esp_ota_end; 300 kB of 0xA5 -> 400 at the first esp_ota_write (IDF checks the image magic there). Nothing under 64 kB reaches esp_ota_begin at all.
4. HANG TEST (done once, the whole point of rollback): an image with for(;;){} at the top of hubTask, version 0.1.5-p4hub-HANG, deployed to ota_1. It booted, never fed the task watchdog, panicked, and the bootloader brought ota_0 (0.1.4-p4hub) back. /diag header after: "slot=ota_0 img=valid boot=7 reset=TASK-WDT". tools/ota.py reported the old version still answering, which is the rollback working and is documented as such in build-test-deploy.md. The hang was never committed.

DOCTRINE (C-3, same commit)
build-test-deploy.md's Deployment section rewritten -- it said "There is no OTA on this board yet". governance.md Map of Truth row "Firmware version constant" allocated to FIRMWARE_VERSION in flagship_p4/src/hub/valence_config.h (it had said "not yet allocated" while the constant already existed), with an Amendments row recorded as VETO-ABLE.

UNVERIFIED / OPEN
- CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_PANIC=y is new and global. Both idle tasks were already watched, they just could not panic before. Nothing has tripped it in ~40 minutes of bench use including four OTAs and 6+ minutes of streaming, but a long stall anywhere is now a reboot rather than a printed warning.
- A full 4 MB slot has never been written; the images are 1.28-1.35 MB. esp_ota_begin sizes the erase from Content-Length, so a bigger image erases more before the first write.
- Concurrency: a second OTA during one in flight answers 409, untested against a real race (one flag, one handler).

title: Diagnostics archive: Geiger ring in PSRAM with GET /diag[/<tag>]?from=<seq> on :80 (dump, not stream; footer next=)
description: Tonight's lockout hunt had no log history: the console census was the only instrument and old lines were gone. Port the S3 doctrine (logging-leds.md 'Diagnostics are a DUMP, not a stream'): a Geiger sink that appends every record into a megabytes-deep PSRAM ring (placement-new, T2), slots carry a monotonic seq, the writer never stops for a reader, a lapped reader truncates WITH A FOOTER NOTICE, the last line is next=<seq> as the resume cursor; GET /diag is the whole archive, /diag/<tag> filters one GLOG tag, ?from=<seq> composes with both. Served on the :80 httpd (esp_http_server chunked send, the hub task untouched; blocking that HTTP task for a full dump is accepted by ruling). The archive dies with its boot; post-panic forensics is a separate RTC_NOINIT crash ring (T19), which the P4 should also get since it now has no panic evidence at all. Rate: a Debug flood must never bury an error in the SMALL display view -- keep the console sink's severity floor, the archive takes everything. Read /diag once after something goes wrong, over HTTP, from tools/diag.py (prints and saves to artifacts/). Acceptance: 10 minutes of hub + stream traffic, then /diag returns the full archive with a valid footer, /diag/hub filters, ?from= resumes with exactly the new lines (T30 item 6: assert the load landed), and int_free is unchanged by a dump (everything lives in PSRAM).
