comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
LANDED bfe9769, fw 0.1.5-p4hub running on 192.168.1.118 [verified 2026-09-21 -- live /diag pulls + COM15 census].

SHAPE
flagship_p4/src/system/ValenceDiag.{h,cpp}. A Geiger sink appends every record into a 2,032,112 B PSRAM ring, 16,384 slots of geiger::Record, placement-new'd (T2). One writer (the hub task via drainToSinks), one reader (the :80 httpd task), NO LOCK: the writer fills the slot and publishes with a release store on a free-running u32 seq; the reader acquires it, copies, and re-checks AFTER the copy that its slot is still inside the window. So the writer is never delayed by a reader and there is no reader-owned state on the ring -- the latched-gate class this project has hit twice cannot appear here.

ROUTES on the shared :80 instance (system/ValenceHttp, same one /uitoken and /ota use): GET /diag, /diag/<tag> via a "/diag*" wildcard handler, ?from=<seq> composing with both. Chunked send off a 1 KB STACK buffer; the handler allocates nothing, so memory pressure cannot switch off the instrument that explains it. The :80 server's stack is 8 KB for this and for /ota.

CRASH RING: RTC_NOINIT, 8 crumbs x 60 B plus a boot sequence, magic + complement validated. Every Warn+ record mirrors into it; diagBegin() adopts the previous boot's crumbs into the archive object and re-arms the ring. They head every dump with the reset reason. The archive itself dies with its boot, as ruled.

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE BEAD: the header carries img=pending|valid (the OTA image state). tools/ota.py reads it, because "the new version answers" only proves the image booted and an unbought image is one reset from being gone. It is two lines in a header that already existed rather than a route of its own.

ACCEPTANCE
Header of a live dump:
  # nucleus-p4 0.1.5-p4hub slot=ota_1 img=valid boot=8 reset=software up=383s
  # archive 2032112 B PSRAM, 16384 slots, seq 0..42, from=0 tag=*, geiger dropped T:0 D:0 I:0 W:0 E:0 F:0
1. ~10 min of hub/session/motion traffic (two lag_probe runs at 180 s plus session churn), then a full dump with a valid next= footer. 42 records; the hub is genuinely quiet at Info and above once up, which is the design, not a gap.
2. /diag/hub -> 14 records, against exactly 14 hub-tagged lines in the whole-archive dump. /diag/hub?from=42 -> 6, composes.
3. ?from=42 -> 12 records, byte-identical to the whole-archive tail from seq 42. The new load was MANUFACTURED (three WS connect/HELLO/close cycles) and asserted to have landed before the comparison -- T30 item 6: an idle board produces nothing and a "no new lines" pass is indistinguishable from a broken cursor.
4. A cursor past the head (from=4294967295) clamps: 0 records, footer at the live write index. It echoed the cursor back on the first build, which would have handed a header-only reader a next= that skips everything since; fixed before the final flash.
5. int_free 128,887 before ten back-to-back full dumps, 128,759 after, int_max 58,368 unchanged throughout. The ~3 KB dip during the burst is lwIP's per-connection state for ten fresh sockets (every answer sends Connection: close) and it returns. The archive and the dump handler cost the internal heap nothing.
6. The crash ring proved itself twice in anger: an OTA reboot carried the previous boot's ota/motion breadcrumbs forward, and reset=TASK-WDT plus an empty crumb list is what named the val-091.16 hang test's rollback.

UNVERIFIED
- THE LAPPED-READER TRUNCATION PATH HAS NEVER RUN. Filling 16,384 slots at this board's log rate is many hours; the branch is read-checked only and carries no stamp. It is ~6 lines and the notice text has never been printed by hardware.
- Geiger's own 64-slot core ring is unchanged, so the console sink keeps its floor and the archive takes whatever clears the logger's runtime floor (Debug). Nothing has been dropped in any run so far (the drop summary is all zeros in every dump taken).

title: Hub locks out new connections after ~40 min: sessions not released on transport close (sess=4 with one live client), lwIP socket table (10) exhausted, both listeners refuse
description: Observed 2026-09-21 ~18:24-18:30 on 57eb828 (uptime 2405 s, no reboot, int_free 136 KB). Timeline: MFP plugin + phosphor.exe + a Playwright Phosphor tab connected; :80 refused /uitoken mints; by 18:27 :80 and :82 both answered TCP RST (curl 000 in 14 ms) while the board pinged and the console census read hub=up sess=4 ws frames climbing (the live clients kept working). Closing the Playwright tab freed :80 (404 on / again); disconnecting MFP left sess=4 unchanged and :82 still refusing. Config: CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS=10 (IDF default, not in sdkconfig.defaults); WS httpd max_open_sockets = kSlots+2 = 7 with lru_purge; uitoken httpd max_open_sockets 4 with lru_purge. Sum of listeners (2) + WS sockets (4-5) + idle keep-alive mint fetches browsers hold for minutes (up to 4) reaches 10. Two defects: (1) sessions/sockets of departed clients are not reaped (the T19 addendum's idle-RX reap and the T3 one-funnel teardown; check ValenceWsPort's close path and whether RFC-042 parked sessions keep their fd open); (2) the socket budget is too small for a hub that expects browsers: raise CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS to 16, make /uitoken answer Connection: close (a mint is one request) with max_open_sockets 2. Acceptance: open and close three browser sessions plus a probe run, then a fourth connect succeeds and the census sess returns to the live count; repeat twice back to back on one boot.
close_reason: fixed in 88fd666, acceptance procedure passed twice on one boot (see comments)

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE PROCEDURE (run after flashing 88fd666; do not run it against the
pre-fix image -- that one passes step 1 and fails step 4)

Preconditions: board flashed and booted ONCE; console on COM15 open for the 5 s
liveness line; <ip> from that line. Everything below happens on ONE boot -- a
reboot between rounds invalidates the run (T3: this leak is invisible whenever
deploys reboot the device between tests).

Baseline. Read one liveness line with nothing connected. Expect
  sess=0+0p socks=0/0
Anything nonzero here means the board was not freshly booted.

ROUND 1
1. Open three browser sessions to ws://<ip>:82/ with subprotocol valence.v1
   (three Phosphor tabs, or three plain WS clients). Each must mint from
   http://<ip>/uitoken first -- that is the half of the bug that lives on :80.
   Census should read sess=3+0p socks=3/0. The SECOND socks field must fall
   back to 0 within a second or two of each mint: a mint leaving a socket
   parked is the Connection: close half not working.
2. Close all three normally (tab close / graceful client shutdown, not kill).
   Within ~1 s the census must read sess=0+3p socks=0/0 -- LIVE back to zero
   and the WS socket count back to zero. sess stuck at 3+0p is the CLOSE-frame
   funnel still broken; socks stuck above 0 is the fd not being released.
3. Run one probe session (tools/valence_probe.py --ip <ip> --port 82) to
   completion. It must connect and pass as it does today.
4. THE TEST: connect a fourth client. It must succeed. On the pre-fix image
   this is the step that fails, with TCP RST on both :80 and :82.
5. Kill one client RUDELY -- no FIN, no close frame (drop the phone's Wi-Fi,
   SIGKILL the client process, or firewall its traffic). Within kIdleReapMs
   (10 x limits::ping_interval_idle_ms = 10 s) plus one tick the console must
   log "slot N silent >10000ms -- reaping" and socks must drop by one. This is
   the T19 ghost path and it has no other way to be observed.

ROUND 2
Repeat 1-5 without rebooting. Same numbers. Parked sessions accumulating across
rounds is fine and expected -- RFC-042 eviction reclaims the oldest under slot
pressure. What must NOT grow across rounds is socks, and sess (the LIVE field)
must return to 0 every time.

PASS = both rounds: step 4 succeeds and steps 2 and 5 return socks to the live
count. On any failure, paste the console line that shows it here.

Reading the census: sess=<live>+<parked>p. A parked session is RFC-042 working
as designed -- slot retained for reattach, transport gone, NO fd held -- so
only the first number is a socket-bearing client. The old single sess= number
folded the two together, which is why this class read as a session leak.

title: Hub drives motion: force_home, move, motion-input/segment streams; catalog acts like a normal motorless machine
description: Operator ruling 2026-09-21: the P4 hub acts like a normal machine with no motor, no Modbus drive, no INA. Hit force_home (0x3101 op 2) and go. DeviceFeatures::has_motion flips true; only the absent hardware stays gated (drive-tune/drive-set/machine-admin behind a has_drive flag; pattern-* behind has_pattern until the pattern engine is ported, separate bead). Delegate maps sources (move->Manual, motion-input/segment->Stream), applies move (0x3100), home ops, onStreamBundle with t_off resolved to vmotion anchors, publishes every advertised STATE channel truthfully (0x1100 motion at rate, plan-strip, motion-diag, sm-*, odometer, machine-modes). Config-set window and limits must reach the arbiter (today they do not: motionSetUserLimits/InputLimits are never called from the hub, and the arbiter has no window setter). Proof: SlopDeck force_home + hero moves, slopsync_probe --stream and --segments, scope capture on the quad via tools/lp_leg_capture.py.
notes:
LANDED + LIVE-PROVEN 2026-09-21 on the bench P4 at 192.168.1.118, fw 0.1.0-p4hub.

Catalog: has_motion=true; new DeviceFeatures::has_drive and has_pattern, both
false here. 29 entries, 14,625 B encoded, etag 0034d22cc3b11512. motion_backend
gained a third option "quadrature" (ordinal 2 APPENDED, 0/1 untouched) and
0x1030 publishes it; modes_set key 5 max 1->2.

Proof (C-4, hub on 192.168.1.118, console over COM15):
- pio run -d flagship_p4 green, canon_lint 0 findings, -t upload verified.
- slopsync_probe --bench-home --bench-home-no-revert: force_home ECHOed
  {1:2, 2:250.0}; 0x1100 pushes 41 samples in the 2 s window at ~20 Hz with
  raw_10um present.
- slopsync_probe --stream 10 (0.8 Hz sine, 50 Hz, 500 single-sample bundles):
  RENDERS. pos tracked tgt within ~0.1 mm at 950 mm/s, flags 0x41
  (homed+stream). Console: edges 23,093 -> 998,951, late=239, catchup=273,
  intents 499 accepted / 2 rejected, residual settles to -1 step.
  45 passed / 3 failed / 4 skipped.
- SlopDeck (Vite, localhost:5173/?hub=...) LIVE, telemetry flowing, hero
  planned position 230.5 / target 230.2 / lag -0.3 / speed 435 mm/s, plan-strip
  style=chase with real durations, limits cards rendering from 0x1000/0x112x.
  Screenshots in artifacts/val-091.11-slopdeck-*.png.

Measured:
- Motion task stack: idle high-water 12,316 B free of 16,384; UNDER THE STREAM
  1,296 B free (8 %). Raised to 24,576 -> 9,488 B free, 39 % headroom.
- Hub task stack: 9,832 B free of 16,384 (60 %) with a SlopDeck session live.
  Not re-measured under the probe stream.
- int_free 147,111 idle, 115,679 at the worst point of the stream.

The 3 probe failures are EXPECTED, not defects:
- subscribe_1200 / pattern_mask: pattern-state is absent by has_pattern=false.
  The probe hardcodes it (the val-b7r class).
- safety_modes: override_on/bypass_on on 0x0005 return UNSUPPORTED_OP. Nothing
  here implements manual_override or bypass_limits, and accepting them would
  latch a mode the machine does not have.

UPSTREAM PROBE BUG (SlopSync, not edited from here): the probe's ANOMALY_KINDS
table has 10 entries and stops at waveform_smoothed=9; the engine and the
catalog carry 11 (dwell_zeroed=10). DIAG_STRUCT is therefore 88 B against a
92 B payload, the length check passes, and every field after the per-kind block
reads 4 bytes early -- step 5.6 printed "bundles=1156614901 samples=500
enqueued=500 dropped=500" where the firmware sent bundles=500 samples=500
enqueued=500 dropped=0. This is the exact regression the comment above
DIAG_STRUCT documents, recurring. Firmware is correct; the probe needs
dwell_zeroed, and it mis-decodes the S3 too.

Decisions taken (veto-able):
- 0x3120 (vmotion tuning) and 0x3030 (modes) NACK UNSUPPORTED_OP; their cards
  publish the engine's real values with enabled_mask 0. Nothing here writes
  them, and an echo of a value not applied is the ground-truth defect.
- home op 1 UNSUPPORTED_OP (no drive, nothing to home against); op 3
  clear_override UNSUPPORTED_OP (no real homing to return to).
- ch::move is gated on homed at the DELEGATE even though the arbiter lets a
  Manual intent through unhomed. force_home is the wire door, per the ruling.
- force_home asserts a RAIL and the 0x1000 window is clamped into it. With the
  default stroke 250 and a stored window of 0..500 the probe's sine clips at
  250 mm and logs WINDOW CLAMP (throttled to 1 Hz with a suppressed count).
  Force-home with stroke 500, or narrow the window, to see the whole sine.
- 0x1000 measured_stroke stays 0.0: nothing here MEASURES a stroke, and
  reporting the asserted one would dress an assertion as a measurement.
- 0x1100 publishes AT RATE (30 Hz cap, granted 20), not on change. An
  on-change gate made a resting machine stop pushing and the probe caught it:
  "no samples observed in the 2s window".
- Intent queue 40 deep (a 32-sample bundle plus slack). The real ceiling on
  anchored commits is vmotion's kScheduleDepth=8; past it the ENGINE refuses
  and counts a plan failure, which is where that ceiling belongs. The probe's
  50 Hz single-sample cadence never reaches it.
- 0x1111 sync_seg_bundles publishes 0: both stream channels land in one
  counter. Understates, never invents.

NOT VERIFIED:
- motion-segment (0x2101) never exercised live (--segments skipped per the
  re-scoped bar). The decode path is written and compiles, nothing more.
- Back-to-back sessions (T3) not run as a deliberate pass, though four probe
  sessions and two SlopDeck sessions ran on one boot with no reboot.
- SlopDeck cannot reach CONTROL tier from the Vite origin: /uitoken carries no
  CORS headers, so the browser is stuck at watch and force-home is disabled in
  the UI. force_home was proven through the probe instead. Pre-existing, not
  introduced here -- the S3 served its UI from the device origin.
- /uitoken is rate-limited device-wide to one mint per 250 ms and SlopDeck
  retries the blocked fetch in a loop, which 429s a probe started alongside it.
  Close the tab before a probe run.

LATENCY FOLLOW-UP, 2026-09-21. BLOCKED ON HARDWARE: the bench P4 went offline
partway through (COM15 absent from the port list, 192.168.1.118 answering
"destination host unreachable" from this host). Commit 6ebc483 is BUILD-ONLY:
pio green, canon_lint 0 findings, NOT flashed and NOT measured. No lag number
was taken. Everything below is code reading or arithmetic.

ITEM 3, tgt_10um -- REAL BUG, FIXED (unflashed).
publishMotion packed m.plan_mm, which MotionCensus documents as the plan's
position RIGHT NOW; it tracks pos within a step or two, so the deck's target
marker rendered on top of the position and could never lead. The S3 reference
(SlopSyncHubService.cpp publishTelemetry) publishes commanded_target_mm there,
the arbiter's accepted AIM, with commanded_raw_mm in raw_10um one stage
upstream. The catalog desc agrees. Fix: new MotionCensus::target_mm = the
active plan's END (vmotion Snapshot.target in mm); plan_mm keeps the residual
job with a comment saying what it is not.

ITEM 2, display chain -- arithmetic only, no measurement needed.
0x1100 granted rate: SlopDeck wishes TELEMETRY_HZ = 25 (machine.svelte.js:87,
a measured choice); slopsync_probe wishes 20 and was granted 20. Firmware
publishes every 33 ms, so the GRANT paces it: ~40 ms between frames at the
deck.
webui/src/ui/hero/telebuf.js: push() files each sample at arrival + LEAD_MS 30
(cap MAX_LEAD_MS 150), and createRenderClock samples at now - delayMs where
delayMs = clamp(20..120, p95_arrival_gap * 1.5 + frameDt).
At a 40 ms cadence: delay = 40*1.5 + 16.7 = 76.7 ms, net of the 30 ms lead
= ~47 ms, plus one ~17 ms raster frame, plus ~20 ms of half-period sampling
= ~85 ms typical. Worst case is the 120 ms clamp: 120 - 30 + 17 + 20
= ~127 ms.
SO THE WHOLE DISPLAY CHAIN IS ~85-130 ms. It cannot produce the ~700 ms the
operator sees. The remaining ~570-615 ms is upstream of the browser.
Display-side lever if wanted: the grant rate. At 60 Hz the same arithmetic
gives ~29 ms, but machine.svelte.js documents 25 Hz as measured-better for
pacing jitter, so that is a trade, not a free win.

ITEM 1, the two lag numbers -- NOT TAKEN. Instrument is written and ready:
tools/lag_probe.py (untracked; tools/* is gitignored here and the negation
list is the operator's). It imports SlopSync's slopsync_probe as a module for
the wire primitives and edits nothing there. It sets the window and force-homes
through the same session, streams the sine, logs every 0x1100 frame, and fits
raw / tgt / pos plus the SENT series at the drive frequency, reporting
raw->pos (the engine's own chase lag, network and scheduling cancelled because
both series come out of one frame), sent->pos (adds the wire and hub
scheduling), and the arrival-gap distribution. Planned invocation, window
chosen so no ceiling shapes the sine:
  python tools/lag_probe.py --ip <ip> --force-home 50 --window 0 50 --seconds 14
0..50 mm with amp 0.35 and 0.8 Hz is 17.5 mm amplitude, peak 88 mm/s against
the 950 mm/s input ceiling and peak 442 mm/s2 against 50,000 -- two orders of
margin, so the phase measured is the engine's, not a clamp's.

WIFI POWER SAVE -- the coordinator's prime suspect, patched, unmeasured.
wifi_up() never called esp_wifi_set_ps, so the C6 ran the IDF default
WIFI_PS_MIN_MODEM and the AP held inbound frames to the next DTIM wake. Both
retired boards disabled it. esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_NONE) now runs after
esp_wifi_start(), return code checked and logged either way (it is an
esp_hosted RPC to the C6, so a silent failure is possible and would read as a
motion-path problem). A typical DTIM 1-3 at a 102.4 ms beacon interval is
100-300 ms of added inbound delay, which is the right ORDER for the gap
between the ~85-130 ms display chain and the ~700 ms observed, but that is
arithmetic, not a measurement, and it is not yet proven to be the cause.

WHAT IS OWED WHEN THE BOARD IS BACK, in order:
1. Flash the CURRENT tree, which already contains both fixes -- so the clean
   baseline for PS_MIN_MODEM is GONE unless the previous image (commit 9eeca30)
   is flashed first. Flash 9eeca30 for the baseline, measure, then flash HEAD
   and measure again, or accept a single post-fix number with no A/B.
2. lag_probe as above, both numbers, both images.
3. If PS_NONE does not move it: the hub tick is 5 ms and pumps the WS port
   once per tick (ValenceHub.cpp hubTask), the emitter steers at 1 kHz, and the
   cross-task snapshot refreshes at 50 Hz -- none of those is a 700 ms
   mechanism, so look at the socket send path (ValenceWsPort SO_SNDTIMEO,
   coalescing) and at the C6 SDIO queue depth before the engine.

Every kinetic knob and overshoot_clamp is applied live and echoed post-clamp; motion_backend is read-only; home_style exists only with has_drive. Not persisted yet (val-091.11.2). Host-verified only, not flashed.

title: Motion path: HP core evaluates the vmotion plan, LP core renders edges from a velocity it is handed
description: Same shape the machine repo already ratified (a sampler evaluates the trajectory; the emitter renders): the HP core runs vmotion (Ruckig) and at its tick hands the LP core (step_q8, dir) from the plan's velocity; the LP core's phase accumulator renders exact edges and its signed edge count IS position truth. Extend flagship_p4/ulp/lp_quad.c from constant-rate bench to steered emitter; keep the deadline-from-previous-deadline rule. MotionArbiter sole-caller rule carries over unchanged.
notes:
MOTION PATH v0 LANDED AND RUNNING ON HARDWARE, 2026-09-20. BEAD STAYS OPEN:
the scope half of the acceptance (item 2) could not run -- the DHO4204 is
powered off and absent from the LAN (no ARP entry and no TCP/5555 on
192.168.1.12, on the guide's 192.168.1.117, or anywhere in the /24; the
instrument's PHY is unpowered when off, so there is no remote wake).

FILES
  flagship_p4/ulp/lp_quad.c        constant-rate bench -> STEERED emitter.
  flagship_p4/src/motion/ValenceMotion.h/.cpp   NEW: arbiter, engine host task,
                                   LP steering, bench sequence.
  flagship_p4/src/main.cpp         motionBegin() + motionBenchStart() after the
                                   hub; census line carries the motion numbers.
  flagship_p4/src/CMakeLists.txt   motion TU, Ruckig step solvers, vmotion and
                                   ruckig include dirs, VALENCE_BENCH_MOTION.
  flagship_p4/partitions.csv       NEW, and see THE ONE TRAP below.
  flagship_p4/platformio.ini       board_build.partitions = partitions.csv.
  flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceHub.cpp   onEstop now parks the emitter; the
                                   ch::move seam is documented there. Nothing
                                   else in src/hub/ touched.

======================================================================
1. DISPLACEMENT vs PLAN -- PASS
[verified 2026-09-20 -- 11 bench cycles over 165 s on COM15, pyserial, one
handle, rx backlog high-water 394 B of a 4096 B driver buffer so nothing was
dropped; board at 192.168.1.118 running the image flashed this session]

  out       steps=+4173  want=+4172  err=+1   pos=20.0040 mm  plan=20.0000 mm
  back      steps=-1     want=+0     err=-1   pos=-0.0048 mm  plan=0.0000 mm
  reversal  steps=-1/+0  want=+0     err=-1/0 pos=-0.0048 mm  plan=0.0000 mm

IDENTICAL on every one of 11 cycles. late = 0 throughout (see the counter
split below). emitter_faults = 0: the demand never reached the emitter floor.
The error never exceeds ONE STEP (4.794 um) and NEVER ACCUMULATES -- the
machine returns to 0 +/- 1 step at the end of every cycle, because at rest the
arbiter re-seeds the engine from the LP count before planning.

WHERE THE +/-1 COMES FROM, and it is not a defect: one edge is always in
flight when the plan reaches rest and the emitter parks. It lands, it is
counted, and the park then discards the accumulator. So a leg overshoots by at
most one step IN ITS DIRECTION OF TRAVEL, which is exactly the +1/-1 pattern
above. ponytail: a closing trim (creep the last fractional step) is the
upgrade path if sub-step landing ever matters; it does not today, because the
encoder is the auditor and every plan starts from the LP count.

2. SCOPE PROFILE -- NOT RUN. Instrument offline (above). Owed: one 2 s single
shot at 1 Mpt (500 kSa/s, 2 us) over a full +20 mm leg on LPG15 (A, CH2) /
LPG12 (B, CH1): 0 illegal transitions, the interval profile binned against the
planned velocity (239.7 us at the 20 mm/s flat top, the 100 ms ramp at either
end), and no gap at the reversal. The capture script is written and the
firmware repeats the sequence every ~15 s, so it is one armed SINGLE away.

3. STACK, HEAP, HUB -- PASS
  Motion task stack high-water: 11,992 B USED of 16,384 (free 4,392 B), after
  a real workload of 44 point-move commits including mid-flight replans.
  [verified 2026-09-20 -- uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark, IDF reports bytes]
  T21 SAYS DO NOT SIZE IT DOWN. 16 KB stays: 73% used is not headroom to
  trade, the waveform path (not exercised here) nests more than chase does,
  and commit() is where the KB-scale Ruckig temporaries live.

  Internal heap, hub idle:  before motion  int_free=186,411  int_max=122,880
                            with motion    int_free=154,211  int_max= 88,064
  Cost -32,200 B free / -34,816 B maxblock, and it is all accounted: 16 KB
  motion stack + 4 KB bench-task stack + ~9.2 KB of engine .bss (static RAM
  31,960 -> 41,120 B) + the intent queue. PSRAM untouched at this resolution.
  THE ENGINE AND BOTH STACKS ARE INTERNAL ON PURPOSE: the HP side is
  unreachable while the flash cache is off, and only the LP core is immune.

  Hub still serves: GET /uitoken -> 200 with a control-tier token, and a raw
  ws://192.168.1.118:82/ connect -> 101 with subprotocol slopsync.v1.
  Catalog etag unchanged. 165 s with no watchdog, no reboot, no panic; parlio
  still running beside it.
  [verified 2026-09-20 -- curl -i, websocket-client, console capture]

======================================================================
DESIGN DECISIONS

HP TICK: 1 kHz (kTickUs), and the task blocks on ulTaskNotifyTake with a 1 ms
timeout rather than vTaskDelayUntil. dt is MEASURED from esp_timer, so an
early wake costs nothing -- which is what lets an intent be PLANNED ON ARRIVAL
instead of waiting out the tick. 1 kHz is kept from the S3 product because it
is the cadence the engine was benched at; the LP core renders every edge
between ticks regardless, so a faster tick buys nothing.

CORE / PRIORITY: core 1 with the hub, priority 6 against the hub's 5. Core 0
keeps app_main and the esp_hosted SDIO service the whole network path needs.

VELOCITY -> LP: cycles_per_edge = 40e6 / (|v| * 208.608), carried in Q8.
PARK THRESHOLD 0.0115 mm/s = 1.024e10 / (2^32 * 208.608), the speed below
which the Q8 product no longer fits 32 bits. Direction is sign(v).
WRITE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: dir first, then step. The LP reads the two words
independently, so writing dir first makes the only reachable interleaving "one
edge at the OLD period in the NEW direction" -- a timing slip of one period.
Writing step first instead allows one edge in the WRONG direction, a permanent
two-step position error nothing detects.
EMITTER FLOOR 40 cycles/edge (~4,790 mm/s, 5x the machine ceiling): a FAULT
DETECTOR count, never a shaper. It read 0 all session.

POSITION TRUTH: lp_quad.c gained volatile int32_t g_pos, a signed edge count,
written by the LP core and by nothing else. The HP keeps its own origin
(_lp_origin) and subtracts, so the word never needs a write from the HP side
and there is no race to reason about.

STEERING LAW: feedforward the plan's own mean velocity across the interval
that just elapsed -- (p_plan(t_k) - p_plan(t_k-1)) / dt -- which telescopes
over a move to exactly the plan's displacement. Plus a residual term against
POSITION TRUTH at 50 Hz, DEADBANDED AT ONE STEP so the quantization of the
count itself never becomes commanded jitter. The residual term exists for the
ramp out of rest, and it is not optional: the emitter renders a VELOCITY, so a
step it could not emit on time is a step nothing else would ever repay.

THE STEERING-LATENCY FINDING, AND IT CHANGED THE LP CODE. The brief's premise
was that a velocity update landing one edge late is a phase error, not a
position error. That is true at a STEADY rate and false out of rest. The plan
opens at ~0.1 mm/s (accel 200 mm/s^2, first tick), whose period is 48 ms; the
old loop read g_step_q8 once at the top and then committed to the wait, so
ticks 2..48 were ignored and every move would have opened with a ~41 ms dead
zone and ~47 steps of permanent shortfall. FIX: a COARSE WAIT ahead of the
fine one. It re-reads g_step_q8 and g_dir while the deadline is still more
than RESTEER_SLACK_CYCLES (2,000 cycles = 50 us) away, and recomputes the
deadline STILL FROM prev, so the accumulator rule is untouched. Inside the
slack the FINE loop runs alone and keeps its shape byte for byte, which is why
the measured 125 ns floor survives by construction. Worst-case steering
latency is now 50 us plus one recompute, at any rate. Measured: 24,413
re-steers over 11 cycles, late = 0.

late=0 NEEDED A SECOND COUNTER, AND THE SPLIT IS THE REAL FINDING. First run
showed late climbing ~5 per cycle. It was not a miss: when the commanded rate
RISES while an edge is pending, prev + T_new lands in the past BY ARITHMETIC,
however fast the core is, and the emitter correctly fires at once. Conflating
that with a real deadline miss makes every ramp out of rest look like an
emitter that cannot keep up. lp_quad.c now counts g_catchup for the re-steered
case and keeps g_late for a deadline computed at the top of the loop and
already past. After the split: LATE = 0 over 165 s and 170,000 edges;
catchup = 39, about one per acceleration.

REVERSAL LANDS ON AN EDGE BOUNDARY, BY CONSTRUCTION AND NOW BY INDEX ARITHMETIC.
The direction is read once per edge, before the wait, so the line just driven
is complete and the next edge is the inverse of it. THE OLD +3 STEP WAS WRONG
ACROSS A FLIP: i holds the next index under the OLD direction, so on a
reversal it must step the OTHER way ((d ? 3 : 1), not (d ? 1 : 3)). Stepping

one phantom count in g_pos, and a two-step position error per reversal. Found
by walking the Gray table, not by the scope; the reversal leg returning to 0
+/- 1 step on 11 cycles is the evidence it is right.

40 MHz XTAL. They are never compared. The plan's displacement is realized by
EDGE COUNT, not by elapsed time, so the measured +26 to +30 ppm crystal offset
(sd-1bi.3) is a VELOCITY SCALE error of 30 parts per million and not a
position error at all: a 20 mm leg still lands on exactly its step count, one
microsecond-ish late.

title: Network up on the P4 through the C6: esp_hosted (or the alternative) over the actual wiring
description: First hard fact needed: how the C6 module is wired to the P4 on this stamp (SDIO or SPI, which pins). No reference doc is on disk; find the vendor doc, save it under docs/reference/, then decide esp_hosted slave on the C6 vs custom firmware. The whole point: the P4 runs the WebSocket server itself with the C6 as a transparent NIC, which deletes the S3/C5 UART bridge and its T31-T33 trap class. Continues SlopDrive-32 sd-1bi.4.
notes:
NETWORK UP 2026-09-20. [verified 2026-09-20 -- console capture after flash:
'Card init success' at 40 MHz 4-bit, 'Identified slave [esp32c6]',
'C6 slave firmware: rc=0 version 2.12.1', esp_wifi_init ESP_OK at 2177 ms,
wifi=up ip=192.168.1.118 on three consecutive 5 s liveness lines, 0 SDIO
timeouts, LP emitter late=0 throughout]
- THE C6 SHIPS WITH THE HOSTED SLAVE IMAGE (2.12.1). No C6 firmware of ours.
  Capabilities advertised: WLAN, HCI over SDIO (BLE only).
- Host side: esp_hosted ^2.9.2 resolved to 2.12.13, esp_wifi_remote ^1.2.2.
  esp_hosted 2.x does NOT self-start under esp_wifi_init: call
  esp_hosted_init(), esp_hosted_connect_to_slave(), then
  esp_hosted_get_coprocessor_fwversion() as the proof line, then esp_wifi_init.
- PIN TRAP, measured: the public CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_SDIO_PIN_* ints are
  promptless and DERIVED from CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_PRIV_SDIO_PIN_*_SLOT_1
  (Kconfig:1127-1135). Setting the public ones is silently ignored; the bus
  came up on the dev-board pins 18/19/14-17 and timed out forty times. The
  PRIV *_SLOT_1 keys carry the value. sdkconfig.defaults says so.
- SRAM COST OF THE NETWORK ON THE P4: 386,632 free before, 232,108 after
  hosted + wifi_remote + netif + lwIP connected = ~154 KB at default queue
  depths, nothing in PSRAM. The driver (MAC/PHY/buffers) lives on the C6.
  Linkable SRAM per the map: sram_low 0x2CBD0 + sram_high 0x60000 = 576 KB;
  boot heap 589 KB. The build summary's 'RAM: 327680' is the board manifest
  (copied from an S3), not the chip. PSRAM (32 MB) not yet enabled.
RULING 2026-09-20 (operator asked whether the C6 should own sockets like the
C5 did): NO. The S3's SRAM pressure came from the on-chip WiFi driver plus BT
controller; on the P4 the driver is off-chip, the part has 2.3x the SRAM and
32 MB PSRAM, and the measured stack is 154 KB and tunable. A sockets-on-C6
design recreates the C5 bridge and its T31-T33 seam to save memory the P4 does
not need. BLE later = NimBLE host on P4, controller on C6, the split the S3
never had. Remaining on this issue: nothing for bring-up; PSRAM enable and a
heap census under load belong to the hub port (val-091.3).

WIRING FOUND 2026-09-20 (M5Stack docs, docs.m5stack.com/en/core/Stamp-P4 and
/en/arduino/m5stampp4/wifi; CNX 2026-03-29): the Stamp-AddOn C6 snaps onto the
Stamp-P4's 20-pin SDIO 3.0 header. Pins, from M5's own Arduino example:
  SDIO_CLK GPIO43  SDIO_CMD GPIO44  D0 GPIO45  D1 GPIO46  D2 GPIO47  D3 GPIO48
  SDIO_RST GPIO42
All four data lines are wired, so 4-bit SDIO is available. The Arduino board
macros are BOARD_SDIO_ESP_HOSTED_*, i.e. the transport is esp_hosted with the
C6 as the hosted slave and esp_wifi_remote on the P4. NOT stated anywhere:
whether the C6 ships with the hosted slave image preinstalled, SDIO speed or
1-bit/4-bit defaults, esp_hosted version. Those get discovered by bringing it
up, not by reading (memory: needs are found by hitting them). Known-good
reference for the P4-side config: Arduino's prebuilt esp32p4_es sdkconfig
(~/.platformio/packages/framework-arduinoespressif32-libs/esp32p4_es/sdkconfig),
which is what M5's example runs on.
close_reason: Network up on the P4 through the C6: esp_hosted 2.12.13 host, C6 ships slave 2.12.1, SDIO 4-bit 40 MHz on the Stamp pins (PRIV *_SLOT_1 keys), ip=192.168.1.118, LP emitter late=0 throughout. C6 stays a NIC; sockets stay on the P4 (ruling recorded).

(INTENT). Kept deliberately: configuration STORAGE is truthfully what the hub
holds and hands on, unlike a gauge reading zero. measured_stroke publishes 0,
which the catalog already defines as "not measured".

  hub-seeded by the library: 0x0003 safety, 0x000A pending-pairing,
  0x000D paired-devices-roster.
  published by hubBegin(): 0x0004 control-owner (20 B, all four sources
  unowned, which is the truth on a hub the delegate maps no source on),
  0x0006 hub-status (14 B, republished 1 Hz), 0x1000 machine-config (37 B,
  republished on change).

CORE CHOICE: the hub task is pinned to HP CORE 1, priority 5, 8 KB INTERNAL
stack, 5 ms vTaskDelayUntil. The LP core owns motion and PARLIO is pure DMA, so
core 1 carries nothing else, while core 0 runs app_main and the esp_hosted SDIO
service the whole network path depends on. Keeping the hub's tick and its
bounded socket writes off the core that services the radio bridge is the S3's
comms/realtime separation drawn where this silicon actually puts the work.
Stack is SIZED, NOT MEASURED -- re-check against a high-water mark once a real
client workload has run.

CONGESTION DESIGN (SPEC 10.3). esp_http_server has NO egress queue and NO
queue-depth API: httpd_ws_send_frame_async is a blocking write straight into
the kernel send buffer. So the watermark IS the syscall. Every send is timed
with esp_timer and bounded by SO_SNDTIMEO = 50 ms (open_fn, alongside
TCP_NODELAY):
  over kSlowSendUs (2,000 us) -> the buffer was full and the kernel parked us,
                              which is what CongestionSignal::QueueWatermark
                              names. Latched into kSlowWindowMs = 200 ms, so
                              the 10.3 one-second threshold is reachable (a
                              per-tick sample would need 200 consecutive slow
                              5 ms ticks).
  send failure              -> the peer is not draining at all.
  control frame unsendable  -> level 2 severe while the stall timer is armed.
Hysteresis is 10.3's own: sustained above for 1,000 ms -> 1; below for
5,000 ms -> 0. Recovery re-probes by construction, because at level 1 the data
classes shed WITHOUT touching the socket while control frames keep probing.
Cost: ONE stalled send charges the hub tick up to 50 ms, paid at stall onset,
not per frame.
TX classes: STATE/STREAM shed as soon as the level is nonzero; BLOB_CHUNK is
its own class paced at limits::blob_chunks_in_flight (4) per hub tick, HELD
never dropped and never arming the stall timer (T16); everything else
including EVENT is control, never shed, and kCtrlStallMs = 2,000 ms of
CONTINUOUS control failure tears the session down. The timer is cleared ONLY
by a control frame actually going out, never by inbound traffic.

SLOT EXHAUSTION: REFUSE AND CLOSE at the handshake
(httpd_sess_trigger_close + ESP_FAIL), not NACK BUSY. SPEC 6.3's BUSY is the
right answer on an ATTACHED transport, and the WS handshake predates HELLO by
definition -- there is no session to NACK into. Returning ESP_FAIL alone would
leave the peer connected-but-silent, the failure users report as a bug (the C5
paid for that one). kSlots = kHubMaxSessions + 1 = 5, so a connection arriving
during a teardown has somewhere to land.

THE ONE BUG THE BENCH CAUGHT, AND WHY MEASURING IT MATTERED
esp_wifi_sta_get_ap_info() for hub-status' rssi field measured 151,008 us
[verified 2026-09-20 -- first call timed with esp_timer, boot log]. The radio
is on the C6, so it is an esp_hosted RPC, not a register read: at 1 Hz on a
5 ms tick that is a thirty-tick stall every second, the instrument
manufacturing the fault it observes (memory-budget.md T27). Fixed by inverting
it -- main.cpp's 5 s liveness loop calls it and pushes the value in through
valence::hubSetLinkRssi(), an atomic<int8_t>. The hub task never makes a
cross-chip call.

SPEC SECTIONS LEANED ON
  6.1  session ids / boot_id from the injected rng
  6.3  a feature exists iff its channels exist (the has_motion gate); NACK BUSY
       belongs on an attached transport (the slot-exhaustion choice)
  7.2  hub time is a WRAPPING u32 of microseconds (EspClock truncates on
       purpose)
  8.3  catalog etag is order-sensitive, so gating never reorders
  9.1  retained STATE pushed on grant (every advertised STATE channel seeded)
  9.3  ECHO carries APPLIED post-clamp values, key-complete
  9.4  EVENT is never replayed and never shed (EVENT is a control class here)
  10.3 congestion levels and their hysteresis windows
  10.4 "the never-shed queue itself cannot drain" = severe
  11.2 motion stops before protocol bookkeeping (onEstop); estop/stop
       role-exempt
  12.2 token -> role mapping; a tokenless HELLO is watch, which is a WORKING
       state
  13.1 transport binding contract and its properties
  13.2 one frame = one BINARY message; the subprotocol MUST be echoed
  17.2 all time and entropy through injected interfaces
  RFC-002 cfg_gen advances iff a value CHANGED
  RFC-016a / RFC-046 / RFC-048  WELCOME identity, endpoint, durable instance id
  RFC-029 section 4  /uitoken: single-use, 60 s, control tier, no CORS
  RFC-042   stale sessions are retained; SLOT_RECLAIMED makes room
  RFC-050   blob_chunks_in_flight is the advertised sender pacing budget
Registry: ws_subprotocol "slopsync.v1" (registry.yaml:1173), UNSUPPORTED_OP
0x0303 (registry.yaml:609), blob_chunks_in_flight 4 (registry.yaml:1088).

NOT DONE / OWED

- Config is RAM-only. NVS persistence for the 0x1000 values is a later task;
  the code says so rather than claiming durability it does not have.
- Hub task stack 8 KB is sized, not measured.

- Congestion and the TX classes are DESIGNED AND COMPILED, never exercised

description: Valence Drive is the pure ESP-IDF firmware for the OSSM Flagship PCB: ESP32-P4 owns motion (LP core quadrature emitter, validated 2026-09-20 at 40 MHz XTAL, 125 ns non-accumulating floor, immune to HP flash writes) and the Valence hub; ESP32-C6 is the radio. title: Oscillator amplitude in millimeters (Valence RFC-112): branch feat/osc-amp-mm, awaiting the ruling
description: Operator 2026-10-10: the oscillator offset is static, not window driven. Branch feat/osc-amp-mm (worktree ../Nucleus-oscmm) carries osc.amplitude, its drive's out bounds and osc.amplitude_effective in mm, ceiling OSC_MAX_AMPLITUDE_MM 1000 (half of ceiling::rail_mm, not bench-chosen), factory 5 mm by hand and 20 mm for a full V8, FIRMWARE_VERSION 0.1.40. The stage runs in rail millimeters (fillStrip converts the plan), so a window move never rescales it and Kinetic needs no change. Lands only if the operator rules RFC-112 in; else drop the branch. Phosphor lane lp/oscmm carries the Neutrino re-pin and the fixture.
notes:
2026-10-10: main took 0.1.40 (overnight batch, 5806a2e); feat/osc-amp-mm merged main (ad42bb0 after the merge) and is FIRMWARE_VERSION 0.1.41, image artifacts/fw-0.1.41-p4hub-bench.bin (sha256 8e2af5fa252211435897256cc558128e12c86a6b8593fda52cf8194147e72524), catalog etag a51bc15705a2890a. Phosphor lp/oscmm re-pinned to it (11d03b6, ce35915).
RFC-112 Cost correction, for the RFC author. Replace the Nucleus and Kinetic sentences with: Kinetic: none. Nucleus: the 0x3140 intent and 0x1140 twin declare the four fields mm, unit_id 0, min 0, max = the ceiling (OSC_MAX_AMPLITUDE_MM, 1000, half of max_rail's catalog max), default and step in mm; the delegate clamps to the ceiling, not 1; the arbiter runs the oscillator stage in rail millimeters: fillStrip() converts the plan it reads to mm, hands render() the input set's ceilings in mm and the backstop's window in mm, and the amplitude, the drive points and osc.amplitude_effective are mm throughout, so there is no span() conversion in either direction and reseedEngine() no longer restates the plan buffer or calls Oscillator::rescale(). Why: converting by span() at the hub leaves the drive points Kinetic already holds in the old window's units. Oscillator::drive() cannot replace a point nearer than driveLeadUs (156 ms) past the head, and rescale() leaves held points alone, so every window move under a V8 stream would play the old window's scale for up to a lead plus a fade (a window grown 5x asks 5x the swing, bounded only by the ceilings). Fixing that needed a Kinetic change (rescale also scaling held drive amplitudes); running the stage in mm needs none, because a window move then changes nothing the stage holds. Kinetic's stage is unit-agnostic (plan, limits, window and amplitude only need one unit); its header's 'window units' wording is the reference's old caller, not a constraint. [verified 2026-10-10 -- test_motion_arbiter: a 10 mm V8 swing held every tick through a window a fifth the size; kinetic_trace.json byte-identical]

New image artifacts/fw-0.1.42-p4hub-bench.bin in Nucleus and Nucleus-oscmm, sha256 ed5838fab3331b17554bde313d532bc8f78e3d46498a80feaf94fa203fab6a9d, catalog etag a51bc15705a2890a (unchanged). title: Classic pattern in a narrow window re-plans every hub tick (200 plans/s) with an anomaly on every second plan while the carriage stays put
description:
Found by the Neutrino fleet soak (Phosphor ph-ode2). A running classic pattern in a narrow travel window re-plans at the hub-tick rate with every second plan an anomaly, while the carriage barely moves: the planner spins.

Direct probe on Neutrino (Phosphor's pinned integral.wasm, Nucleus 4226af7), boot {homed:true}, one control session, pattern-cmd {1:true, 2:1, 3:73, 4:15, 5:71}, kinetic-diag over 3 s:
  window 0..500    4 plans/s, 0 anomalies/s
  window 100..120  83 plans/s, 42 knot_trimmed/s
  window 100..105  200 plans/s, 100 knot_trimmed/s (one plan per 5 ms hub tick)
  window 5..8      200 plans/s, 100 knot_trimmed/s, carriage parked at 5.43 mm
  window 5..6      0 plans/s

title: motion-anomaly 0x4100 is declared in the catalog but never emitted: anomalies only reach the kinetic-diag counters
description:
Found by the Neutrino fleet soak (Phosphor ph-ode2). The catalog declares 0x4100 motion-anomaly (EVENT, role events.anomaly, event_kinds labels, body schema kind/seq/target/detail/t_us; ValenceCatalog.h addMotionAnomaly), but nothing in flagship_p4/src calls Hub::publishEvent: MotionArbiter::drainAnomalies() only increments the 0x1111 kinetic-diag counters. A client subscribed to 0x4100 never receives an event (Phosphor's Log and Health views bind the anomaly feed by role).

Evidence: `node test/fleet/fleet.mjs --replay 3 --hw-safe` (Phosphor lane lp/fleet): kinetic-diag ends at anomalies 9 (knot_trimmed 6, piece_over_ceiling 3) and the trace holds zero 0x4100 events; across the fleet the per-client anomaly-event counts are all empty while 0x1111 counts thousands per minute. Grep: no publishEvent( anywhere under flagship_p4/src at HEAD 24cc412.
Either emit one EVENT per drained anomaly (kind as event_kind, body per the schema, rate-capped) or drop the entry from the catalog until it is emitted (a declared channel that never speaks is the dead-gauge lie the catalog comments warn about).
notes: Final 0.1.39 image is 105e6fb (fix commits 167a12d + 186a382), sha256 92316e9eaa0fb251122301f3748bb929d44076a3dd29f7e5639054ed7d453f21; catalog etag 83f67d8b16f12749.
close_reason: 167a12d (fw 0.1.39): emitted, not removed (SPEC 9.4 events.anomaly, RFC-065; Phosphor's Log and Health bind it by role). MotionArbiter::popAnomaly() counts each anomaly for 0x1111 and hands it on (target in the client frame); the P4 planner posts to a 16-deep queue, the sim to a ring; motionTakeAnomaly() is the hub task's door; ValenceDevice::publishAnomalies() publishes each on 0x4100 (event_kind, body kind/seq/target/detail/t_us) under a bucket of 8 refilled one per 100 ms, so a planner in trouble cannot push safety and log events out of the shared per-session event queue; the rest stay on 0x1111 and show as seq gaps. title: config-set: a max_rail write does not hold the travel window inside it (SPEC 9.6); 0x1000 publishes a window past max_rail
description:
Found by the Neutrino fleet soak (Phosphor ph-ode2). SPEC 9.6 (RFC-101): a write of geometry.max_travel holds the travel window inside it "as any write of that setting holds it". ValenceDevice::applyConfig does not: setConfigKey clamps window keys 1/2 only to ceiling::rail_mm (and, since val-3kd, to the measured stroke while a real home stands), never to next.max_rail, and key 8 never moves the window. So machine-config publishes a window wholly past max_rail.

Minimal repro on Neutrino (Phosphor's pinned integral.wasm, Nucleus 4226af7; HEAD 24cc412 has the same applyConfig), boot {homed:true}, one control session:
  config-set {2: 400}            -> ECHO, window 0..400, max_rail 500
  config-set {8: 100}            -> ECHO; 0x1000 reads window_max 400 > max_rail 100
  config-set {1: 200, 2: 300}    -> ECHO; 0x1000 reads window 200..300, max_rail 100
Same with home_sense_at_mm/rail_end_at_mm (a measured stroke of ~490 does not help when max_rail is written below it).
Fleet seed: `node test/fleet/fleet.mjs --replay 3` from Phosphor (lane lp/fleet) flags window-past-rail ~9.5 s in (a config-set carrying {1: 206, 2: 217, 8: 80.9} applied whole while the carriage sat at 391 mm); 347 of 1024 fleet hubs hit it in one minute. The arbiter's WINDOW CLAMP/BACKSTOP still hold motion, so this is the published configuration lying, not a fence breach, as far as the twin shows.
Fix direction: after the keys apply, hold next.window inside next.max_rail (clamp the edges; a window write wholly past it refused INVALID_VALUE like the measured-stroke case), ECHO post-clamp.
notes: Final 0.1.39 image is 105e6fb (fix commits 167a12d + 186a382), sha256 92316e9eaa0fb251122301f3748bb929d44076a3dd29f7e5639054ed7d453f21; catalog etag 83f67d8b16f12749.
close_reason: 167a12d (fw 0.1.39, 9f43588): every config-set write and a stored blob at adoption hold the window inside max_rail (SPEC 9.6, RFC-101); a window write wholly past it is refused INVALID_VALUE 'window past max_rail' (or the measured-stroke detail past the stop); any other write collapses such a window onto the rail's far end, 1 mm wide, logged. [verified 2026-10-10 -- test_valence_device VD-HOME-9 fails on 25713b4 (window_max 400 > max_rail 100, no NACK), passes now; VD-HOME-8 updated; 59 cases exit 0. Phosphor lp/neutrino fleet --replay 3: see the lane commit] Firmware NOT flashed.

title: P4 v1.3 erratum: an AHB/APM permission failure can stall the flash/PSRAM bus until system reset; make sure a hang like that resets the chip and the carriage stops safely (matters more under XIP)
description: Operator 2026-10-09: documented ESP32-P4NRW rev 1.3 erratum: if several AHB masters access PSRAM or flash and one makes an unauthorized access, DMA APM intercepts it but may leave later authorized transfers stalled; avoid unauthorized PSRAM/flash transactions; once stuck, the only documented recovery is a system reset. Consequences: a stalled bus hangs every HP task whose code or data is on it (total under val-5gh XIP, near-total today since the hub box and diag archive live in PSRAM). Check: (1) the LP core's lease (LP SRAM, off that bus) stops the carriage within 4 ms: confirm the LP program and its data never touch flash/PSRAM; (2) a hardware watchdog stage reset (MWDT/RWDT, not a software handler that would itself need the stalled bus) fires and reboots; read the IDF config for interrupt/task watchdog panic-vs-reset and the RTC watchdog; (3) after that reset, boot is safe (self-check, motor power gate); (4) audit DMA users (esp_hosted SDIO, UART/RS485 DMA if any, any GDMA) for buffers that could point outside their permitted regions; (5) record the chip revision on our Stamp. Ties to val-5gh.

title: Execute from PSRAM (ESP-IDF XIP from PSRAM): copy code + rodata to PSRAM at boot so a flash write no longer freezes the planner/steer; would remove the LP lease lapse on settings saves and OTA buy
description: Operator 2026-10-09: 'can we not move the steer to psram? can the whole system not load the code to psram?'. ESP-IDF offers execute-in-place from PSRAM (CONFIG_SPIRAM_XIP_FROM_PSRAM on chips that support it; the S3 equivalent is SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS + SPIRAM_RODATA): instructions and read-only data are copied to PSRAM at boot and fetched from there, so disabling the flash cache for an erase/write no longer stalls code. Verify for the ESP32-P4 in the IDF version Nucleus uses: support, the exact Kconfig names, whether the other core keeps running during spi_flash writes (or is still parked by esp_ipc), PSRAM fetch latency vs flash (hex PSRAM at 200 MHz vs quad flash), boot-time cost, PSRAM used (~1.3 MB of 32 MB), interaction with the LP core and the motor/RS485 paths. Bench acceptance: with the option on, a settings save and an OTA image-buy mid-motion show lapses=0 on the status line (today: one LEASE LAPSE + STALL at every image buy). If it holds, val-4rr's deferral stays as wear/coalescing hygiene only.
notes:
2026-10-09 SUPPORT VERDICT (IDF 5.5.4, framework-espidf 3.50504): SUPPORTED on the P4, opt-in, one symbol.
- CONFIG_SPIRAM_XIP_FROM_PSRAM (esp_psram/esp32p4/Kconfig.spiram:67-87) selects SPIRAM_FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS, SPIRAM_RODATA and SPIRAM_FLASH_LOAD_TO_PSRAM; depends only on SPIRAM_BOOT_INIT (on). No PSRAM mode/speed constraint (hex 200 MHz stays; ECO2 only bars 250 MHz, :33-34). soc_caps.h:606 SOC_SPIRAM_XIP_SUPPORTED. IDF CI runs it on P4 (esp_psram/test_apps/psram sdkconfig.ci.esp32p4_xip, pytest_psram.py:82; app_update sdkconfig.ci.xip_psram).
- FLASH WRITES: spi_flash_os_func_app.c:29 defines SPI_FLASH_CACHE_NO_DISABLE when FETCH_INSTRUCTIONS && RODATA; spi1_start/spi1_end (:129-130, :177-178) then take a plain mutex instead of cache_disable(). So spi_flash_disable_interrupts_caches_and_other_cpu (cache_utils.c:125-192: esp_ipc park of the other core :162, esp_intr_noniram_disable :183, cache off :188-191) is NOT called for esp_flash erase/write. Both cores keep running, caches and all interrupts stay on, the scheduler is not suspended (SPI_FLASH_DISABLE_SCHEDULER_IN_SUSPEND unset).
- EXCEPTION, still parks: esp_mmu_map/unmap on P4 always disables caches and parks the other core (esp_mmu_map.c:377-395, "On P4 ... we temporarily use cache disable/enable"; callers :443/:640). Only the MMU table write, microseconds. Nucleus hits it via esp_partition_mmap in read_otadata (esp_ota_ops.c:84-86): the image buy and every /diag (otaPendingVerify -> esp_ota_get_state_partition).
- Boot: the bootloader leaves PSRAM-addressed segments to the app (bootloader_utility.c:904-910); the app copies them page by page (mmu_psram_flash_v2.c:54-108) and logs "mmu_psram: .rodata xip on psram" (:229) and ".text xip on psram" (:167). MMU page 64 KB (CONFIG_MMU_PAGE_SIZE_64KB). OTA between XIP and non-XIP images works with the IDF 5.5.4 bootloader on the board.

ENV: flagship_p4_bench_xip (flagship_p4/platformio.ini) = flagship_p4_bench + xip.sdkconfig.defaults (one line). Generated sdkconfig differs from the bench one in the XIP symbols only. Built 2026-10-09 from the working tree (incl. the other agent's uncommitted MotionArbiter edits), beside a fresh flagship_p4_bench from the same tree:
                     bench        bench_xip
  firmware.bin       1,346,960    1,351,488   (+4.5 KB, slot 4 MB)
  .flash.text        958,944      954,720     (now at 0x48000020, PSRAM)
  .flash.rodata      285,328      283,732
  internal static    170,360      180,788     (+10.4 KB: IRAM text +7.2 KB, dram data +3.2 KB; boot/PSRAM init code made noflash)
  PSRAM taken        0            1,310,720   (15 text + 5 rodata pages of 64 KB, of 32 MB)
  .tbss / .tdata     none / 0     none / 0
Boot copy: 1.25 MiB read through DIO 80 MHz flash, estimate ~0.1 s added; measure from the boot log.

BENCH PROCEDURE (operator; COM15, hub 192.168.1.118; A = flagship_p4_bench, B = flagship_p4_bench_xip, BOTH built from the same commit):
0. Precondition: val-4rr's deferral must NOT be in the image, or a mid-stroke save waits for a still window and lapses=0 proves nothing. If it has landed, run this on the commit before it.
1. Load A by OTA (curl --data-binary @.pio/build/flagship_p4_bench/firmware.bin -H "X-OTA-Token: <secret>" -H "Expect:" http://192.168.1.118/ota). OTA, not USB: only a PENDING_VERIFY image's buy erases and writes otadata; a USB-flashed image's buy is a read.
2. IMAGE BUY: the buy runs on its own ~5-10 s after boot (app_main liveness loop, once the hub ticks and WiFi has an IP), next to the pgest NVS write at 10 s uptime. The OTA estops and reboots, so the buy can never land mid-stroke today; it lapses the lease idle too (the steer renews every tick). Watch the COM15 status line (every 5 s) until "image bought: ..." appears, then record lapses= and stalls=, and look for "LEASE LAPSE" / "STALL" in GET /diag.
3. Home from Phosphor. Start a funscript with continuous full strokes; run 60 s; lapses= and stalls= must not move (control).
4. SETTINGS SAVE MID-STROKE: with the script running, change Motion > Machine modes > Home speed (modes_set key 9; accepted at all times, unused by a running stroke, persists the "cfg" blob 2 s after the last change, ValenceDevice.cpp kCfgPersistDebounceMs). Alternate 40 <-> 41 mm/s, one change every ~3 s, 30 changes (~25 cfg writes fill an NVS page, so this covers at least one sector erase, the long write). Each write logs "persisted cfg, N B, T us". Record lapses=, stalls=, late=, and the T us values.
5. Repeat 1-4 with B (OTA the xip firmware.bin). Confirm the boot log (COM15) shows both "xip on psram" lines; note the boot time stamp against A.
6. PASS: B shows lapses=0 and no new STALL through steps 2 and 4, where A shows one lapse per write that reached flash. Also compare int_free/psram_free (B: about 10 KB less internal, 1.25 MB less PSRAM) and a plain-motion late=/stalls= run of a few minutes (code now shares the PSRAM bus with the hub box in PSRAM; Kconfig.spiram:82-87 asks for profiling).

RISKS:
- mmap reads are not serialized against XIP-mode flash writes (the writer holds s_spi1_flash_mutex, esp_mmu_map takes spi_flash_op_lock). The buy (app_main) and /diag (:80 task) read otadata through an mmap while the hub task may be mid NVS erase (pgest at 10 s uptime sits right next to the buy). I am not sure what the P4 cache reads from flash during an SPI1 erase; assume garbage. Worst case seen in code: the buy fails, g_bought is already set, the image reverts at the next reboot (no brick). Before XIP ships: read otadata once at boot and have the buy run on the hub task (src, not this bead's files).
- ValenceOta.h (T31) and ValenceHub.cpp saveBlob comments explain safety by "the flash driver stalls the other core / cache-off window". On an XIP image that mechanism is gone (the hub keeps running, with the cache on, which is also safe). Reword them if XIP becomes the release config.
- +10.4 KB internal static RAM; check int_min against the memory budget before adopting.
- Alternative not taken: CONFIG_SPI_FLASH_AUTO_SUSPEND (spi_flash/Kconfig:85-101, SOC_SPI_MEM_SUPPORT_AUTO_SUSPEND on P4) keeps code in flash and suspends erases in hardware, but needs a flash chip Espressif qualifies for it; the stamp's flash part is unverified.

title: Oscillator drives and the osc-drive stream (RFC-103 items the hub does not render yet)
description: val-dzf landed the fixed oscillator (0x1140 STATE twin, 0x3140 osc-set, Kinetic 920836b's stage in the strip). Not yet: osc.frequency.drive / osc.amplitude.drive with in_min/in_max/out_min/out_max on 0x3140 (fixed, speed, position, axis over osc_drives; linear_clamp of SPEC 8.11; drives read the PLANNED motion), and the c2h samples-kind STREAM 0x2140 osc-drive (role osc.drive: amplitude then frequency, f32 norms, no input.target, never a rail slot, an axis-driven parameter reads 0 after stream_quiet_release_ms). A driven frequency changes continuously, and the stage latches frequency only at rest (a fade): drives need a slewed-frequency mode in Kinetic's oscillator first. Library-blocked parts (WELCOME key 7, setter-session clear, idle owner slot) are Valence rfc-ns5c.
notes:
2026-10-09 Kinetic 725d448 (kin-kzq4, unpinned; pin is 920836b): the oscillator's driven mode, the kernel half of this bead. API, kinetic2/oscillator.hpp header:
- set(OscParams{enabled=true, driven=true}): a plain sine whose frequency and amplitude follow drive(); shape, dwells, frequency, amplitude fields unused. Fixed to driven and back fades through rest.
- Per osc.drive sample: drive(t_base + t_off, hz, amplitude). Map each through its bounds (SPEC 8.11) first; a fixed parameter passes its own field's value; clamp hz to OSC_MAX_HZ (the kernel caps at a quarter of the grid rate, 250 Hz at 1 ms). Returns false when 64 points are held (kDriveMax, about 120 Hz of samples under the 250 ms lead cap): count it.
- A point lands no nearer than driveLeadUs(kMotionTickUs) = 156 ms past the last render's head, and replaces every point at or after its time. Declare driveLeadUs as the osc-drive grant's schedule_latency_us (SPEC 5.4) so a player that leads by it lands on its stamps.
- Speed and position drives: drive(t0 + driveLeadUs(step), ...) from the plan at that instant (inside _plan_ext), every few ticks, not every tick (kDriveMax).
- Nothing is asked from 500 ms past the last point (kDriveQuietUs, SPEC stream_quiet_release_ms): input loss fades to rest by itself. hz 0 asks nothing.
- render() per tick unchanged. One render per step: the lead covers up to 4 steps per call.
- Size: MotionOscillator grows from about 4 to about 7 KB.
- The driven strip is exact for the executed head; its tail past (lead - fade) is a prediction that later points may lower.
Open for this bead: SPEC 9.7 does not limit drives to the sine; the kernel's continuous path is sine-only. A non-sine shape with a non-fixed drive needs a hub rule or an RFC.
Operator rulings 2026-10-09, as relayed: (1) "8/9 should be wired by default either way": factory osc.frequency.drive and osc.amplitude.drive = axis; while an osc.drive stream is live it drives (and may enable the oscillator for its duration); with no live stream axis falls back to the parameter field so the card works by hand. (2) Coordinator pick, veto-able: while any drive is bound the hub renders sine and 0x1140 reports shape = sine (honesty; Kinetic driven mode is sine only). IMPLEMENTED (hub side): default axis; quiet or no stream -> an axis parameter reads 0 (SPEC 9.7 as written); osc.enabled still gates rendering (no auto-enable); sine honesty on 0x1140 and the ECHO. DEVIATIONS NOT TAKEN, need SPEC amendments (pre-tag rule, operator ruling): (a) SPEC 9.7 The external axis, "Once the stream has been quiet for `stream_quiet_release_ms`, an `axis`-driven parameter reads `0`: silence ends the oscillation as silence stills every stream." -> proposed "With no live `osc.drive` stream (none published, or quiet for `stream_quiet_release_ms`), an `axis`-driven parameter reads its own field's value, as `fixed` does: silence ends a stream's drive, never the hand-set oscillation."; the same clause in registry osc_drives 3 axis ("0 once the stream has been quiet for stream_quiet_release_ms") and channel_roles osc.drive ("Quiet for stream_quiet_release_ms, an axis-driven parameter reads 0."). (b) Auto-enable: SPEC 9.7 Telemetry defines osc.active as "enabled and rendering"; to let a live stream enable it add to the Scripts paragraph: "A live `osc.drive` stream renders the oscillator for its duration whether or not `osc.enabled` is set; `osc.active` reads true while it does." Until then a player writes osc.enabled itself. (c) Sine only: add to Driven parameters: "While either drive is bound (not `fixed`) the oscillator renders a sine and its STATE twin reports `osc.shape` = `sine`; shape and dwells take effect again when both drives are `fixed`." (relayed as an RFC-105 amendment; the oscillator is RFC-103).
Hub side landed 3c5987c on Kinetic 725d448 (pin af50061): drives + bounds on 0x3140/0x1140, 0x2140 osc-drive stream, driven mode wired, schedule_latency_us = kOscDriveLeadUs 156 ms, sine honesty, dropped points counted (oscDriveDropped(), logged; no wire field). pio test -e native 26/26, bench image 0.1.36 builds [verified 2026-10-09]. Still open here: the three SPEC amendments above (operator), and the library-blocked items on rfc-ns5c.
2026-10-09 13f29c3: deviations (a) and (b) IMPLEMENTED ahead of the pinned SPEC 9.7 (operator ruling '8/9 should be wired by default either way'; the Valence agent drafts the amendment on rfc-ns5c). (a) with no live osc.drive stream (none, or stream_quiet_release_ms past the newest stamp) an axis parameter reads its own field while osc.enabled holds (0 when disabled: no hand to return to): factory axis drives + osc.enabled now oscillate by hand, points every kOscPlanDriveTicks at the lead (MotionArbiter::feedOscillator). (b) while an axis drive is bound a live stream renders the stage whatever osc.enabled holds (MotionArbiter::streamOscillator, before the plan read); osc.active is the census's, true while it renders. Quiet, back to the hand state through the kernel's fade: the first hand point lands on the tick the quiet window ends (kOscQuietUs == kDriveQuietUs static_asserted), so no gap (2 mm hand under a 5 mm stream: least amplitude through the handover 2 mm); disabled, rest. PAUSE, ESTOP, unhomed, uncommissioned hold a stream as they hold the hand. PICKS, veto-able: (1) a stream enables the stage only while an axis drive is bound (both drives fixed or plan-driven: the stream drives nothing, enables nothing); (2) the hand state under axis drives is the driven mode's sine, so shape/dwells by hand need both drives fixed ((c) unchanged); a stale stream session's last points play out (<= lead cap + quiet), no per-session cut. [verified 2026-10-09 -- pio test -e native exit 0, test_motion_arbiter 4 oscillator-drive cases]. Still open: SPEC amendments (a)(b)(c) (operator, Valence agent), rfc-ns5c item 3 (library).
2026-10-09 (Valence RFC-110 draft review, rfc-mol-8if): takeOscDrive() clamps each sample's stamp to the lead cap one at a time (0x2100 does the same); §5.4 RFC-090 moves a bundle past the cap earlier as a whole, spacing kept. Since a drive point replaces every point at or after its time, samples clamped onto the same instant replace each other; RFC-110 item 4 invites players to send near the cap, so this case gets more common. RFC-110 also asks of this bead: liveness from the newest stamp (as oscStreamLive), per publishing session, ended by that session's end or STALE; render only while a drive is axis; oscShapeRendered() on a LIVE drive (axis without a live stream counts as fixed) and dwells reported 0 while driven; cfg_gen on the reported flip (§4.2).
2026-10-09 96946be FIRMWARE_VERSION 0.1.37 on Valence pin f79567d (16541da): bench image artifacts/fw-0.1.37-p4hub-bench.bin, 1,366,928 B, sha256 c58c91463b4856dc5675292496b31773200cc86a0e6005f47523fffe2aaf98bf, no .tbss, internal RAM unchanged vs 0.1.36 (.dram0.bss 72,176 B, g_motion 48,264 B); valencesim etag 99c7be4f31c520c4 unchanged, wasm check ALL PASS. NOT flashed; OTA: python tools/ota.py --image artifacts/fw-0.1.37-p4hub-bench.bin --expect 0.1.37-p4hub-bench [verified 2026-10-09 -- pio test -e native 26/26 exit 0, ota.py --dry-run image matches]
2026-10-09 correction to the RFC-110 note above: NO per-session cut. RFC-110 now states the reference's rule: a stale or departed publisher's points play out under the quiet release (13f29c3 as is). Still owed for RFC-110 item 3: oscShapeRendered() on an EFFECTIVE drive (speed/position, or axis with a live stream; axis without one is exactly fixed, so the hand card keeps every shape), dwells reported 0 while driven (RFC-110 pick, against the current pass-through), cfg_gen on the reported change. Item 6 (home INTERLOCK while enabled or rendering, force_home exempt) matches 79590ab.
2026-10-09 6a42410 + 25713b4 (FIRMWARE_VERSION 0.1.38, Valence pin f79567d), per the coordinator's pick (veto-able) and Valence RFC-110 (f54fbac): SUPERSEDES 13f29c3's hand-state points. An axis drive with no live stream is EXACTLY FIXED (mode, shape, dwells): the factory card renders square/saw/dwells by hand. Driven mode (sine) only while a parameter is driven by a live input: speed/position, or axis with a live stream (stream_quiet_release_ms past the newest stamp, whichever session published it; a stale publisher's points play out, no per-session cut, the withdrawn ask). Stream start/end switch mode through rest (kernel fade out/in, up to 150 ms each). A live stream renders the stage while an axis drive is bound, osc.enabled or not. 0x1140 and the ECHO report shape sine and both dwells 0 while driven, written values kept; the report moving with liveness is a hub-side cfg_gen (none for a kept sine with no dwells); census osc_stream_live feeds it. title: Window change mid-stream re-targets in place: keep the pending knots, re-plan from the carriage in the new frame, no reset
description:
Observed by the operator 2026-10-08 on the machine (0.1.29): while a funscript stream plays, dragging the travel window (window.min / window.max writes, SPEC 11 "the travel window stays writable at any time") stops the motion outright; it resumes only when the stream's next knots land and plan from rest.

Why: MotionArbiter::setWindow() sets _frame_moved; planTick() then resetEngine() at the carriage (the "A FRAME MOVE IS NOT MOTION" block), which drops every pending knot and bumps the strip generation. That block was written for the pre-split feedforward (val-091.13: a jump in plan_mm became a 1e5 mm/s demand). With the planner/steer split the steer follows the strip the planner publishes from the engine, so a replan from the carriage's true state is already the normal path (a jog, a supersede).

Wanted (operator, "re-target in realtime"): a window change mid-stream keeps the pending knots (they are window shares and stay valid) and re-plans from the carriage's actual state in the new frame: p_norm' = toNorm(positionMm()) in the new window, v_norm' = v_mm / new_span. The next knot is then reached inside its own interval if the limits allow, else by the solver's ordinary lateness handling (dilate), exactly as a late start. The LP fence and the window clamp still bound everything. The strip re-anchors as any replan does.

Design to verify, not a ruling:
- Keep the reset for force_home (the count re-origins: the knots' shares mean the same but the committed profile is in a frame that no longer exists) unless the same reseed covers it; the operator's ask is the window.
- Engine API: Engine::resetAt() clears pending. Either a new Engine entry (Kinetic repo, header-only, kinetic-change formula: reseed state at now keeping pending knots, then re-solve) or the arbiter truncates at now (truncateAfter) and resubmits the surviving knots from its own copy. Prefer the smallest Kinetic change that the native suite can pin with a fixture.
- Still parked when nothing is pending and the carriage is at rest (today's behavior is fine there).
- Keep home cycles ending on a frame move (homeEnd).

Acceptance: a native test in test/native/test_motion_arbiter: a stream of knots in flight, window moved mid-stroke by 20 % of the rail; the plan never stops (velocity never reaches 0 unless a knot asks it), no PLANNER STALL, no emitter saturation (the val-091.13 class: no tick demands more than the ceilings), position stays inside the new window after the retarget settles. Fixture kinetic_trace.json unchanged unless the trace itself is the thing under test. Suite 71/71 stays green plus the new cases. Lint clean under Python310.
notes:
2026-10-08 implemented (Kinetic 5f50726 kin-5bj + this commit). MECHANISM: a new engine entry, Engine::reseedAt(State, now), not the arbiter-only route: the arbiter holds no copy of the knots and the engine exposes only newest()/solved(), which lose has_v/family/sample, so a truncate-and-resubmit would turn free knots into authored-velocity knots. reseedAt retires what is due, drops the curve in flight (committed or not), keeps every pending knot and re-solves from the given state; nothing pending and moving brakes from it (an explicit pause brake stays explicit); at rest it holds. ARBITER: planStep's frame branch resets for force_home (new _origin_moved flag), a home cycle, or nothing pending at rest (unchanged); otherwise reseedEngine(): the plan's own state (sampleEngine) restated out of the frame the engine was last set in (_eng_lo/_eng_span, written by every reset/reseed) into the new one, p' = (lo_old + p*span_old - lo_new)/span_new, v' = v*span_old/span_new, a likewise; the engine limits scale by the same factor so the curve in flight keeps its mm ceilings until the next intent sets the new frame's. DEVIATION from the design text: the seed position is the PLAN's position, not positionMm(): the strip then runs on in mm with no step (d = 0 at the hand-off, no LATE PLAN), and the carriage's tracking lag stays the bounded kick's job as through every re-plan. WHY val-091.13 CANNOT RECUR: the steer never converts frames; it follows the strip, whose entries are mm computed by the planner from the engine. The gen still bumps before the flag drops, so no strip of the old frame (or one torn by setWindow racing fillStrip) steers; the refill after the reseed starts at the old plan's mm position, and the new PlanStrip.continuous flag keeps the steer's command instead of re-anchoring, so the first feedforward is the plan's own velocity, never a jump. Every steer stays under vmax + one tick of amax. On the board the steer still parks while the flag is up (until the planner publishes): one or two ticks with no steer, then the plan resumes from the carriage via the gap rule. TESTS: 2 new cases in test_motion_arbiter (73/73, was 71): a 20-segment sweep with the window moved by 80 mm (a fifth of a 400 mm rail) at 145 mm with 2 knots pending: slowest plan 128 mm/s, slowest steer 107 mm/s, steer peak 1155 mm/s (<= 1300), plan jump beyond velocity 2.7e-5 mm, 0 planner stalls, 0 emitter faults, 0 rejected, ends at the new window's share 0.9 (368 mm); and the steer-ahead-of-planner split. Both fail on the old reset path. LEFT: kinetic.pin bump to 5f50726 (operator, kinetic-change gate kin-mol-ch5); the pre-existing torn-frame race between setWindow (hub task) and fillStrip (planner) is unchanged and still covered only by the steer's flag park. A Manual jog in flight also re-targets by share (its knot is a window share like any other).

title: Plan strip names the next segment while a committed piece still renders toward its knot (style 4 with start = end mid-flight)
description:
Seen in the hub replays of 2026-10-08 (ADSR): the plan strip (0x1110) read style 4 (kPlanStyleHold, ValenceCatalog.h; set in publishPlanStrip when |target - start| < segment_dwell_span) with start = end = 0.05 while cur was mid-fall at 0.5.

Cause: readPlan() takes start from Engine::segStart() and end from the first pending knot. When a submit lands in the later half of a piece, Engine::commitHorizon commits through that knot and calls boundary(), which moves segStart to the knot while the committed curve is still rendering toward it. From then until the knot's time the strip names the NEXT segment: start = the knot ahead, end = the knot after it, duration that segment's, elapsed 0. Style 4 mid-flight was this plus a hold the arbiter inserted a few microseconds after the knot (gone with b097a81); without the hold the strip still reads the next segment for the last part of every stroke.

What it should read: while the committed curve is in flight (has_committed, now < committed.end_us), start = where that piece began, end = the committed knot, duration and elapsed on that piece.

Why it matters beyond the display: Phosphor's funscript scheduler measures its latency compensation from plan.elapsed and plan.duration (observePlan: start = arrival - elapsed, the least over a plan's samples). Samples taken while the strip names the next segment early give elapsed 0 and an arrival before that segment starts, so the measured start is early and the lag reads short. Check before trusting auto latency compensation on a dense script.
notes: 2026-10-09 triage: still valid at HEAD: MotionArbiter.cpp readPlan (~1458-1466) still takes start from Engine::segStart and end from the first pending knot, with no has_committed branch.
close_reason: Fixed in 64843ee: readPlan keeps the committed piece (start, knot, duration, elapsed) until the knot's time; test_motion_arbiter val-0ep case fails on the old readPlan, passes now; pio test -e native green [verified 2026-10-09]

title: A flash write longer than the 4 ms LP lease stops the carriage mid-motion (val-fi5 consequence): defer or accept
description: Consequence of bd val-fi5 (operator ruling 2026-10-06, the LP lease). The motion task runs from flash; with the cache off (NVS or OTA writes, measured ~20 ms per 4 KB erase+write under the 2026-09-20 hammer) it cannot renew the lease, so the LP core stops the carriage after kLeaseUs (4 ms) from whatever speed it holds, then the next tick resumes it. Before val-fi5 the LP core coasted the last steer through the write. Options for an operator ruling: (a) accept, the stop is the safe direction; (b) defer settings writes while busy; (c) put the motion tick in IRAM so it renews through a write. Evidence owed: count lapses= on the status line during a settings save mid-motion.
notes:
2026-10-09 triage: NEEDS THE OPERATOR: defer flash writes while moving, or accept the 4 ms lease stop mid-motion? (val-fi5 consequence, unchanged.)
RULING 2026-10-09 (operator): (b) defer the flash write ('a machine unplugged mid move is likely not a good save'). Settings apply in RAM at once; the persist waits for a STILL WINDOW: the published plan strip shows zero velocity for at least the worst-case write time plus margin (start 60 ms; measure the real erase+write on the P4 and set it), which a funscript hold that long qualifies for; otherwise at quiet release, PAUSE, ESTOP or when the stream ends. Pending saves coalesce (one write of the latest state). Never write while the strip shows motion inside the window. Test: a save requested mid-stroke lands in the next still window, never during motion; lapses= unchanged.
close_reason: Done in 8e8f94a: persist waits for a still window (strip still 60 ms, or ESTOP, never homing), coalesced; VD-PERSIST-1/2 + val-4rr arbiter case; pio test -e native 26/26 [verified 2026-10-09]. Bench measurement of the write time owed: val-ggj.

title: Home-sense park survives a flash write: IRAM-resident interrupt path (needs ruling)
description: val-cp5 parks the seek from the home-sense GPIO interrupt, but the GPIO ISR service is installed without ESP_INTR_FLAG_IRAM and the path (onRise -> parkSeekFromIsr -> MotionArbiter::homeSenseRose -> LpEmitter::park via vtable) is flash-resident, so a flash write (NVS save, OTA) holds the interrupt off for the length of the cache-off window while the LP core keeps rendering the seek velocity into the stop. The motion task is equally frozen then. Fix shape: an IRAM non-virtual park door (store 0 to ulp_g_step_q8 directly from an IRAM_ATTR handler with DRAM-resident state), its own ISR registration with ESP_INTR_FLAG_IRAM (the shared GPIO ISR service would force every handler IRAM), or forbid flash writes while homing. Operator ruling needed on which; the sole-door rule (LpEmitter the only writer, arbiter the only caller) is what the first option bends.
