title: Kinetic 2: one knot-timeline kernel with lookahead, one sample behind, no Ruckig in firmware, multi-DoF from day one
description: Operator 2026-10-05: Kinetic needs a full rewrite and multi-axis; blend/stretch/chase are not good; native tests with hard motor limits are the verifier. PROPOSED ROUTE (veto-able). Diagnosis: Kinetic plans one trajectory per command at arrival with one-segment lookahead, Hermite-then-bend for timed segments, and a zero-latency chase of the newest point whose feedforward, lookahead, accel-ff, second-order aim, jerk scaling, recovery vmax, settle grace, starve-settle and overshoot guard are all compensations for not buffering (17 tuning members, each bench-tuned). Kernel: ONE knot timeline (t, p, optional v) per axis fed by every source: segments are the sender's knots; samples become knots delayed by the declared schedule_latency_us (SPEC 5.4: that key IS the chase budget, so chase and segments collapse into one solver and val-1bf disappears by construction); strokes and jogs are knot emitters; the oscillator (RFC-103) is an additive post-stage. Solver over the lookahead window (32 parked, 125-1000 ms): junction-velocity forward/backward pass under amax/jmax with deadlines, then per-interval profiles from Ruckig with minimum_duration = the interval (exact-time, jerk-bounded by construction instead of fit-then-bend); infeasible intervals keep the Blend/Stretch semantics and the amplitude floor but decided over the window, not per segment, so no stretch cascade. Keep: the 1 ms sampled-ceiling test discipline, determinism rules (double math, -ffp-contract=off), the anomaly drain, plan-as-data, the wasm ABI (Phosphor preview = truth), the brake via Ruckig's velocity interface, the dwell rule. Drop: every chase heuristic above. Multi-DoF: DoF as a template parameter, shared timeline and deadlines so axis sync is free; Ruckig is multi-DoF natively for point-to-point. Costs to bench first: the P4 has a single-precision FPU, double is soft-float, and Ruckig plans in double; measure profiles per second on the P4 before committing to Ruckig per interval (val-4ix shares this bench); if too slow, an analytic 7-phase S-curve in float with a determinism test against the wasm build. Verification: property tests over random knot sequences (ceilings never exceeded in sampled reality, knots hit within tolerance or an anomaly names the spend), the kinetic-trace bit-exactness test, and a replay harness over the funscript corpus scoring RMS tracking error at the declared latency, overshoot count, amplitude retention and ceiling violations (must be 0); the rewrite is accepted on those numbers, not on feel. Home: the Kinetic repo once val-0n4 gives it a board (kin-).
notes:
Operator 2026-10-05 leans to dropping Ruckig. Analysis: with a knot timeline and fixed interval durations the objective is not time-optimality (Ruckig's whole job) but smoothness through timed knots under ceilings: a C2 quintic spline through the window's knots with junction velocity and acceleration as free variables (one tridiagonal solve, O(n)), ceilings checked by the polynomial extremum referee Kinetic already has, infeasibility spent by a global iterative scale at the violating knot and re-solve (Blend as a window search, a handful of O(n) passes). Continuous jerk (quintic) beats bang-bang jerk (Ruckig) on a belt drive: smoother spectrum, less resonance. What remains of time-optimal planning is two small cases: brake from any (p, v, a) to rest, and park/point-to-point from a known state, each a bounded 3- or 7-phase profile of a few hundred lines. Samples: zero-latency chase of the newest point is prediction and therefore overshoot; delaying by the declared schedule_latency_us turns it into interpolation between a known pair of knots, which is 'get there before the next one' stated exactly. Ruckig stays only as a TEST ORACLE in the native suite (how far our brake/park sit from time-optimal), a dev dependency never vendored into firmware; the firmware math goes float-first with the determinism test against wasm, which the P4's single-precision FPU wants anyway. Decision owed: operator confirms drop.
RULED 2026-10-05: one sample behind (the declared schedule_latency_us) is the approach; the machine is a Dyneema rope drive, hard stops are mechanically fine. REQUIREMENT: a script segment may end hard: smooth accel in, then a stop as fast as the decel and jerk ceilings allow, landing at the knot. Kernel contract for junctions, no new wire: three junction kinds. SMOOTH (no end_vel, C2 family): velocity and acceleration are free variables, the spline picks the smoothest. AUTHORED (end_vel given): the junction velocity is pinned to the sender's value, acceleration free under C2, free to step under C1. HARD (end_vel 0 under C1 family, or any C1 knot where the authored curve corners): the acceleration may change as fast as the jerk ceiling allows, and a stop is rendered as the fastest legal brake profile (jerk ramp to -amax, hold, ramp out so v and a reach 0 exactly at the knot time), i.e. the segment's tail is the time-optimal stop and only its head is spline. If that brake needs more time than the segment leaves, the policy spends (Blend trims amplitude, Stretch moves the knot) and the anomaly names it. This is the SPEC curve_family rationale made concrete: a C1 corner is something the author put there on purpose and C2 smoothing must not erase it. Rope note: the one number where rope slack shows is the stop decel; amax already is that number.
RULED 2026-10-05: no Ruckig in firmware. Kinetic as it stands today (with its vendored Ruckig) is kept whole as the TEST ORACLE in the native suite: Kinetic 2's brake, park and segment rendering are graded against Kinetic 1's answers under the same ceilings (time to stop, ceiling compliance, knot hits), never shipped. Kinetic 2 is the firmware planner. Operator's reasoning: Ruckig had to be vendored, and vendoring a whole library to call two functions of it is the wrong trade. Follow-ups: val-etc (two copies of the suite) resolves as 'Kinetic 1 + its suite become the oracle package'; val-63b (-ffp-contract) applies to Kinetic 2's float math; val-0n4 gives Kinetic its board before the rewrite starts.
NAME: Kinetic² (superscript two) in prose, docs and marketing; Kinetic2 in identifiers, paths and package names.
RULED 2026-10-05: the oscillator yields first under the ceilings; a full-speed movement sheds its oscillation before anything else; planned motion keeps its amplitude (RFC-103 updated).
Oracle numbers 2026-10-05 (Kinetic tests/test_kinetic2_oracle.cpp): the Kinetic² brake stops in exactly Ruckig's time from the same state (ratio 1.000); a rest-to-rest quintic park takes 1.20 to 1.23x the time-optimal profile across strokes of 0.05 to 0.9 of the window. The park-profile option (quintic or S-curve) in RFC-105 is therefore a real 20% on jogs and homing; decide after the bench says whether anyone feels it.
2026-10-09 triage: route executed: Kinetic² is the planner (0b29990), Ruckig gone, the handle model (RFC-106) and tuning set (RFC-108) shipped, Kinetic 1 off Kinetic main (7f7330d). No open children. NEEDS THE OPERATOR: close this epic, or keep it open until the park-profile option (quintic vs S-curve, RFC-105) is decided after the bench?

title: motion-segment max_rate_hz 50 caps scripts at 25 reversals/s: raise to what Kinetic measures

The cap chain: ValenceCatalog.h motion-segment maxRateHz = 50 -> the grant (SPEC 6.2 min(wish, catalog max)) -> the client's token bucket (SPEC 10.5, burst <= 4x) -> the player thins the script to 50 segments/s = 25 reversals/s. Physics note for the amplitude the user will get: a = A(2 pi f)^2, so 1 mm p-p at 50 Hz is ~49 m/s2 and the jerk/accel ceilings will shape it; a native vibrate/oscillate intent (one command, hub-side oscillator) is the companion proposal, RFC pending the operator's yes.

title: motion 0x1100 STATE arrives below its grant: valencesim ~21 Hz flat, P4 ~28 Hz, at a 50/60 Hz grant
description:
Found from Phosphor ph-6vh (display latency), measured 2026-10-03 with a read-only valence-js session (SUBSCRIBE [[0x1100, hz, elevated]], 6 s, arrival stamps at the client).

valencesim 0.1.6-p4hub (127.0.0.1, --homed, idle and under a 0.8 Hz sine stream alike):
  wish 25 -> grant rate 25, gap p50 46.8 ms p95 48.4
  wish 50 -> grant rate 50, gap p50 46.8 ms p95 48.1
  wish 60 -> grant rate 60, gap p50 46.8 ms p95 47.8
P4 192.168.1.118 0.1.6-p4hub-bench (MultiFunPlayer streaming):
  wish 25 -> grant 25, gap p50 40.4 ms p95 54.2
  wish 50 -> grant 50, gap p50 34.8 ms p95 47.8 (min 0.0: two in one read)
  wish 60 -> grant 60, gap p50 35.0 ms p95 46.7

So the WELCOME/SUBSCRIBE grant says 50/60 Hz but the channel is delivered at about 21 Hz on the sim and 28 Hz on the P4, whatever the grant. SPEC 10.2 clamps a rate to max_rate_hz (60 here) and nothing says a grant may be met below its rate. The sim's 46.8 ms is 3 x 15.6 ms (sim main.cpp calls timeBeginPeriod(1), so not the Windows timer by itself; suspect the motion engine's publish cadence or the pacer tick). Why it matters: a client sizes its render delay to 1.5 x the arrival p95 gap, so this gap is ~70 of the ~100 ms Phosphor still adds to the numeral (Phosphor ph-6vh). Either deliver at the grant or grant what will be delivered.
notes:
2026-10-09 triage: val-27y closed as its duplicate. Its finding: the census refreshes at kPublishUs = 20 ms (ValenceMotion.cpp:58), and 0.1.28 measured 28.6 Hz (35 ms median) idle and streaming alike, so the cadence is not stream load.
2026-10-10 root cause + fix (branch fix/telemetry-rate 71199fd in worktree ../Nucleus-rate, unmerged; Valence main be2f7c9). Cause 1 (Nucleus): ValenceDevice::tick published 0x1100 once 33 ms had passed since the last publish, checked on the 5 ms hub tick -> 35 ms gaps, 28.6 Hz at any grant (old twin 46.8 ms = same gate on a 15.6 ms timer tick). 0x1110 same gate at 50 ms -> 20 Hz under 45. Cause 2 (Valence lib): SubscriptionEntry restarted the period at each push and truncated to whole ms -> 60 Hz grant on a 5 ms tick delivered 50, 1 ms tick 62.5. Fix: pacer is a schedule (us, rounded up, re-anchors when a whole period late); 0x1100/0x1110 publish at catalog max_rate_hz on that pacer; P4 census kPublishUs 20 -> 10 ms. valencesim before -> after (6 s, idle and moving): 50 Hz 28.3 -> 50.0, 60 Hz 28.5 -> 60.0, 0x1110@45 19.8 -> 45.0, rate-0 wish held to 60. Without the pin bump 60 Hz delivers 51.8. OPEN: valence.pin bump to be2f7c9 (operator), merge, P4 measurement (expect 50/60 Hz, gaps 20 / 15+20 ms from the 5 ms tick).
2026-10-10 LANDED on Nucleus main: merge f4929c3 (fix/telemetry-rate 71199fd, --no-ff), valence.pin -> Valence be2f7c9 (grant scheduler, subscription.hpp) in 5a3ab4f; frozen sibling hashes unchanged (measured). canon_lint 0 findings; pio test -e native 26/26 suites PASSED; flagship_p4_bench compiles; FIRMWARE_VERSION not bumped (still 0.1.40, next build takes 0.1.41). valencesim rebuilt from main (old exe aside as build/valencesim.running-20261010-0425.exe, locked by a running suite); rate_probe on main: 0x1100 grant 50 -> 50.0 Hz, grant 60 -> 60.0 Hz idle / 59.9 Hz driven; 0x1110 grants 50/60 -> granted 45 (ceiling) -> 45.0 Hz. Worktree Nucleus-rate and branch fix/telemetry-rate removed. OWED: the P4 measurement (unflashed; no flash/OTA in this pass). Kept open for that.

title: A move refused SOURCE_CONFLICT by the delegate still takes the Jog source: the next session's move is refused TAKEOVER_REQUIRED
description:
A motion intent refused by the delegate still leaves the refusing session OWNING the source it acquired, so the next session's move is refused TAKEOVER_REQUIRED by an owner that never moved anything. Found from Phosphor ph-vdk.55 (test/safety-live.mjs), measured 2026-10-02 against valencesim (Nucleus 0.1.5-p4hub, catalog etag 92cb8dce4ccd9e65, Valence pin a88c6bf), three control-tier sessions, each with its own /uitoken:

1. streamer (session 1183908628) publishes motion-input samples at 50 Hz; control-owner (0x0004) reads owner0 0, owner1 1183908628 (Stream).
2. other (session 1474275172): INTENT 0x3100 move {1: 100.0} -> NACK SOURCE_CONFLICT. control-owner now reads owner0 1474275172 (Jog), owner1 1183908628.
3. streamer stops and closes; 1.5 s later control-owner reads owner0 1474275172, owner1 0.
4. third (session 2824702872): INTENT 0x3100 move {1: 200.0} -> NACK TAKEOVER_REQUIRED. The Jog source belongs to a session whose only move was refused.

In the page: after a refused move, the operator's jog under override reads 'refused: TAKEOVER_REQUIRED (Move to)' until the refused session leaves.

Mechanism (read, not measured): Valence lib hub_impl.hpp handleIntent step 6 acquires source ownership (Acquired, publishControlOwnerState) BEFORE step 7's delegate applyIntent, and the delegate's refusal path NACKs without releasing what step 6 just acquired. SPEC 11.4 has ownership decided by the hub; a refused intent took no control, so an acquisition made for it should not outlive the refusal (AlreadyOwner and TakenOver need their own answer: a TakenOver followed by a refusal has already displaced the previous owner). The fix's home is likely the Valence hub library (lib/), owned there; filed here because the sim and the P4 run it.

Acceptance: step 2's refusal leaves owner0 at 0, and step 4's move is accepted.
notes:
2026-10-09 triage: still valid. The reported repro is now refused by the hub's rail gate BEFORE acquisition (Valence 3f4bd87, RFC-098 railHeldByOtherSource). The general hole remains: hub_impl.hpp step 6 acquires (Acquired/TakenOver, ~1966-1987), and a delegate refusal at step 7 NACKs without releasing it. Fix home: the Valence library.
2026-10-09: library fix landed in Valence cb9b810 (hub releases a source an intent Acquired or TookOver when the delegate refuses it; reason 2; a takeover is released, not handed back: veto-able). Closes here once valence.pin moves past cb9b810 and the sim repro (or its rail-gate-free variant) is re-run.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/u8a-resets d8c990d (worktree ../Nucleus-u8a, unmerged). The library half (Valence cb9b810) is inside valence.pin be2f7c9. Nucleus root cause: applyMove() stamped _jogMark before motionSubmit(); a refused submit (intent queue full) counted nothing, so sourceQuiet(Manual) stayed false and the jog's owner kept the source after its last move settled (the AlreadyOwner case the library keeps by design). The mark now lands only with the submit. Evidence: test_valence_device VD-OWN-1 (refused move leaves owner0 0, a second session's move ECHOed) and VD-OWN-2 (owner's second move refused, first settles, owner0 0, second session ECHOed; failed before the fix) [verified 2026-10-10 -- program.exe 64/64]. Not re-run: the sim/Phosphor safety-live repro (its original path is caught earlier by the RFC-098 rail gate).

title: LP IO clock: an HP-side gpio_config() or gpio_reset_pin() on any LP pad can gate the emitter's LP GPIO clock
description:
Found reading ESP-IDF 5.5.4 for val-091.30 [source read 2026-10-02, not bench-verified]. gpio_config(), gpio_reset_pin() and gpio_config_as_analog() call rtc_gpio_deinit() on every LP pad (GPIO0-15). On the P4 that calls io_mux_force_disable_lp_io_clock() (esp_hw_support/port/esp32p4/io_mux.c), which clears LP_GPIO.clk_en.reg_clk_en whenever the HP-side claim mask is empty. The LP core turns that clock on from its own side (ulp_lp_core_gpio_init -> _rtcio_ll_enable_io_clock(true)), so the HP mask stays empty, and the first such HP call after the emitter starts gates the clock under QUAD_A/QUAD_B. The bit is documented Reserved (reset 1), so the effect is unmeasured; the feared one is frozen quadrature while ulp_g_edges keeps counting, i.e. position truth that lies.
Today: nothing triggers it. BoardPins.h carries the rule (accessory LP pads are set up with gpio_set_direction / gpio_set_pull_mode and the peripheral drivers' own pin setup, never gpio_config or gpio_reset_pin), and ValenceAccessoryIo.cpp follows it. LEDC, HP I2C and HP UART pin setup do not call rtc_gpio_deinit (read in the same IDF).
Owed: (1) the structural fix, so no future caller can trip it: the emitter's HP host claims the clock at LP launch (rtc_gpio_init() on QUAD_A and QUAD_B, idempotent with what the LP core already selected, or the private io_mux_enable_lp_io_clock()); (2) the bench proof, folded into val-091.18's run: with the emitter rendering, gpio_config() an unused LP pad and scope QUAD_A/B, then repeat with the fix.

title: valencesim drops a GOODBYE followed by a socket close in the same tick: the session parks STALE and the next HELLO reattaches
description:
A voluntary GOODBYE is lost when the WebSocket close follows it in the same tick, so the session parks STALE (RFC-042) instead of ending (SPEC 6.9), and the next HELLO from the same instance_id REATTACHES: same session_id, the old session's grants, its own HELLO wishes ignored (RFC-042 path B, correct for a real resume). Found from Phosphor ph-0bw (pairing-roundtrip.mjs), measured 2026-10-02 against valencesim (Nucleus 0.1.5-p4hub, catalog etag 92cb8dce4ccd9e65, Valence pin a88c6bf).

Frames (127.0.0.1, sim with --pairing-window, instance_id a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1):
1. A1: HELLO (no token, no wishes) -> WELCOME session_id S, roles 0.
2. A1: PAIR_REQ -> PAIR_GRANT role 2 (configure), 16-byte token.
3. A1: valence-js close(): GOODBYE {code: NORMAL_CLOSURE}, then ws.close() in the same JS tick. Sim log: 'ws: slot 0 detached', no session-left line.
4. 400 ms later A2: HELLO, same instance_id, token, key 10 subscriptions [{15: 0x000A pending-pairing}, {15: 0x000B pairing-events}] -> WELCOME session_id S (SAME), roles 2, grants [], retained_pending 0.

3 of 3 runs reattach. With only step 3's socket close delayed 50 ms behind the GOODBYE (a WebSocketImpl wrapper, nothing else changed): 3 of 3 runs get a fresh session_id, grants [0x000A, 0x000B], retained_pending 1. So the hub grants configure-tier HELLO wishes at the token's tier correctly; the GOODBYE is what goes missing.

Mechanism (read, not measured): WsServerPort's IX callback thread pushes the GOODBYE into the slot's RX ring, then raises _closeEvt. The sim's hub pass (sim/valencesim/src/main.cpp:385-386) runs port.loop() BEFORE hub.update(): consumeCloseEvent() -> hub.detachTransport() -> parkAndDetach() marks the session STALE and nulls the transport, then reap() and the next onOpen() reset the ring, so the queued GOODBYE is never pumped. Valence Bench uses the same WsServerPort (Valence hub/bench/src/net/WsServerPort.cpp, compiled into the sim from its home), so the fix likely belongs there or in the loop order: drain a slot's queued frames before honoring its close event. Unverified on the P4's own WS binding (a different transport).

Acceptance: Phosphor test/pairing-roundtrip.mjs check "A1's GOODBYE ended its session" passes (A2 gets a new session_id), and its knock checks pass on HELLO-carried wishes alone.
close_reason: 2026-10-09 triage: done. Valence 8b0361e (rfc-ia3) holds a close once while RX frames are queued, so GOODBYE+close ends the session in the bench port the sim uses; consumed through valence.pin (2de239c). P4 half was b789b57.

title: ESTOP_BYP (G29): the hardware unplugged-cable bypass as a single-session, configure-gated toggle, off at boot
description: Split from val-091.23 item (3); val-091.23 landed the runtime reader without it. Today selfCheckHoldMotorOff() drives G29 LOW for the boot and nothing raises it. title: 0x3000 config-set stores a NaN: fieldF32 + clampf pass it, and the next boot refuses the whole cfg blob
description: ValenceDevice.cpp applyIntent, the config_set branch (keys 1-8), reads each key with fieldF32() and clamps with clampf(), and clampf passes NaN (numberOf()'s own comment: a clamp is only as good as the finite check in front of it). applyTuning and applyModes read through numberOf() and NACK INVALID_VALUE on non-finite; this writer does not, and the Valence CBOR reader admits any float32 bit pattern. Effects of one NaN write: the inverted-window refusal (window_min >= window_max) is false for NaN, so it is accepted; cfgChanged is true on every such write (NaN != NaN) and bumps cfg_gen; the ECHO and 0x1000 report NaN while MotionArbiter::setWindow ignores non-finite input and keeps the old window, so the reported machine does not exist (Ground Truth); the debounced persist writes the NaN and the next boot refuses the whole blob (BadConfig since 3f3653e), so window, ceilings, tuning, modes and the commissioning record all fall back to factory and content motion is re-gated. comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02, b789b57. Root cause found on valencesim, which reproduced it (24 pass / 3 fail: pair1/pair2_pending_state, knock_teardown): the probe GOODBYEs and closes each session inside one hub tick; the port applied the recorded detach BEFORE Hub::update() read the RX ring, so the GOODBYE was never read and the session PARKED (RFC-042) instead of ending (sim log: 12 joined, 1 left). The admin's configure reconnect then REATTACHED to its parked watch-era bootstrap session, and a reattach keeps the parked grants verbatim: 3 grants (0x000B, 0x000E, 0x0003), never 0x000A, so no pending STATE could reach it and the departed-knocker check saw no 0x000A at all.
Answer to "Nucleus or the Valence library": both halves exist. Nucleus: ValenceWsPort::loop() now holds a recorded detach while the slot's RX ring still has frames (one tick: nothing refills it after close_fn). Valence: (1) the bench WS port the sim uses has the same ordering, rfc-ia3 with the patch; (2) a LIBRARY defect it exposed, rfc-7au with the patch: a reattach after a ROLE change keeps the old role's grants (upgrade never gets configure channels; a revoked device keeps receiving configure STATE). Measured: sim built against Valence with both patches 27/0; with the port patch alone 27/0 (sessions end on GOODBYE, 12 joined / 10 left), so the port ordering is the probe's cause and rfc-7au is latent in that run.
[verified 2026-10-02 -- host: patched valencesim probe --pair 27/0; pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS]. Bench verdict owed: valence_probe --pair against the P4, expected 25/25 (pending_state and knock_teardown pass).

Root cause: MotionArbiter::evaluate() returns early while the power gate is shut, before it ever reads _return_req, so a return accepted unpowered waited for a planner arrival that cannot happen. returnToPause() now answers a ReturnStart: gate open = queued (as before); gate shut = decided on the calling task from the emitter count and the paused position: within one step = arrived (override drops, returns counts, the delegate's tick() clears the hub override off that count); further = unpowered, NACKed INTERLOCK with "motor power off (switch off)" and override held. Also fixed: a pause that landed while unpowered discarded its brake request without recording a rest point, so the return target was a stale earlier pause; the unpowered branch now records the parked carriage. _pause_pos_mm and _returns became atomics (written from the motion task and the hub task).
Known residual, not fixed: a return QUEUED with power on and voided by a power loss mid-way leaves the delegate's _returnPending set until an ESTOP clears it; on this board every switch fault latches one (tick), so the window is a cut without a fault, which the board does not produce today.

title: CANON FLAG: SPEC 9.6 rest-without-successor is not implemented; unspecified end velocity resolves to the stream estimate
description:
Raised while landing val-091.43, which asked to confirm the rest-without-successor resolution matches the landed SPEC text. It does not.

Source A: Valence spec/SPEC.md 9.6 at 9dd395d: 'Without a scheduled successor the hub MUST resolve unspecified to rest (0), never to an estimate derived from prior motion.'
Source B: lib/kinetic/include/kinetic/kinetic.hpp commitWaveform: vf = has_end_vel ? end_vel : (chase_feedforward && est_ema_ok && streamIsDense()) ? est_v_ema * chase_ff_gain : 0. The decode (ValenceDevice.cpp onStreamBundle) leaves has_end_vel false for the sentinel, and nothing in Nucleus sets Command::has_next_chord, so no segment ever has a known successor at commit time. RFC-058's own receipt (2026-09-03) recorded the same gap on the S3 (sd-4k1.20, archived board), never ported.

My read: the spec is ratified and the code is wrong, but the fix is a motion-feel decision, not a one-liner. Options: (a) resolve unspecified to 0 always (conformant, the MAY is unexercised; an I-only segments stream then arrives at rest at every knot); (b) the bundle decode supplies the successor's chord for every segment but a bundle's last (derive vf from adjoining chords per the MAY, rest on the bundle tail); (c) (b) plus re-planning a queued, not-yet-started tail when its successor arrives, so one-segment bundles also flow. (b)/(c) also arm the RFC-008 handoff guard, which is dead in Nucleus today for the same reason.

Your call: which of (a), (b), (c), and is the feel regression of (a) acceptable as an interim?
close_reason: 2026-10-09 triage: superseded. The flagged path was Kinetic 1's commitWaveform estimate, gone with 0b29990; Kinetic² rests a free knot with no successor (RFC-106). The one deliberate exception, Engine::expect for a stream owner (27d0ff2, val-g62), is recorded in RFC-105 log (v) and lands through rfc-105.

title: Dwell rule defeated by the arbiter's at-rest re-seed: a hold re-sent after the machine came to rest whips through it
description:
Found landing val-091.43 (host-verified, test_motion_arbiter). MotionArbiter::plan() re-seeds the engine at rest (Engine::resetAt), and resetAt clears _prev_wave_tgt_ok, so the dwell rule (SPEC 9.6, registry limits.segment_dwell_span, anomaly kind 10) never sees a re-sent hold once the previous hold segment has ended and the engine went idle. That is exactly the field shape RFC-058 origin 1 measured (hold re-sent ~1 Hz during lulls with a stale tangent; 54 mm lost on the S3). Repro: arbiter rig, Stream segment to 200 mm (132 ms, vf 0), run 400 ms, re-send the same target with vf -900 mm/s: census anom[DwellZeroed] == 0; re-sent at 60 ms (still in flight) it is 1.

SPEC 9.6 keys the rule on the previous ACCEPTED target on the same source, with no reset clause. Options for the ruling: (a) resetAt keeps the dwell latch (stream memory, like the cadence under the One activity clock rule) and only frame moves (force_home, window change, rail frame) clear it; (b) the arbiter's at-rest door re-seeds position without touching stream memory (a narrower Engine entry). The kinetic header comment that clears the latch on re-seed ('inheriting one turns the first post-seed stroke into a dwell') is the line to revisit. A false-positive dwell only zeroes one vf (conservative); a false negative is a whip.

Prove it: the arbiter case above passes with a 400 ms gap; test_kinetic re-seed cases unchanged; bench: a hold re-sent at 1 Hz with vf != 0 shows no excursion on the encoder.
close_reason: cf7fbdf: Engine::reseedAt keeps the dwell rule's previous target across the arbiter's at-rest re-seed (option b of the bead); every frame-moving reset still clears it. Arbiter case re-sends after rest: fails on the old code, passes now [verified 2026-10-02 -- pio test -e native exit 0, pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS]. Bench stamp owed: a hold re-sent at ~1 Hz after the carriage stops, with a stale vf, shows dwell_zeroed in kinetic-diag and no encoder excursion.

title: Name the EN-node drop's cause: read the board monitor's latched fault code when the motor switch faults en_node
description: Split from val-091.24 item (2). The motor switch module (MotorSwitch.h, ValenceMotorSwitch.cpp) latches faulted with Fault::en_node when the EN/UVLO wired-OR (G23) falls while pre-charging or on, latches ESTOP cause fault, and on the next enable reads the INA DIAG_ALRT (powerTakeAlerts) and logs its flags. Not done: telling the four pullers apart (E-stop Q901, bus OVP Q405, INA ALERT, board monitor FAULT_N). Owed: on an en_node fault, read the board monitor's STATUS latched fault bits (docs/supervisor.md, Supervisor.h) off the switch task (I2C, never the motion task) and name the cause over Valence; the hardware E-stop case is val-091.23's reader (cause user, not fault). Needs the board monitor runtime link (val-091.19).

title: Upstream: the reference hub DROPS a segments bundle stamped beyond the horizon; RFC-084 says clamp
description: Valence lib/valence hub_impl.hpp handleStream step 3c (at pin 715e21c) drops a c2h segments bundle whose LAST start lies more than the granted horizon ahead of hub time, before HubDelegate::onStreamBundle runs. SPEC 5.4 (RFC-084): a sample stamped further out is CLAMPED, not rejected. Nucleus clamps every sample that reaches it (ValenceDevice::onStreamBundle, lead capped at the horizon for segments and max_future_schedule_ms for samples, e678979), but cannot clamp what the library never hands it, and Valence is read-only from here. The 1dbdc3e lander flagged the gap as pre-existing. Needs a Valence-side fix (rfc- board) and then a valence.pin bump; nothing more owed here once it lands.
close_reason: 2026-10-09 triage: done. Valence 9dd395d clamps a c2h bundle to the 5.4 lead cap instead of dropping (hub_impl.hpp step 3c, clampLead); in valence.pin.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Fixed upstream in Valence 9dd395d (feat/rfc-050-blob-done): handleStream clamps instead of dropping, both kinds. Rule: the whole bundle moves earlier until its LAST stamp sits on now + cap (granted horizon for segments, max_future_schedule_ms for samples); order and spacing kept; only BundleView::tBase() moves, payload bytes keep the sent t_base, so the delegate must read tBase()/sampleTimeUs(), never the raw header. Past stamps never move. Malformed bundles (span cap t_off[n-1]*100us <= horizon, n, order, size) still rejected whole. Needs a valence.pin bump to 9dd395d. Spec wording conflict in 5.4 rule 3 filed as rfc-0wp.

title: 0x1111 sync_dropped does not count bundles the hub drops under PAUSE
description: RFC-085 / SPEC 11.1: a source-mapped bundle under PAUSE is dropped and counted 'in the hub's existing stream-drop counter where it publishes one'. Since e09c50e the library drops it before onStreamBundle, so it lands only in the hub's per-session StreamIngressCounters (Hub::streamIngressCounters), which nothing publishes; 0x1111 sync_dropped counts delegate-side SAMPLE drops only. Options: fold per-slot dropped deltas into motion-diag in ValenceDevice::tick (bundles vs samples units differ: needs its own field or a units decision), or accept the per-session counter as the home. Found while landing val-091.34.
close_reason: Landed f7cc19c (host-verified 2026-10-02: test_ingress_drop_tally 6/6 run directly, pio test -e native exit 0, pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS; live valencesim ports 8962/8969: 10 bundles streamed under PAUSE moved sync_dropped 0->10, a second back-to-back session 10->20). The drop happens in Valence hub_impl.hpp handleStream (PAUSE check after sourceForChannel, ++streamBundlesDropped, before onStreamBundle). ValenceDevice::tick folds Hub::streamIngressCounters per-slot deltas every hub tick (IngressDropTally.h, new session id = new baseline) and publishMotionDiag adds the total to sync_dropped; sync_enqueued unchanged. VETO-ABLE DECISIONS: (1) a dropped bundle counts ONE in sync_dropped (desc says samples; the library keeps no sample count for a dropped bundle, so the field understates) chosen over a new layout field, which would move the catalog etag; (2) all library ingress drops are counted, not only PAUSE, per SPEC 11.1 'exactly as 9.2's ingress drops are'. No catalog change, etag 830ca5fa689f3814. Ceiling: drops a session makes in the tick it leaves are lost (<= one 5 ms tick).

title: RFC-076/077: accessory capacity advertised on the accessories roster, in JOIN_REPLY, and refused with NACK ACCESSORY_CAPACITY
description:
RFC-076 (rfc-7bq) and RFC-077 (rfc-cou) ACCEPTED, operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 01:32). Slice width 32 ids (accessory_slice_ids 0x20): r=0 session-scoped, r=1 accessory-status, r=2..31 the accessory's own (30 at most). User space 0x8000-0xBFFF holds 512 slices; a forgotten slice is never reused for the life of a hub. User space is accessories only.

Change: the capacity budgets (per accessory and overall user space, in entries/fields/bytes as the landed text names them) are advertised on the accessories roster STATE; JOIN_REPLY carries the remaining capacity; a declaration that does not fit is refused with NACK ACCESSORY_CAPACITY carrying the numbers (SPEC 4.5). Budgets are computed from the build-time catalog capacities (sibling bead, RFC-077 item 8), never a second constant. Answers Isotope iso-yg8.

Likely files: the join handler and accessory store from val-9u0.11, ValenceCatalog.h accessories roster, sim/valencesim twin.

Prove it: native accessory-store suite: a join that overflows any budget is NACKed ACCESSORY_CAPACITY with the numbers and leaves the store and catalog unchanged; valencesim shows the roster budget fall by one slice per join.

title: RFC-077 item 8: size the Flagship build's catalog capacities for its accessory count at 30 channels per slice
description:
RFC-077 (rfc-cou) ACCEPTED, item 8 ruled 2026-10-01 (comment 01:32): break it now, before any tag: the reference library's catalog capacities (Catalog32 entries, layout and schema field counts, kCatalogScratchBytes) become a BUILD-TIME PARAMETER of the hub; the Flagship build is sized for its accessory count (RFC-076 at 30 channels per slice; val-9u0.5 sizing recomputed). Risk accepted knowingly by the operator.

Change: once the Valence library exposes the parameter (Valence reference-library capacity bead), the Flagship build instantiates its catalog at the capacity val-9u0.5 picks: machine catalog (42/48 entries, 188/200 layout, 23,595 B encoded today per docs/accessory-store-sizing.md) plus N accessories x (30 channels + status entry). Pools live in PSRAM (T2), the encode scratch too; no catalog-sized temporaries on any stack (T1). valencesim builds at the same parameter.

Prove it: native build of buildValenceCatalog at the chosen capacity with N worst-case 30-channel declarations encodes under the scratch with the 80% headroom floor; [stack] census unchanged; P4 boots with the larger pools and heap headroom stated (memory-budget.md updated).

title: RFC-069/079: wifi_join accepted over BLE GATT and the USB serial binding, both live at once in config mode
description:
RFC-069 (rfc-qf5) ACCEPTED as drafted, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:11): the gate already admits BLE GATT, serial and in-process; the section 13.5 USB serial binding is a FIRST-CLASS provisioning path beside BLE; in config mode both are active at once and both accept wifi_join. No hub-published SSID scan list: the client enters the SSID. RFC-079 (rfc-ewm, comment 01:11) confirms config mode activates BLE advertising AND the USB serial binding together. RFC-054 is obsolete (no hub-discloses-credentials path).

Change:
- wifi_join INTENT handler on the hub: secret-flagged passphrase never echoed or logged, ECHO carries ipv4 + ws_port on success, NACK NETWORK_JOIN_FAILED on failure; credentials persisted in NVS only after a successful join.
- A USB serial transport port for the Valence hub (section 13.5 framing) beside the C6 BLE path; callbacks enqueue, never mutate hub state (T5); session teardown through the one funnel (T3). The P4's USB-Serial-JTAG or the CH340 path, whichever the board routes (state it here).
- Config-mode boot (val-9u0.14) brings up both transports; normal boot keeps serial available only if the draft says so.

Reference client to test against: rfc-cat (clients/provision, Web Bluetooth + Web Serial) and Phosphor's wizard (ph-vdk.24).

Prove it: valencesim over serial accepts wifi_join and answers ECHO; bench stamp on the P4: factory-fresh board in config mode provisioned once over Web Serial and once over Web Bluetooth, each joins and the next boot connects; passphrase absent from /diag and the log ring.
close_reason: c075519: serial binding + provisioning desk, host-verified; catalog val-9u0.21, bench val-9u0.23, desk move val-9u0.22 carry the rest

Serial binding is SPEC 13.5 COBS (0x00 + COBS + 0x00), live in every mode on the stamp USB-Serial/JTAG shared with the console; the hub task is the port's only reader (zero-tick ring reads at the top of each tick), the driver ISR owns the FIFO. Desk answers 0x000F before the hub; joins run on the Provision task, outcome handed back by release/acquire sequence; ECHO true for ssid+passphrase, NVS 'sta' only after a join. Host-verified: test_serial_provisioning 20/235, pio run flagship_p4 SUCCESS. Dark until val-9u0.21 declares 0x000F; BLE GATT + ws_available ride val-9u0.14/val-9u0.18; valencesim over serial not done (sim not touched); bench val-9u0.23. Not flashed, COM15 not opened.

title: RFC-072: pin the BLE manufacturer-data layout (company_id 0xFFFF + flags u8); no _valence._tcp record; hostname responder only beside a served page
description:
RFC-072 (rfc-uvh) ACCEPTED AS RESCOPED, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:16): the _valence._tcp mDNS service record and its TXT keys are RETIRED (section 13.7 text and the mdns_service limit struck); native clients discover by the section 13.8 UDP probe, which carries hub_instance_id. A hub that SERVES A PAGE SHOULD run an mDNS hostname responder (machine.local); that is hostname resolution, not service browsing. Item 3 survives: the BLE manufacturer-data layout is pinned as company_id 0xFFFF + flags u8 (the 0xFFFF testing-id question stays open pre-v1.0). No TXT fw key.

Change for Nucleus:
- When the C6 BLE path lands (val-9u0.3/.14), the advertisement's manufacturer data is exactly company_id 0xFFFF + flags u8 (config_mode bit per RFC-079) from the generated registry constants.
- Never plan or add a _valence._tcp service record. Nucleus serves no page today (ValenceHttp: /ota and /diag only), so no hostname responder now; add it only with a served page.
- sim/valencesim: its --no-mdns flag is already a no-op; leave it for CLI compatibility or drop it with a C-9 proof.

Prove it: UDP probe 13.8 finds the P4 with hub_instance_id; a BLE scan (nRF Connect or Phosphor ble-adv.js) decodes company 0xFFFF and the flags byte from the P4 in config mode.

title: RFC-079: machine geometry and kinetic ceilings become setup-category (15) settings with a required first-run pass
description:
RFC-079 (rfc-ewm) ACCEPTED with ui category 15 setup, operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 01:11, 01:16 scope, 01:17 principle).

Scope ruling: category 15 is the machine COMMISSIONING surface: network credentials, machine name, accessory pairing, AND the machine's own geometry and ceilings (rail length, travel window, speed/accel/jerk ceilings, geometry, degree-to-mm ratio). Pinout and board facts stay out. Categories are static per entry, so these entries carry setup in every mode; the wizard steps through them in authoring order.

Operator principle: the Flagship is a motor controller strapped to any machine with a motor. How motor motion becomes machine motion is the OWNER's configuration, entered through setup, never firmware knowledge. The rail archetype presents that configuration; it is not an assumption in the firmware.

Change:
- machine-config (0x1000) and its writer config-set, and the kinetic ceilings (kinetic-limits jmax/vmax/amax and wherever max_rail lives) move to category setup (ValenceCatalog.h ~511, ~1253, ~1745, ~1903). If a ceiling shares a channel with non-setup tuning, split the pair (the catalog's own 'a category that outgrows its channel SPLITS' rule, ~72-77).
- Geometry and ceilings are settings with sane defaults (never compile-time constants that a client cannot change), persisted via StoredState, plus a REQUIRED first-run pass: a factory-fresh hub reports itself uncommissioned (the draft names how) and refuses motion until the owner has confirmed the setup values.
- Authoring order in the catalog is the wizard's step order: network, name, geometry, ceilings, pairing.

Prove it: native test_stored_state covers the new setup fields' persistence; a factory-fresh valencesim refuses motion until the setup pass is written; Phosphor's wizard (ph-vdk.24) walks category 15 against valencesim end to end; catalog lint zero findings.
close_reason: 2026-10-09 triage: done host-side. Catalog half d7565f3 (category 15 on machine-config and kinetic-limits), first-run refusal dde220a, sim posture 8281f12. The end-to-end wizard proof is Phosphor ph-vdk.24.

Wizard order = ascending id. [verified 2026-10-02 -- probe census setup on both]. Open: the first-run pass (uncommissioned report, motion refused) and test_stored_state coverage are the sibling half.

StoredModes.setup_written (config blob v5), kSetupRequiredMask = all eight 0x3000 keys, arbiter gate refuses Stream/Pattern while uncommissioned (Manual moves, as unhomed; veto-able), older blobs migrate uncommissioned.

FOR THE CATALOG/SIM OWNER (sibling): (1) category 15 move of machine-config/config-set and the kinetic-limits ceilings is yours, in wizard order network, name, geometry, ceilings, pairing. (2) 'reports itself uncommissioned' needs a wire home: suggest a hub-status (or machine-config) field carrying commissioned (bool) or setup_written vs required (u8 pair); ValenceDevice holds both (_modes.setup_written, kSetupRequiredMask in StoredState.h). Until then the only signals are the 0x0402 NACK on pattern start, the arbiter's 'REJECT: not commissioned' log and the census rejected count for streams. (3) I added ONE line to sim/valencesim/src/SimMotion.cpp (motionSetCommissioned forwarder) so the twin links and gates. (4) A factory-fresh valencesim now refuses stream and pattern motion even with --homed until a config-set pass: Phosphor e2e flows against a fresh --state need that write first, or a sim flag that commissions (your call).

title: RFC-073: pattern-presets store items carry the optional payload digest (blob_keys 11)
description:
RFC-073 (rfc-019) ACCEPTED as drafted, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 02:06): digest over payload only, kind domains open. Ratifies Nucleus's reuse of blob_keys 3/5/6/7 (slot, name, kind, payload) for store items (val-091.12, commit 631f31d).

Change: emit the OPTIONAL blob_keys 11 digest (SHA-256 over the payload bytes only) on each pattern-presets item so BLOB_DONE status 1 (hash mismatch) is decidable without a caller-supplied expectDigest; name/payload bounds tie to the STORE entry's name_max/per_item_max. The P4 has hardware SHA (mbedtls); the sim uses the same code path. Optional by ruling: skip if a measured cost says so, and state it here.

Likely files: flagship_p4/src/patterns/PatternPresetStore.h, flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceDevice.cpp readBlob.

Prove it: native round trip: item encode carries key 11, a flipped payload byte fails the digest check; Valence clients/js BLOB_DONE reports status 1 on a tampered item against valencesim.
close_reason: 63ce1eb: PatternPresetStore::encodeItem emits blob_keys 11 SHA-256 over the payload on every item; blob scratch 128 -> 160 B with a static_assert. Library software SHA, same path on sim. [verified 2026-10-02 -- test_stored_state 10/10: digest present, flipped byte HashMismatch]. Valence clients/js tamper test against valencesim not run.

title: RFC-065: events.anomaly role and event_kinds labels on motion-anomaly; anomaly.summary on kinetic-diag
description:
RFC-065 (rfc-x3n) ACCEPTED as drafted, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:19), open question 1 answered yes: the STATE twin carries channel role anomaly.summary so log and counters bind together.

Change:
- motion-anomaly EVENT (ValenceCatalog.h addMotionAnomaly ~1098): entry-level purpose role events.anomaly and the entry-level append-only event_kinds label map (none, plan_failed, settle, endvel_clamped, deadline_stretched, waveform_fallback, waveform_scaled, waveform_centered, handoff_bounded, waveform_smoothed, dwell_zeroed, in kinetic::AnomalyType order). The body key 1 select-with-options mirror stays only if the landed text still wants it; kinds are labelled by event_kinds from now on.
- kinetic-diag STATE (~996): channel role anomaly.summary.
- The pause_latched/pause_cleared rename on session-events (RFC-085 PAUSE bead) uses the same event_kinds mechanism if those are device kinds.

Needs the library to emit the two new entry keys (Valence reference-library catalog-keys bead).

Prove it: catalog lint zero findings; valence_probe anomaly vocab check reads labels from event_kinds and PASSes; Phosphor ph-vdk.39 binds the anomaly log by role against valencesim.
close_reason: 166b2b4: 0x4100 role events.anomaly + event_kinds (11, AnomalyType order); body key 1 keeps the kind, drops its labels (SPEC 9.4: mirror is never the label home); 0x1111 anomaly.summary. [verified 2026-10-02 -- probe census]. probe anomaly_vocab SKIPs until it reads event_kinds (Valence side).

title: RFC-086: new unit ids (us, hub-time stamp, deg) on fields that carry them
description:
RFC-086 (rfc-263) PRE-APPROVED and landing directly as ACCEPTED with registry allocation of the three unit ids, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:37). Display autoranging is a client choice.

Change: retag every field whose unit is microseconds or a hub-time stamp with the registered unit ids instead of free strings: motion-anomaly t_us (hub-time stamp), plan-strip duration_us / elapsed_us (us), kinetic-diag plan_us_last/max/avg (us), any *_us in kinetic-chase/kinetic-waveform settings; deg where a field carries degrees (machine geometry, if the setup-category bead adds an angle). Keep the scale semantics unchanged.

Likely files: flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceCatalog.h, sim/valencesim. Prove it: catalog lint zero findings at the pin bump; grep '.unit = "us"' over ValenceCatalog.h matches only fields the registry unit covers.
close_reason: 5eafe6f: unit_id us on duration_us, elapsed_us, plan_us_last/max/avg and 0x4100 t_us; every '.unit = "us"' field tagged. t_us hub-time cannot ride: hub_s is seconds and a schema field has no scale, no us hub-time unit registered. No degree field exists. [verified 2026-10-02 -- probe census].

title: RFC-063: mark destructive ops and settings with the setting_flags destructive bit and destructive_options mask
description:
RFC-063 (rfc-c5u) ACCEPTED as drafted, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:19): setting_flags gains destructive; schema-field key destructive_options (64-bit per-option mask) for op selects; action.reboot/action.reset roles imply it; background_run stays confirm-gated by role; the RENDERING 5.4 pointer repair lands with it. Clients MUST confirm-gate; the hub never relies on it.

Change: audit every op select and setting in flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceCatalog.h and set the bit/mask where the act cannot be undone: machine-admin 0x30F0 (~1966: clear_fault, save_config, servo_scan; decide per op and state the verdict here, servo_scan if it moves or re-addresses the drive), pattern-presets-cmd delete (destructive by RFC-067 registration; set the mask anyway if the landed text asks emitters to), any future reboot/reset op (implied by role). Needs the library encoder to emit the bit and the destructive_options key (Valence reference-library catalog-keys bead).

Prove it: catalog lint zero findings; Phosphor's confirm seam (ph-vdk.31) gates exactly the flagged options against valencesim.
close_reason: 49ff2da: audit verdict, no op or setting destructive. machine-admin clear_fault (latch re-asserts), save_config (values stay client-writable), servo_scan (register reads only, archived handler) all no; presets delete destructive by registration (RFC-067), no mask. Trust surface ops are the library's. Constraint comment at the op table.

title: RFC-088: Flip mode on machine-modes with mirrored position, window and every c2h target
description:
RFC-088 (rfc-tnm), operator direction 2026-10-01 plus the label ruling (comment 01:21: label is Flip, not Invert).

Change:
- A stored mode on machine-modes (0x1030) written through modes-set (0x3030), persisted across reboot (it describes how the machine is mounted), registered role per the landed registry (draft proposed axis.inverted; take the landed name).
- Effect: position 0 becomes the far end; the hub mirrors position telemetry (motion pos/tgt/raw), the travel window (window.* roles), every c2h stream and intent target, so no client needs to know the state; presets keep their meaning.
- Gate (hub MUST): NACK SOURCE_CONFLICT while any source owns the rail; NACK while unhomed; never acts mid-motion.

Likely files: flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceCatalog.h (machine-modes ~1122-1200, modes-set ~1854), StoredState (persist), MotionArbiter (gate), the kinetic input/telemetry boundary in ValenceMotion.cpp (mirror once, at the edge, not inside kinetic), sim/valencesim.

Prove it: native arbiter case: flip under a stream NACKs SOURCE_CONFLICT, flip unhomed NACKs, flip homed accepted and persisted; bench stamp named by the draft: a homed rail flips and telemetry reads travel minus position.
close_reason: Landed 26b3aed (host-verified 2026-10-02: native exit 0 incl. arbiter mirror and force_home-under-flip cases, stored v4 flip round trip and v3 migration; pio run SUCCESS; valencesim live: moving INTERLOCK, at rest ECHO with telemetry rail-minus-position and the window mirrored, generator owning SOURCE_CONFLICT, unhomed NOT_HOMED). Mirror lives in MotionArbiter (the one core both hosts compile) rather than ValenceMotion.cpp, so the sim cannot drift; kinetic never sees it. Travel = the asserted stroke (this board has no measured travel). Bench stamp OWED (no board): a homed rail flips and telemetry reads travel minus position.

title: RFC-084: commit() treats a samples-kind chase point's future anchor as its arrival time
description:
RFC-084 (rfc-csn) ACCEPTED as drafted, ruled together with RFC-059, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:28). Nucleus follow-up named by the ruling: commit() treats a chase point's future anchor as its ARRIVAL time; ph-vdk.26 sine is the regression case.

Today: lib/kinetic/include/kinetic/kinetic.hpp ~513 'Scheduled start (anchored commit)': commit() anchors the plan at anchor_us as a scheduled START, and the hub clamps future anchors at 250 ms. For samples-kind (chased) points the anchor is when the point should be REACHED, so the planner must aim to arrive at anchor_us, not depart from it. Segments-kind keeps its scheduled-start meaning (RFC-087 horizon bounds start time).

Likely files: lib/kinetic (commit anchor branch keyed by stream kind), flagship_p4/src/motion/MotionArbiter.cpp (anchor pass-through ~185), flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceDevice.cpp (samples decode), the lead cap per the landed SPEC 5.4 text.

Prove it: test/native/test_kinetic case: a samples point anchored 100 ms ahead is reached at its anchor within the chase budget, not 100 ms late; Phosphor's ph-vdk.26 sine through the samples STREAM shows no phase lag beyond schedule_latency_us on a bench capture.
close_reason: 1569d02: commit() plans a future-anchored chase point as an arrival (starts where the previous point arrives, Ruckig minimum_duration to the anchor); segments keep scheduled start; due points unchanged. ph-vdk.26 shape (1 Hz sine, 100 ms lead, 30 ms jitter): factory lag 1 ms / peak +0.19 % of amplitude (was -5 ms / +2.3 %), session tuning lag 8 ms (was 28) [verified 2026-10-02 -- pio test -e native exit 0, pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS]. Bench stamp owed: Phosphor's ph-vdk.26 sine through the samples STREAM on the P4, position telemetry lags the stamped curve by no more than schedule_latency_us (val-091.44) and peaks within one scope sample of the media cue.

title: RFC-087: segments-kind bundles span the schedule horizon; horizon advertised per grant (250 default, 500, 1000)
description:
RFC-087 (rfc-66i), operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 01:06, 01:08). Draft lands as ACCEPTED once it addresses flush.

Change:
- For a c2h STREAM with stream_kind segments, the per-bundle span cap is the schedule horizon instead of bundle_max_span_ms (20); n stays bounded by bundle_max_samples (32) and the 242 B payload. Samples-kind and every h2c STREAM keep the 20 ms span.
- The hub advertises its horizon per grant (new granted_publishes key beside schedule_latency_us): 250 ms default, 500 or 1000 for poor WiFi; registry ceiling 1000. The horizon is a CAP on how far ahead a segment's start may be stamped, never a delay the hub adds and never a wait for a bundle to fill: each segment executes at its stamped time. Who picks 500/1000 on Nucleus (a setup-category setting is the natural home) is decided at implementation and stated here.
- Flush: at 1000 ms a player seek plays out up to a second of scheduled segments. The landed draft says whether pause-then-resume is the flush or a scheduled-plan flush gets its own spelling; implement exactly that (the queue clear on PAUSE belongs to the RFC-085 PAUSE bead's stream-drop path).
- A segment longer than the horizon is legal; a gap settles per section 6.6.

Companion bench: val-has (rapid-oscillation buffer effect) measures before the value is tuned. Likely files: flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceDevice.cpp (bundle validation, grant), flagship_p4/src/motion/ValenceMotion.cpp (segment queue depth must hold 1000 ms of 32/s), lib/kinetic, sim/valencesim.

Prove it: native case: a 32-segment bundle spanning 250 ms accepted, one spanning past the advertised horizon NACKed; valencesim probe reads the horizon key; bench stamp on the P4: a funscript at 1000 ms horizon renders segment starts at their stamps (scope on DBG marker, val-091.32).

Horizon picked by the operator through 0x1030 schedule_horizon (setting key 7), refused INTERLOCK while a segments grant is live. Queue 32 deep, lead 1000 ms (+16.5 KB internal bss). Supersede is the engine's drop-from-anchor. The beyond-cap clamp is done for everything that reaches the delegate; the library-side drop is filed as its own upstream bug. Bench stamp OWED (no board): a funscript at 1000 ms horizon renders segment starts at their stamps (scope on DBG marker, val-091.32).

description:
RFC-059 (rfc-r4v) ACCEPTED as drafted, ruled together with RFC-084, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 00:28): for samples-kind grants schedule_latency_us states the chase-planning budget. Commitment semantics: a change is a re-GRANT. Clients lead media by it and MUST NOT hardcode it.

Change: the hub delegate supplies the measured render delay per granted c2h motion STREAM (today ~120 ms + 40 ms behind the stream head for segments; the chase budget for samples) to the library's granted_publishes encoder (Valence reference-library granted_publishes bead). The value comes from kinetic's real configuration (chase_lookahead, chase_dense_ms, segment queue lead), computed, never a second constant; a kinetic-set write that moves it re-GRANTs.

Samples 0x2100 = chase_dense_us + kMotionTickUs, factory 61000 us. chase_dense change refused INTERLOCK while a samples grant is live (no production publish re-GRANT in the library; RFC-087 horizon precedent). [verified 2026-10-02 -- private valencesim build + clients/js: grants read 61000 / 1000 us, 81000 after dense 80, dense 90 NACK 0x0402 under a live samples grant; pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS]. title: PD daughterboard contract: PD_INT on LPG0, TPS26750 at 0x21 on the Qwiic bus, motor power profile from the source
description:

TPS26750 I2C target 0x21. Contract: the main-board input sees 24-36 V, never above 36 V; the main board never negotiates, it reads the contract over J16 and sizes the motor power profile (PD sources shut off rather than sag, so acceleration peaks stay under the source's 5 A). SPEC 2026-09-23 also asks for a 24 V or 36 V profile picked from the bus reading at boot.

Today: BoardPins.h names LPG0; nothing reads the daughterboard.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed 1f39759: flagship_p4/src/system/ValenceDbg.h, header-only. dbgBegin() claims G37 (output, low; the ROM boot log owns the pin until then). dbgLevel(bool) is one store to GPIO.out1_w1ts / out1_w1tc with a compile-time mask: write-one-to-change registers, so no read-modify-write and no lock; any task, either core, or an ISR. dbgPulse(n) is 2n back-to-back stores. Called from nowhere; main.cpp includes the header so every build compiles it. DECISIONS (veto-able): (1) API is dbgBegin/dbgLevel/dbgPulse (the bead's set/clear are dbgLevel(true/false)); (2) always compiled, no Kconfig switch: unused inline functions emit no code, so "compiled into test images" costs nothing in production; (3) dbgBegin() is not called at boot, so G37 stays U0TX until a bench image claims it. title: Drive link: RS485 Modbus on G33/G32/G41 plus DRV_ALM (G31) and DRV_RDY (G28)
description:

P4 UART TX G33 (D), RX G32 (R), DE G41 (DE and /RE tied: HIGH = transmit), so the IDF UART RS485 half-duplex mode drives DE. ZO (encoder index) is NOT brought out: absolute position comes over Modbus. All five are provisional pins (Hardware hw-kzr). The drive's logic is powered from the motor bus, so nothing answers until motor power is on.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02, f45485e: the press/hold core and the board host landed; the BINDING is held on this flag.
Landed: ButtonGesture.h (hardware-free; suite test_button_gesture 9 cases / 84 assertions; the PAIR button reuses it): 30 ms stable-time debounce, gesture only on the debounced RELEASE (a hold never also fires press), press < 3 s <= hold < 30 s <= stuck, not armed until seen released (held through power-on fires nothing), wrap-safe. ValenceButtons.cpp: G49 polled every 10 ms on the BoardIo task (no GPIO ISR), each gesture a Warn log line ("HOME press at the board"; reaches 0x0008 through the log bridge), parked in one atomic byte for the hub task: homeButtonTake(). Nothing acts on it; TODO(val-091.26) in ValenceButtons.h.

CANON FLAG -- the bead binds press to the home intent path and hold to the admin reset path; on this board neither path can carry it.
Source A: bd val-091.26 "home submitted as an intent through the MotionArbiter (sole-caller rule), the reset through the same path an admin reset takes."
Source B: flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceDevice.cpp applyHome, case 1: "home op 1 refused: no drive and no encoder on this board, nothing to home against -- use force_home (op 2)" -> UNSUPPORTED_OP; and no reboot or reset op exists in ValenceCatalog.h or the firmware (the only esp_restart is OTA's rebootTask).
My read: a press should go through the delegate's applyHome op 1 exactly as the wire's does (refused, logged, today; real once sensorless homing lands); force_home (RFC-025 HAZARD, asserts an unmeasured stroke) must never sit behind a button. "Reset" is undefined: a reboot (Hardware SPEC: "two buttons, no reset button", so a hold standing in for one), the SPEC 11.2 release of a held e-stop into PAUSE, or a motor-switch fault clear are three different things with different gates.
Your call: what does a HOME hold do -- (a) reboot through a graceful path (GOODBYE REBOOTING to sessions, only at rest with no source owning the rail), (b) the 11.2 release, or (c) something else -- and may a press stay a refused op 1 until homing exists?
The binding itself lands in ValenceDevice::tick() (take the gesture, run it through the same gates a wire intent meets); that file belonged to another agent this session, so it was not touched.

title: Status LED: Flux glue for the XL-3528RGBW on G26 (GRBW, 32 bits per pixel), NEOPIXEL OUT on the same chain
description:
Board fact (Hardware flagship/SPEC.md 2026-09-23 status-LED row, 2026-09-25 XL-3528RGBW row, 2026-09-26 D5 decoupling row, 2026-09-23 accessory row): LED_DATA on G26 (USB1.1 D-, free while OTG is off) -> 74AHCT125 gate 3 (U10, 5 V) -> R607 100 R -> D5 DIN; R601 10k holds the line low while the P4 boots. D5 is an XINGLIGHT XL-3528RGBW-2812B: GRBW, 4 bytes per pixel, not 3. Its DOUT continues to the NEOPIXEL OUT header (J12, 5 V through F1003 1 A), so user strips chain after the status pixel.

Today: BoardPins.h names the pin; lib/flux has no IDF glue (logging-leds.md: no LED was fitted).

Owed: one board glue file driving RMT at WS2812 timing in GRBW order, the two-axis grammar of logging-leds.md, the liveness gate, and a decision on how the chained user strip is addressed (pixel 0 is the status LED). The board monitor's own 10-LED bank (U12 PC6) belongs to the monitor firmware, not this.
close_reason: Landed f45485e (host-verified; bench owed val-091.66)

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Landed f45485e. ValenceGlow.cpp is the board's one Flux glue: RMT TX on G26, 10 MHz, one GRBW frame (32 bits) every 20 ms, gray moved to the W die, brightness ceiling 96/255 before gamma; StatusLook.h maps facts -> machine state -> Flux (System, Status) pair in one editable table; the engine is pumped only by the BoardIo task (core 0, prio 3); the boot rainbow ends on app_main's self-check verdict (glowSetSelfCheck); liveness gate = the hub's tick counter via hubCensus() every 250 ms, registered once the hub ticks. Suite test_status_look 5 cases / 38 assertions. DECISIONS (veto-able): (1) the table names Flux PAIRS, not colors, because logging-leds.md makes color/effect fleet-wide; rows: boot rainbow, idle (unhomed) Motion/Latched solid amber, homed all-Nominal green breathe, running Motion/Working, paused Motion/Degraded slow amber blink, estop Safety/Urgent, fault (self-check held power off OR switch faulted) Safety/Latched solid red, flashing (OTA) Flash/Working; precedence boot > estop > flashing > fault > paused > running > homed > idle. (2) Chained J12 strip: pixel 0 only, the chain is never written and stays dark until a channel owns it (user strips are usually 24-bit RGB, so a future owner must declare the downstream pixel width). (3) Bit timing 0.3/0.9 and 0.9/0.3 us (IDF's WS2812 values), not yet checked against the XL-3528RGBW-2812B datasheet. (4) Every frame is sent even when unchanged, so a transient-corrupted pixel repaints within 20 ms. (5) No motion-task heartbeat: the census has no tick counter; the hub's is the gate. (6) hubCensus() is heavier than needed for a tick (it walks sessions, the stack mark and two client lists); a hubTicks() accessor in ValenceHub.cpp would be leaner, not done this session because hub files were another agent's. C-3: logging-leds.md and flux.h no longer say Flux has no IDF glue. title: Fan and thermistor: FAN_PWM on G27, FAN_TACH on G38, THERM on G16
description:
Board fact (Hardware flagship/SPEC.md 2026-09-23 fan row and fan-filter row, 2026-09-22 sensing row, 2026-09-24 J6 row): FAN_PWM on G27 drives a high-side P-FET (Q702 via Q701; R701 100k pull-down = fan off by default), P4 HIGH = fan on, no inversion. The output is LC-filtered to DC (100 uH + 22 uF, damped), a controller-less buck at ~50 kHz, so firmware closes the loop on the tach. FAN_TACH on G38 (10k pull-up, 1k series; G38 is sampled only in download mode) is valid at every speed because the fan's ground stays solid. THERM on G16 (ADC1, 1k series + 100 nF, 10k pull-up) takes any 10k NTC on J7. Fan rail 5 V by default, 12 V by jumper JP2. G16 is a provisional pin (Hardware hw-kzr).

Today: BoardPins.h names all three; nothing drives or reads them.

Owed: LEDC PWM at ~50 kHz, PCNT on the tach, ADC1 oneshot on THERM, a fan policy keyed on THERM and the regen telemetry, and their channel on the wire.
close_reason: Landed f45485e (host-verified; wire channel val-091.65; bench owed val-091.66)

comments.text: Landed f45485e. Thermal.h (hardware-free, suite test_thermal 11 cases / 52 assertions): 10k B3950 table in ln(R) with kOffsetC as the calibration knob, NaN outside the table (open/shorted J7); fan curve 40 C 30 % -> 50 C 55 % -> 60 C 100 %, hysteresis on >= 40 C / off < 35 C; FanPolicy: 2 s full-duty kick on every start (its end RPM = learned top speed, raised whenever a higher reading appears), integral loop on tach RPM (gain 0.3 per 1 s step, duty floor 20 %), stall after 5 s with no pulses -> re-kick, tach sticky per boot, no-tach fan -> open-loop duty, no usable THERM -> 50 %, no sample yet -> off. ValenceFan.cpp: LEDC LS timer 0/ch 0, 50 kHz, 10-bit on G27 (USB D+ pad pull-up disabled); PCNT on G38, falling edges, 1 us glitch filter, read+cleared each step, 2 pulses/rev; no ISR. THERM: the motor switch task samples G16 once a second (ADC1 has ONE reader: a second task's try-lock collision makes the EN-node read NaN and cuts motor power) and hands volts over via motorSwitchThermVolts(). WIRE: no catalog channel exists for a board temperature or a fan -> TODO(val-091.65) in ValenceFan.h, bead val-091.65 filed (etag cascade is a separate step); the 5 s console line carries therm/duty/RPM. title: Regen clamp telemetry: CLAMP_MON on-time capture and SHUNT_TEMP, dissipation published over Valence
description:
Board fact (Hardware flagship/SPEC.md 2026-09-22 regen-clamp-revised row, 2026-09-24 PWR263S row, 2026-09-25 monitor ADC row): the self-acting regen clamp (U3 TLV1805 driving Q501, ON 44.5 V / OFF 43.2 V, trimmed down by the board monitor's CLAMP_TRIM) exposes its gate through the 10k + 3.3k CLAMP_MON divider to G17 (an ADC1 pad, C504 1 nF at the P4), meant as a capture pin for on-time counting: power = duty x V^2 / 7.5 R (two Bourns PWR263S 15 R in parallel), published over Valence. SHUNT_TEMP is TH501 (10k NTC, B 3435, beside the regen resistors) on G18 (ADC1, 10k pull-up R512, C503 100 nF). Both also reach the board monitor (U12). G17/G18 are provisional pins (Hardware hw-kzr).

Today: BoardPins.h names both pins; no firmware reads either.

title: Board: trust ledger is not persisted and a factory-fresh hub does not boot claimable (SPEC §12.3)
description: Found 2026-10-01 while splitting val-sf7.5. SPEC §12.3 (pinned b0a412e): 'Tokens survive hub reboots and firmware updates', and under (c) 'Factory-fresh (zero configure tokens exist): no gesture is needed. The hub boots claimable and the first knock gets configure.' Static evidence: grep for pairing(), PairingManager and openPresenceWindow across flagship_p4/src finds no call; Hub::pairing() is the documented 'NVS persistence adapter' seam (lib/valence hub.hpp) and nothing uses it. So every reboot drops every paired token, and a fresh board never opens the presence window, leaving no association mode that reaches configure without a configure session already present. The two halves are ordered: boot-claimable without a persisted ledger would make every reboot claimable by the first knock, so persistence lands first. Not verified on hardware; the claim is from source. The sim twin follows (val-sf7.6).
close_reason: Landed b09ee3f (host-verified 2026-10-02: pio test -e native exit 0 all suites, test_trust_store 12/12 run directly; pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS against Valence HEAD 83371ce, no API used here changed since the 3b8d6c8 pin). SPEC 12.3: ledger is NVS blob 'trust' in namespace 'valence' (<= trust_ledger_max_bytes, full 8-entry ledger at every cap fits, TS-08), loaded on app_main in hubBegin before the WS port starts, written on the hub task only when the encoded bytes change, at most once per 2 s, held while otaInFlight(). Factory-fresh (zero configure tokens, no rejected ledger) opens the presence window at boot: first knock gets configure. Gesture counter 'pgest' (1 B): 3 consecutive short power-on boots arm the window on the 4th; written at boot on app_main, cleared on the hub task at 10 s uptime. VETO-ABLE DECISIONS: (1) only ESP_RST_POWERON counts toward the gesture (a crash/WDT/software reset breaks the sequence, so a remote fault loop cannot open pairing); (2) a stored ledger that is unreadable or rejected boots UNclaimable with an empty ledger, the gesture is the way back; (3) claimable opens the window once per boot for pairing_window_default_s (120 s), not indefinitely while unclaimed; (4) a ledger holding only control/watch entries is still factory-fresh per 12.3's definition. COST: TrustStore 3,824 B in the PSRAM HubBox; decodeLedger stages 800 B (+100 B) on app_main's 6,144 B stack at boot, unmeasured. Bench stamp OWED (no board): power-cycle x3 opens the window; reboot keeps a paired token.

title: Relationship engine as hub policy: hardware-free core, event-driven, e-stop/STOP force declared safe values
description:
Relationship engine: hub policy that drives an accessory field from any machine field (position, speed, pattern state, anything in the catalog), evaluated on the hub so it survives Phosphor closing.

Shape (the pattern engine is the model: flagship_p4/src/patterns/PatternEngine.h):
- HARDWARE-FREE and liftable: inputs are field values handed in, outputs are accessory writes returned; no radio, no queue, no clock grabbed. Native suite + valencesim run it verbatim.
- EVENT-DRIVEN, never clocked: re-evaluate when a source field changes, rate-limited to the target accessory's declared update rate, so a 1 kHz source cannot flood ESP-NOW.
- SAFETY OVERRIDES POLICY: e-stop latched or STOP (RFC-074 semantics) forces every target to its declared deadman-safe value immediately and holds it until the latch clears AND the relationship is re-armed explicitly; nothing resumes by itself (hardware SPEC: "firmware must not resume motion by itself" applies in spirit to accessories).
- Relationships are hub-authored data (from Phosphor), persisted in the hub-authored blob beside the store; how they are exposed on the wire (a store per RFC-073, or intents) rides the Valence RFC ritual.
- Runs on the hub task (it reads catalog state the hub owns); its output goes to the spoke task by message.

Acceptance: native suite covers linear map, clamp to declared range, rate limit, e-stop force-safe, STOP force-safe, re-arm required; bench shows the stand-in pump PWM tracking machine position.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp running the motion path motorless + stand-in accessory driving an LED PWM + analyzer): relationship pump_duty = f(position); run a pattern; capture LED duty vs census position; press e-stop mid-stroke and measure e-stop -> LED at safe value.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- native <suite> exit 0; duty-vs-position lag p50/max ms; e-stop -> safe max ms n=20]
acceptance_criteria: Native suite (map, clamp, rate limit, e-stop/STOP force-safe, explicit re-arm) exits 0; bench duty tracks position; e-stop -> safe measured.
notes: RFC-089 (Valence 44c52b8, SPEC 8.7): the relationships writer 0x0015 tags its slot, name and item fields store.slot/store.name/store.item and enforces the per-verb set; a save without store.item is INVALID_VALUE (no live state). The preset writer's implementation is the model: ValenceDevice::applyPresets (24cc412, val-9s6).

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RFC-078 (rfc-j5f) ACCEPTED 2026-10-01 (comment 01:32) with the map table: relationship_maps 1 linear_clamp, 2 invert, 3 threshold_hysteresis, 4 slew_limit, 5 lowpass, 6 gate (output only while the source is inside a range, else safe), 7 piecewise_table, parameters in physical units. Under RFC-085 there is no STOP or HOLD: PAUSE disarms relationships and forces targets to their commanded safe values; ESTOP forces safe; reboot and ESTOP release re-arm nothing. Direct client writes under pause are the operator's act, allowed. Stream stamps applied on arrival with relative offsets, no spoke time sync. Relationships are authored through RFC-067 store verbs (a relationships STORE with action.store, store_id per RFC-070); relationship-admin is dropped. Chains allowed; feedback loops rejected at put. A bound target is owned by its relationship (SOURCE_CONFLICT). Native suite must cover all seven maps, loop rejection at put, pause disarm.

title: Config mode: boot with PAIR held -> BLE-only, no WiFi, setup category (blocked on the Valence config-mode RFC and RFC-069)
description:
Config mode: boot with PAIR held -> pairing window open, BLE advertising with the window flag, NO WiFi at all, no softAP ever (the ESP-NOW rule). Configuration over BLE; the session lands at configure tier; the catalog exposes a setup category (WiFi credentials as an admin INTENT per RFC-069, machine name, accessory pairing); Phosphor lists it like any hub and renders the category generically (wizard pattern RENDERING section 10 is polish, not a prerequisite).

BLOCKED UPSTREAM on the Valence RFC to be drafted as "Config mode: a BLE-only provisioning session with a setup category" (not in RFC-QUEUE.md as of 2026-09-26), and on RFC-069 (DRAFT, ruling rfc-qf5) with its companion RFC-054 (PROPOSED).
Prerequisite inside Nucleus: a BLE transport port for the Valence hub (NimBLE host on the P4, controller on the C6, per V3). Nucleus has none; transport.md already names it ("BLE later means a NimBLE host on the P4 with the controller on the C6"). Its callbacks run on the NimBLE host task: enqueue, never mutate hub state (T5); session teardown through the one funnel (T3).
Boot path: PAIR sampled once, early in app_main, before wifi_up(); config mode skips esp_wifi_start entirely. G52 is not a strap pin (hardware SPEC 2026-09-23), so the hold reaches firmware.

Acceptance: a factory-fresh board (NVS erased) booted with PAIR held appears over BLE, a client writes WiFi credentials, the next normal boot joins the AP; a normal boot never advertises the config-mode flag.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp + C6 on the V3-proven image + button on a free GPIO + phone/PC BLE client): erase NVS (esptool erase_region 0x9000 0x6000), boot with the button held, scan (nRF Connect: name + window flag), connect, run the setup category through valence_probe's BLE path or Phosphor, reboot normally, read the IP from the boot log; repeat 5 times; then 5 normal boots confirming no config flag and no BLE advertising of it.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- COM15, 5/5 provisioned-and-joined, 0/5 flag on normal boot, BLE internal heap cost N B, RFC-<nnn> at valence.pin <sha>]
acceptance_criteria: Factory-fresh board provisioned over BLE 5/5 and joins the AP on the next boot; normal boots never show the config flag.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: UNBLOCKED by rulings 2026-10-01: RFC-079 (rfc-ewm) ACCEPTED with ui category 15 setup; config mode activates BLE advertising AND the USB serial binding together, both accept RFC-069 wifi_join (val-9u0.17). Configure goes to the first knock in config mode; the advertisement bit is enough. Accessory pairing waits until WiFi is joined. Category 15 is the commissioning surface (network, name, pairing, AND geometry and ceilings: val-091.51). RFC-054 is OBSOLETE: no hub-discloses-credentials path. BLE advertisement layout per RFC-072 (val-9u0.18). The title's 'BLE-only' now reads 'BLE + USB serial, no WiFi'.

title: Pairing window on the hub PAIR button (RFC-027 lineage; BTN_PAIR G52 provisional, pin from the board header)
description:
Pairing window on the hub's PAIR button, RFC-027 lineage (push-to-pair: presence at the device is the proof). Hold PAIR at runtime -> window opens; the beacon's pairing-window bit goes up; an Isotope in pairing state broadcasts a join request; the hub accepts during the window only.

- GPIO: SW2 PAIR = BTN_PAIR on G52 per hardware/flagship/SPEC.md (2026-09-23 P4 pin map; the map is "provisional, swap at layout"), internal pull-up, active low. Pin injected from the one board config header (architecture.md, pin allocation), never inside a class. On the dev board: any free HP GPIO with a button to GND.
- Window length: 120 s, the RFC-027 push-to-pair window the archived S3 used (veto-able). A second hold closes it early.
- Debounce and hold detection in a hardware-free core (host-testable); the GPIO read is glue.
- LED: Session/Ceremony per the two-axis grammar (logging-leds.md) for the whole window, so the gone-if-missed ceremony is never masked (T15).
- Advertised to Valence clients too (WELCOME pairing_modes is re-evaluated per session, RFC-027), so Phosphor can show "pairing open".
- NOT the power-on hold: that is config mode (its own bead). hardware SPEC.md still says "held at power-on = AP config mode"; that contradicts the no-softAP ruling and is the hardware repo's row to fix.

Acceptance: hold >= 2 s opens, 120 s closes, second hold closes early, LED and beacon bit follow; native test of the hold/debounce core exits 0.
BENCH VALIDATION PLAN (P4 stamp, a button on a free GPIO, V4 stand-in accessory reading the beacon bit): 10 holds, 10 taps (must NOT open), 10 early closes; analyzer on the button line and the stand-in's WINDOW pin.
Stamp: [verified YYYY-MM-DD -- 10/10 open, 0/10 taps opened, 10/10 early close, window 120.0 s +/- 0.1, beacon bit latency max N ms]
acceptance_criteria: Hold opens a 120 s window, taps do not, second hold closes early; LED Ceremony and beacon bit follow; native test of the hold core exits 0.

comments.text: Rulings 2026-10-01: RFC-079 (rfc-ewm, open question 2): accessory pairing waits until the hub has joined WiFi (the spoke follows the AP's channel; config mode has none), so the PAIR window is refused or deferred in config mode. RFC-076 (rfc-7bq): one join per window; a configure session may open the window in-band (an INTENT beside the button). Config mode itself remains the power-on hold (val-9u0.14).

title: STOP does not deactivate a live Stream source: the next 0x2100/0x2101 sample replans past the brake
description: Found while landing val-cu2. SPEC 11.1 STOP: decelerate to zero, SOURCE DEACTIVATED, clears by any new accepted motion intent. The 0x0005 stop op now halts the generator (Pattern gate) and brakes the plan in flight, but onStreamBundle never consults the hub's STOP latch, and the hub's own STOP-clear lives in handleIntent, which stream bundles do not pass through. So a client still streaming samples replans the machine on the next bundle after the brake. Needs a ruling: does a stream sample count as 'a new accepted motion intent' that clears STOP (then this is correct as-is and the spec should say so), or must the stream re-acquire the source first? Either way the answer lives upstream in Valence SPEC 11.1 before code here.
close_reason: Stream samples are refused while the hub's 0x0003 STOP latch holds: ValenceDevice::onStreamBundle drops the whole bundle and counts it in kinetic-diag sync_dropped (never NACKed, SPEC 9.2); MotionArbiter::stop() closes a Stream gate before the brake request so samples queued before the STOP are refused at accept(). The latch clears only on an accepted source-mapped intent (0x3100 move, pattern_cmd); the next bundle reopens the gate. Stream re-arm by PUBLISH proposed upstream as RFC-074 (Valence rfc-2ly, fab628f), not coded. Commit fefadf4. [verified 2026-09-25 -- pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS; test_motion_arbiter 11/11, test_pattern_engine 9/9 (binaries run directly, exit 0); live vs valencesim 9082: 1 Hz sine stream, STOP mid-stream, 87/87 samples sent under STOP refused and counted, position range 0.000 mm over 2 s, 0x0003 STOP set, 0x3100 move cleared STOP and the stream resumed; node test/valence-sim.mjs --estop 54/0; valence-modes 8/8; canon_lint only the standing valence.pin finding]

title: 0x0005 stop does not stop the pattern generator (delegate answers UNSUPPORTED_OP)
description: ValenceDevice::applyIntent NACKs every 0x0005 op the hub does not handle itself (stop/hold/pause/...) with UNSUPPORTED_OP. With the pattern generator landed (val-091.12) and source.background_run able to keep it running unattended, RENDERING.md §10.1 and the catalog's background_run desc say it is 'stoppable via Stop/E-Stop'; today only E-STOP stops it (onEstop drops running). Needed: decide the stop op's hub-side latch semantics (SPEC §11.2) and have it clear PatternSettings::running plus brake the in-flight stroke.
