E-stop closes the same gate; only a pattern_cmd start reopens it. Stream deactivation under STOP split out as val-2w2. title: Power-monitor driver: support both INA228 and INA237 (DEVICE_ID at boot)
description: Hardware ruling 2026-09-24 (Hardware flagship/SPEC.md): U11 may be an INA237AIDGSR or an INA228AIDGSR, same VSSOP-10 pinout, same I2C address pins and ALERT wiring. The INA228 is out of stock everywhere (DigiKey restock 2026-11-11), so first boards carry the INA237. Firmware must read DEVICE_ID at boot and pick the register layout: INA228 is 20-bit (CURRENT/VBUS/VSHUNT 24-bit registers, ENERGY and CHARGE accumulators); INA237 is 16-bit (16-bit registers, no ENERGY/CHARGE, so integrate power in firmware). SHUNT_CAL scaling differs between the two. The shunt over-limit ALERT (hardware motor cut via the TPS48111 EN wired-OR), the bus-overvoltage alert (~50 V) and the boot-time clamp-trim voltage read must work on both. Sensorless homing uses the current reading: 1.25 mA/LSB on the 1 mOhm shunt at +/-40.96 mV (INA237) is enough.
acceptance_criteria: Boot log names the detected part; current, bus voltage, power and the ALERT trip verified on a board with each part (or on the INA237 board plus a register-level unit test for INA228).
notes:
2026-10-09 triage: code done (INA228/INA237 by register probe, PowerMonitor.h). NEEDS THE OPERATOR: the SOVL trip level (TODO(val-091.22) in ValencePower.cpp, 15.0 A today); then the bench acceptance on an INA237 board (rides val-091.66).

PowerMonitor.h (identify by MANUFACTURER_ID + DEVICE_ID + the CONFIG bit 5 probe, 20-bit vs 16-bit decode, SOVL/BOVL) and ValencePower.cpp are on main; test_power_monitor 12 cases / 98 assertions exit 0. The SOVL TODO is replaced by the 2026-10-09 ruling (36889b0 on feat/overnight-batch) and docs/board-map.md's owed column keeps only the bench. comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Driver landed host-verified, bench OWED (no Flagship PCB exists yet; the bare stamp has no U11). flagship_p4/src/system/PowerMonitor.h = hardware-free register layer (identify, SHUNT_CAL, 20-bit vs 16-bit decode, SOVL/BOVL encode); ValencePower.{h,cpp} = IDF i2c_master glue on SDA G34 / SCL G36 @ 0x40, called from app_main before motion; boot log names the part (GLOGI tag power). DATASHEET FINDING: the INA237 datasheet (SBOSA20A, rev May 2022) documents NO DEVICE_ID register at 0x3F, only MANUFACTURER_ID 0x5449. So DEVICE_ID alone cannot select the part: the driver reads 0x3F and cross-checks it against a documented probe (CONFIG bit 5 TEMPCOMP is R/W on the INA228, reserved/reads 0 on the INA237); an unrecognized id with a dead bit 5 is treated as INA237, contradictions are refused. Both parts run ADCRANGE=1 (+/-40.96 mV): INA228 78.125 uA/LSB, INA237 1.25 mA/LSB, SHUNT_CAL=4096 on both; SOVL/BOVL/DIAG_ALRT layouts and LSBs are identical on both parts. ALERT is LATCHED (a transparent alert would re-close the motor switch on the next conversion after the cut); powerTakeAlerts() reads DIAG_ALRT to re-arm. RULING OWED: SOVL trip level, set to 15.0 A (= the TPS48111's own 15.2 A over-current level, so the INA adds a one-conversion detector rather than a lower limit); BOVL 50 V per this bead. NOT DONE: firmware energy integration on the INA237 -- nothing consumes energy/charge today and the INA228 accumulators are not read either, so both parts expose the same V/I/P/die-temp surface; add when a consumer exists. Catalog has_current_sensor/has_power_monitor wiring and the power channel publisher are not touched. [verified 2026-10-01 -- native test_power_monitor 8 cases / 44 assertions exit 0 (all 7 native suites exit 0); pio run -d flagship_p4 SUCCESS, ValencePower.cpp compiled clean; canon_lint 1 finding = pre-existing valence.pin mismatch (sibling Valence HEAD moved), none from these files] Bench stamp owed per acceptance: boot log + V/I/P + ALERT trip on an INA237 board, INA228 when one exists.

comments.text: 2026-10-02, d562f0e: the probe and its failure path are documented in docs/board-map.md (new U11 identification row) as the hw-8zu answer on the firmware side. Probe: MANUFACTURER_ID (0x3E) must read 0x5449; DEVICE_ID (0x3F) is read but never decides alone; CONFIG is reset, TEMPCOMP (bit 5) written 1 and read back: it sticks on the INA228 (R/W), reads 0 on the INA237 (reserved). id 0x228x + sticks = INA228; id 0x237x + dead = INA237; unknown id + dead = INA237; contradiction, non-TI id or an I2C error = none (ina2xx::identify, suite test_power_monitor, 9 decision checks). No code change was needed. title: P4 programs the CH32V003 monitor over SWIO; image ships inside the Nucleus OTA
description:
Why: the Flagship wires P4 G50 to the CH32V003's SWIO pin (PD1) so no external programmer is ever needed; boards flash their monitor on first power-up and the monitor updates with every OTA (SPEC board-monitor ruling). A WCH-LinkE on the rescue pads stays possible.

What: an SWIO driver on the P4 (RMT, or a bit-bang with interrupts masked per transaction; ch32v003fun's minichlink documents the protocol and has ESP32-S2 and RP2040-PIO programmers as prior art). At boot, read the monitor's version register over I2C; if there is no reply (blank chip) or the version is older than the embedded image, halt it over SWIO, erase, program, verify, reset. The monitor image is built from the Nucleus monitor target and embedded in the P4 app.
acceptance_criteria: A blank CH32V003 on a fresh board is programmed by the P4 at first boot and answers its version register; an OTA carrying a newer monitor image updates it; a corrupted monitor flash is recovered by the P4 alone.
notes: 2026-10-01: contract only, docs/supervisor.md section 6 (wiring G50 -> 100R -> PD1 with 10k pull-up, protocol per minichlink, programming sequence, image embedded in the P4 build, boot check = exact CRC-32 match of the 16 KB code flash via IDENT, sv_needs_flash in Supervisor.h, covered by test_supervisor). No SWIO driver: pins are firm, bit timing is not set by SPEC; needs a scope session on the bench first. Open: IWDG behavior during a debug halt; embed mechanism (pre-build step vs CMake).

title: Board monitor firmware for the Flagship's CH32V003 supervisor
description:
Why: the OSSM Flagship adds a WCH CH32V003F4U6 as a board monitor (Hardware repo flagship/SPEC.md, 2026-09-23 board-monitor ruling) so the P4 does not poll rails. It watches VIN_RAW, +12V, +5V, the accessory rail, +5V_SYS, MOTOR_V+, CLAMP_MON and SHUNT_TEMP on its eight ADC channels, and owns two safety-direction outputs.

What: firmware in the Nucleus repo (own target, same RISC-V family; ch32v003fun is the reference SDK). ~1 kHz scan, window compare with debounce, VDD-tolerance correction via the internal 1.2 V reference. FAULT_N (open-drain onto the motor-switch EN wired-OR) is pulled on motion-critical faults: 12 V out of window, input stage fault (VIN_RAW present, bus absent), MOTOR_V+ present while the switch is commanded off. Accessory rails only raise a warning. CLAMP_TRIM PWM (~20 kHz) sets the regen threshold: at power-up with MOTOR_V+ ~0 and VIN_RAW stable, trim to VIN_RAW + 3 V (LTC fitted) or + 1.2 V (budget link), never above the 44.6 V ceiling; release to duty 0 whenever the clamp conducts while the bus is not above VIN_RAW (the supply is feeding the bank) or SHUNT_TEMP is high. Boot clamp test on request: pull the threshold below the bus for a ~30-50 ms pulse, confirm CLAMP_MON conduction. I2C register map: version, status, per-channel readings, fault code (latched), trim setpoint, command register.
acceptance_criteria: Registers readable from the P4; each fault class demonstrated on the bench by forcing it (pull a rail, hold MOTOR_V+ with the switch off, clamp-at-idle); trim measured with a scope at 24 V and 36 V supplies against the SPEC thresholds; FAULT_N cuts the motor switch.
notes: 2026-10-01: contract docs/supervisor.md; message set flagship_p4/src/system/Supervisor.h (shared C/C++); firmware flagship_ch32v003/ (monitor_core.c hardware-free, main.c ch32v003fun glue). [verified 2026-10-01 -- pio test -e native -f native/test_supervisor exit 0; program.exe 16 cases / 326 assertions] [verified 2026-10-01 -- monitor_core.c compiles clean as C99 -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion on host and with riscv32-esp-elf-gcc -march=rv32ec_zicsr -mabi=ilp32e -c: 2390 B text, needs __mulsi3/__udivsi3/memcpy/memset]. NOT BUILT: main.c and the image; no ch32v003fun, no platform-ch32v, no riscv-none-elf toolchain on this host (the ESP riscv32 gcc has no ilp32e multilib, so it cannot link). Description drift vs Hardware SPEC: the monitor no longer reads MOTOR_V+ (SPEC L92, channel is +BUS), so the 'MOTOR_V+ present while switch off' fault is not implementable here (Hardware hw-c7j); duty-0 ceiling is 44.5 V in SPEC L89, 44.62 V from the nominal parts (bead said 44.6). Rulings owed: docs/supervisor.md section 8 (thresholds, heartbeat, I2C 0x2C, budget detection, clamp test energy, exact-match version rule, shared INA bus) and the CANON FLAG on the MON_LED bank vs the Flux grammar. Hardware beads filed: hw-cjn (P1, stuck-on clamp has no actuator), hw-c7j.

title: Quadrature jitter with the accessory GPIO hammered (LP pads driven by HP peripherals)
description:
Why: the OSSM Flagship routes optional accessory I/O (2 pump PWMs, AUX buttons, a Qwiic I2C bus, UART + 6 GPIOs on a header) onto the spare LP pads LPG0-15, driven by HP peripherals through the GPIO matrix (Hardware repo flagship/SPEC.md, 2026-09-23 accessory ruling). Architecturally this is free: per-pad LP/HP select is set once at boot, lp_quad.c only issues atomic out_w1ts/w1tc stores for its own two bits, and HP matrix peripherals generate no LP-bus traffic. That is reasoning, not measurement. Accessories are optional, so a failure here only restricts them; quadrature stays sacred.

What: rerun the lp_scope capture (tools/lp_scope.py, the 1,078-edge baseline of val-091.4 / sd-1bi.3: spread one scope sample, late=0, 0 illegal) while hammering the LP pads from the HP side: LEDC PWM on two pads at ~20-25 kHz, HP I2C polling on LPG9/LPG11 at 400 kHz, RMT WS2812 data streaming, HP UART TX/RX on LPG14/15, GPIO toggling on the rest.

Firmware rule this test protects: only HP peripherals (UART1-4, HP I2C, LEDC, RMT, PCNT, plain GPIO) on the accessory pads, never the LP UART or LP I2C, because those put HP register traffic on the LP bus the emitter's store loop uses.
acceptance_criteria: Scope capture with all accessory pads active matches the val-091.4 baseline: 0 illegal transitions, late=0, edge spread within one scope sample at the same timebase. Result stamped on this bead; a regression names the pad/peripheral that caused it.

title: Kinetic chase aim over-predicts on a clean link: rendered position leads the asked position 30-70 ms and overshoots amplitude 16-18 percent
description: Measured 2026-09-21 with tools/lag_probe.py on Nucleus 57eb828 after WIFI_PS_NONE: window 0..50 raw->pos -69.7 ms ratio 1.178; window 0..500 raw->pos -31.1 ms ratio 1.164 (asked +-175 mm, rendered +-203 mm). Before the power-save fix, with clumpy arrivals, the same instrument read +13 ms / ratio 1.06 (0..50) and +2.5 ms / 1.065 (0..500). Cause hypothesis: Kinetic Config chase_lookahead = 3.0 intervals with chase_aim_accel_extrap on, tuned on the S3 bench where arrival jitter and hub latency were larger; on the P4 with 35 ms clean cadence the extrapolation runs ahead of the source. Options: (a) drop lookahead toward 1 interval and re-sweep on this hub; (b) tie lookahead to the measured arrival gap / RFC-059 schedule latency so it self-scales; (c) expose kinetic-set (0x3120) so the sweep can run without reflashing. A client asking for +-175 mm and getting +-203 mm is an amplitude-fidelity defect, not just feel; the window clamp catches it only at the rail.
close_reason: fixed in the kinetic commit; lag_probe bare points -2.2/-3.0/+1.9 ms, amplitude 1.001/1.001/0.998 on 0..50/0..150/0..500 [verified 2026-09-21]

title: Rebrand rulings and rename inventory (slop-* -> Valence family)
description: Operator rulings, 2026-09-20/21. RULED: SlopDrive/SlopDrive-32 -> Valence Drive (short Vdrive; old repo archived as the S3-era reference, not renamed in place). SlopSync -> Valence (repo, slopsync:: namespace, JS package, MFP plugin SlopSync.dll, slopsync.pin, probe/lint tools, test dirs, canon skill). slopmotion/slopglow/sloplog -> vmotion/vglow/vlog (done in ValenceDrive). PCB -> OSSM Flagship. Board prefix sd- -> val- (done). SlopDeck -> Phosphor (full name Valence Phosphor; users say Valence and Phosphor as separate things; runner-up was Ember). Naming pattern for the rest: brand + kind, so SlopBench -> Valence Bench, SlopSim -> Valence Sim, slopsync_probe -> Valence Probe, SlopSoak -> Valence Soak. WIRE-VISIBLE strings ride ONE atomic RFC in SlopSync before any tag (T11; pre-release wire strings ARE respelled per the 2026-07-27 C-11 ruling): ws_subprotocol slopsync.v1, endpoint /slopsync, hub identity string slopdrive-32, docs-site URL; fixtures, goldens and etags regenerated, then a pin bump. title: Port the pattern engine to the P4 (unblocks DeviceFeatures::has_pattern)
description: val-091.11 added DeviceFeatures::has_pattern and left it false: no pattern generator is ported to this repo, so every pattern-* channel (0x1200, 0x1210-0x1216, 0x1220, 0x3200, 0x3210, 0x3220) and the 0x5220 preset store stay out of the catalog. A hub with no generator advertising pattern-state would publish a permanently stopped generator, which is the dead-gauge lie the feature flags exist to prevent. Porting means StrokeEnginePatterns plus AdvancedPattern plus PatternPresetStore from SlopDrive-32, their own task, and the delegate cases behind the flag. (3) The probe now reports 13 failures where val-091.3 saw 12; the new one is safety_modes and it appeared after val-091.4. notes:

======================================================================
ITEM 1 -- BOTH STACKS RAISED ON THE MEASUREMENT, BOTH RE-MEASURED

The size had TWO homes before this (the xTaskCreatePinnedToCore literal and
main.cpp high-water watch table), which is the T20 shape: the reported total

ITEM 2 -- THE BENCH LEFTOVER IS RESET AND THE RESET PERSISTED

DEFAULT IS 50.0 mm/s (DEFAULT_USER_MAX_SPEED_MM_S, valence_config.h:34), the
number the catalog mirrors.

SlopSync/tools/slopsync_probe.py own encoders (T20: never a second hand-written

SPEC 8.4 gates retained STATE and every INTENT until it does, which is why a

  over the wire, fresh session: WELCOME cfg_gen=16, 0x1000 user_speed 50.0

The machine is left at the default. The val-091.9 leftover is gone.

======================================================================
ITEM 3 -- safety_modes: THE PROBE IS WRONG, NOT THE HUB. AND THE PREMISE WAS
WRONG TOO.

EXACT FAILURE TEXT
  == Step 5.9: safety ops -- override/bypass on 0x0005 (RFC-025c) ==
    x override_on NACKed: UNSUPPORTED_OP
  ...
    x  safety_modes           FAIL
  28 passed, 13 failed, 5 skipped

IT DID NOT APPEAR AFTER val-091.4. It is the --no-motion FLAG, and both results
were reproduced on ONE image, back to back, before any change this session:
  slopsync_probe.py --ip 192.168.1.118 --port 82 --no-motion  ->  27/12/7,
      safety_modes SKIP  (byte-identical to the val-091.3 recorded result)
  slopsync_probe.py --ip 192.168.1.118 --port 82              ->  28/13/5,
      safety_modes FAIL
slopsync_probe.py:2394 reads "if skip_intent:" where skip_intent =
args.no_motion or args.listen_only (:1529), so with --no-motion step 5.9 never
runs at all. The val-091.3 12 was a --no-motion run and the val-091.9 13 was a
full one; nothing regressed between them. Re-ran the full probe after this
session flash: still 28/13/5, unchanged.

THE HUB IS RIGHT, AND SPEC SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS.
  SPEC.md 11.1 (line 914): "a hub whose application does not implement a level
  MUST NACK UNSUPPORTED_OP and latch nothing. That is discoverable and honest
  -- without it, a generic client could not know whether sending HOLD to an
  arbitrary hub did anything at all."
  registry.yaml:609, 0x0303 UNSUPPORTED_OP: "intent op not implemented on this
  hub".
The ValenceHub.cpp delegate returns exactly that for every 0x0005 op it does
not implement, and the hub latches nothing. There is no drive on this board, so
there is no manual override to engage; latching a mode bit that gates nothing
would be the dead-gauge lie SPEC 6.3 and the has_motion gate exist to forbid.
estop and estop_clear never reach the delegate -- the hub owns both -- so the
red button is unaffected.

THERE IS NO CATALOG-LEVEL WAY FOR THE PROBE TO KNOW, AND THAT IS ALSO BY
DESIGN. 0x0005 is a core channel and the catalog option_access list (key 17)
declares each op TIER, never its implementedness. The SPEC stated discovery
mechanism for an unimplemented op is the NACK itself. So the probe cannot gate
this step the way it gates power (0x1010) on catalog presence; it has to accept
UNSUPPORTED_OP as a conformant answer.

SECOND INSTANCE RECORDED ON val-b7r. NO HUB CHANGE. Same class as the twelve
motion/pattern failures -- the probe asserting a SlopDrive-32 capability on
every hub -- with the distinction that this one cannot be fixed by a catalog
check and needs an "UNSUPPORTED_OP is a PASS for a hub that does not implement
this op" arm instead.

title: Hub config durability and stack measurement: NVS-persist 0x1000 + cfg_gen, report task high-water marks
description: The two items val-091.3 left owed. (1) The 0x1000 machine-config and its cfg_gen are RAM-only, so every reboot silently reverts an operator's settings and restarts the generation at 1, which lets a client precondition CAS pass against config that already moved (SPEC 4.2). Persist both in NVS, loaded before the first retained 0x1000 push so adoption never transmits, written through on the hub task with a debounce so a slider drag does not wear flash. (2) The hub task's 8 KB stack is SIZED, NOT MEASURED. Report uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark for the hub task, the motion task and app_main, printing only tasks that went deeper than last reported (T21), and read it after a representative workload.

BOTH OWED ITEMS LANDED AND ARE PROVEN ON HARDWARE. Image 0.1.0-p4hub, flashed
over COM15, build exit 0 (no clean build needed: no memory-map change).

FILES
  flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceHub.cpp  NVS persistence + hub task handle
  flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceHub.h    HubCensus::stackFree
  flagship_p4/src/main.cpp            the deeper-only stack reporter

======================================================================
ITEM 1 -- 0x1000 AND ITS cfg_gen NOW SURVIVE A REBOOT

SHAPE. One NVS blob, namespace "valence" (the one loadOrMintInstanceId
already opens; nvs_flash_init stays where it is, in main.cpp's wifi_up),
key "cfg": magic "VCFG" + version + cfg_gen + the eight floats, 40 B,
static_assert'd. An out-of-range or wrong-version blob is REJECTED WHOLE and
the factory defaults stand -- never clamped into shape, because clamping at
boot would be a machine-originated config change that SPEC 4.2 says must bump
cfg_gen, against the generation being restored in that same breath.

LOAD ORDER. The blob is read and adopted into the delegate BEFORE the Hub is
constructed, so the first retained 0x1000 push carries stored truth. Adoption
is a plain assignment (adoptConfig): no intent, no ECHO, no dirty flag, no
bump -- adoption never transmits.

cfg_gen RESTORE. The pinned library exposes advance-only
(Hub::bumpConfigGeneration, RFC-011) and no setter, and the sibling is
read-only from here, so the restore walks the u16 from its initial 1 up to the
stored value. It terminates by wrapping and costs one increment per step.

WRITE-THROUGH. Armed by the same branch that republishes 0x1000, re-armed by
every further change, fired 2,000 ms after the last one, on the HUB TASK
(T5: never in a transport callback). cfg_gen is read at write time, after
hub->update() has already applied that tick's bump.

title: Quadrature polarity: the +20 mm leg renders B leading A at the stated probe assignment
description:
Scope acceptance for val-091.4 measured the quadrature pair on LPG15/LPG12 with the probes as the operator stated them (CH2 = LPG15 = A, CH1 = LPG12 = B). On EVERY record the +20 mm leg renders B LEADING A, and the return-to-0 leg renders A leading B -- the opposite of the declared convention.

The firmware says the other thing in two places: flagship_p4/ulp/lp_quad.c builds g_seq as raise A, raise B, drop A, drop B (forward Gray walk 00 -> 01 -> 11 -> 10 over (B,A)), and flagship_p4/src/motion/ValenceMotion.cpp:96 writes ulp_g_dir = (v_mm_s < 0.0f) ? 0u : 1u, so a positive velocity walks that table forward and A must lead on a +X move.

Leg identity is not in doubt: the bursts sit at exactly the bench sequence's 2.5 s spacing and the 14.6 s cycle period, and the 1390 ms reversal-shaped burst anchors the phase (ValenceMotion.cpp benchTask).

So one of two things is true and NOTHING reachable over SCPI can tell them apart:
  (a) the two probes are on each other's through-hole (most likely -- costs nothing, and the acceptance numbers are unaffected), or
  (b) the emitted phase order is inverted against the declared convention, which would make a real drive in encoder-follow run backwards.

OPERATOR ACTION: eyeball which probe is on LPG15 and which on LPG12, or move one probe to a known pin and re-run tools/lp_leg_capture.py. If (a), nothing changes. If (b), the fix is in lp_quad.c's g_seq order or the dir sense, and every displacement number stays valid because they are magnitudes.

Does NOT block val-091.4: transition counts, illegal-transition counts, displacement magnitude, the velocity profile and the reversal legality are all polarity-independent.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-21 AS CASE (a): THE PROBES ARE ON EACH OTHER'S THROUGH-HOLE.
The firmware is correct and lp_quad.c was NOT changed.

THE TABLE WALK, BY HAND, BOTH DIRECTIONS AND ACROSS A FLIP.
g_seq is [0] set PIN_A, [1] set PIN_B, [2] clr PIN_A, [3] clr PIN_B, and the
per-edge advance is i += (fwd ? 1 : 3). From (B,A) = 00 with i = 0 the forward
walk is 00 -> 01 -> 11 -> 10 -> 00: raise A, raise B, drop A, drop B, which is
A leading B by 90 degrees. dir = 1 therefore renders A-leads, as
ValenceMotion.cpp:96 declares.
THE REVERSAL CORRECTION (d ? 3 : 1) IS ALSO RIGHT, and the brief's suspicion
that it inverted steady-state is wrong on two counts: it fires only on a
direction change, and its constants are the only ones that work. Let i_f and
i_r be the next index under forward and reverse for the same state:
  state 00  i_f 0 (raise A)  i_r 1 (raise B)
  state 01  i_f 1 (raise B)  i_r 2 (drop A)
  state 11  i_f 2 (drop A)   i_r 3 (drop B)
  state 10  i_f 3 (drop B)   i_r 0 (raise A)
so i_r = i_f + 1 for every state. Flipping TO reverse must therefore add 1 and
flipping TO forward must add 3, which is exactly (d ? 3 : 1). The old
(g_dir ? 1 : 3) would rewrite a line already at that level: no edge on the
wire and a phantom count. Steady state is untouched either way; it lives at
i += (fwd ? 1 : 3), which never changed.

WHY THE SCOPE SAID OTHERWISE, AND WHY IT COULD NOT HAVE SAID ANYTHING ELSE.
Phase is MIRROR-SYMMETRIC: a swapped probe pair and a swapped emitter table
produce byte-identical decodes. No amount of gray-step reading separates them.
The original acceptance run also anchored leg identity by the 2.5 s bench
spacing, which is not an anchor at all -- the park state between legs is the
LP's ABSOLUTE edge count mod 4, and that count includes every edge of the
constant-rate startup burst, so a park carries no leg identity.

WHAT DOES SEPARATE THEM, and it needs no probe move and no firmware change:
the absolute edge count. lp_quad.c walks (LPG15, LPG12) = (0,0) (1,0) (1,1)
(0,1) over k = count mod 4 from the LP's first edge, so the park LEVEL PAIR
names the pins outright once k is known, and k = (ORIGIN + census steps) mod 4.
ORIGIN is the free-running edges count at the pre-bench park, off the console.

MEASURED [verified 2026-09-21 -- DHO4204 at 192.168.1.12:5555, 1 Mpt at
5.00 us over a 5 s window, fixed 1.65 V threshold, patched
tools/lp_leg_capture.py, correlated to COM15 census on the same boot]
  ORIGIN = 23,278 (edges frozen at 23,278 from 5 s to 10 s, before the bench
  starts; the board did not reboot for the rest of the session, uptime 675 s).
  Reversal burst, identified BY STRUCTURE and not by timing -- the only burst
  carrying a direction flip, 1390.1 ms, -1 x 2505 then +1 x 2506, net 0:
  it PARKS AT CH1 = 1, CH2 = 0.
  It ends at census steps = -1, so k = (23278 - 1) mod 4 = 1, where the code
  puts LPG15 HIGH and LPG12 LOW.
  Therefore LPG15 IS ON CH1. The bench declares LPG15 on CH2. SWAPPED.
Cross-check, same record set: a 4173-edge single-direction leg parks CH1 = 0,
CH2 = 1, which is k = 3, i.e. census steps = +4173 -- the OUT leg, positive,
and it decodes gray -1 under the declared map. Same mirror, same cause.

CONSEQUENCE: every polarity claim in val-091.4's scope section is inverted in
its LABELS and unchanged in its NUMBERS. Counts, magnitudes, intervals,
illegal-transition totals and the reversal legality are all polarity-free and
all stand. 0 illegal transitions in every record taken this session.

OPERATOR ACTION, and it is a bench act, not a code change: swap the two probe
leads at the board (or correct the declared map). Until then
tools/lp_leg_capture.py carries the measurement: pass ORIGIN as its third
argument and read the PROBE IDENTITY line before trusting any polarity claim
it prints. Its docstring records the reversal as measured.

======================================================================
PROBE SWAP CONFIRMED AT THE HARDWARE 2026-09-21. The bead stays closed;
this is the confirming measurement for the operator action it asked for.

The operator physically swapped the two leads, so CH2 now carries LPG15 (A)
and CH1 carries LPG12 (B) -- the map tools/lp_leg_capture.py declares. No code
changed, here or in lp_quad.c.

MEASURED [verified 2026-09-21 -- DHO4204 at 192.168.1.12:5555, unpatched
tools/lp_leg_capture.py 5 6 23332, 1 Mpt at 5.00 us over a 5 s window, fixed
1.65 V threshold, NORM sweep + :RUN + dwell + :STOP; ORIGIN 23332 read off the
same boot's COM15 census, edges frozen at 23,332 through the 5 s and 10 s lines
before the bench starts]

PROBE IDENTITY, the line that settles it:
  "origin 23332, k=3 -> LPG15 parks LOW; measured CH1=1 CH2=0, so LPG15 is on
   CH2 (declared: CH2)"
Declared and measured now AGREE. Under the previous wiring the same arithmetic
read LPG15 on CH1.

PHASE, and it is the inverse of every label in val-091.4's scope section:
  reversal burst  1390.1 ms  +1 x 2504 then -1 x 2505, parks CH1=1 CH2=0
    -- the first half is POSITIVE by construction (benchTask submits +20 mm,
       then 0 mm 600 ms later), and it decodes gray +1, i.e. A (CH2) LEADS on a
       positive move. That is what lp_quad.c's forward table and
       ValenceMotion.cpp's dir = (v<0)?0:1 assert.
  out leg   +1 x 4173  (A leads)   parks CH1=0 CH2=1
  back leg  -1 x 3151  (B leads)   -- clipped by the 5 s record, magnitude is
                                      the window's, not the machine's
  edge interval min 235.0 us, max 10990.0 us, median 240.00 us (the 20 mm/s
  flat top is 239.7 us planned)

ILLEGAL TRANSITIONS: 0, in every record. Three records carried edges
(7,326 + 4,056 + 5,010 = 16,392 decoded transitions); two landed in the idle

NUMBERS UNCHANGED, LABELS CORRECTED: this bead's own conclusion (case (a),

title: flagship_p4 does not compile, and pio run reports SUCCESS without building it
description: src/CMakeLists.txt calls idf_component_register with no REQUIRES, so the component gets only the common requirements and never sees esp_timer, nvs_flash, esp_driver_parlio, esp_http_server (and their transitives, e.g. http_parser). Proven 2026-09-20 by running ninja directly on esp-idf/src/CMakeFiles/__idf_src.dir/hub/ValenceHub.cpp.obj: 'fatal error: esp_timer.h: No such file or directory'. esp-idf/src/CMakeFiles/__idf_src.dir/hub/ is EMPTY - no object was ever produced - yet 'pio run -d flagship_p4' answers SUCCESS in ~5 s without invoking ninja, and a stale firmware.elf sits in the build dir looking like evidence. Replaying the recorded compile command with the real GCC and four extra -I dirs got ValenceMotion.cpp to rc 0, so the include set is the only thing missing. Likely fix: declare REQUIRES on idf_component_register so cmake resolves the transitives; do NOT hand-list -I in .clangd, which would paper over a broken build. Second defect in its own right: a build that cannot fail is a green result that is a lie (C-8).
notes:
REFRAMED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-20: the firmware DOES compile and run --
the hub (val-091.3, SlopDeck LIVE) and the motion bench (val-091.4,
displacement verified) were both built from this tree and are running on the
P4 now. What the compile-database agent measured is that PlatformIO compiles
the APP sources through SCons with pioarduino's all-components include set,
while ninja's own __idf_src target (never invoked by PlatformIO; the agent ran
ninja by hand) fails because src/CMakeLists.txt's idf_component_register
declares no REQUIRES. Consequences that ARE real: (1) ninja's
compile_commands.json is incomplete for the app TUs, so clangd cannot resolve
esp_timer.h / nvs.h / driver/parlio_tx.h / esp_http_server.h; (2) a pure
idf.py build of this component would fail; (3) the manifest lies about its
dependencies. Fix: REQUIRES (and PRIV_REQUIRES where private) derived from the
actual includes -- esp_timer, nvs_flash, esp_driver_parlio, esp_http_server,
esp_wifi, esp_netif, esp_event, ulp, esp_hosted, esp_wifi_remote, plus what
transitively resolves -- then a CLEAN build (delete .pio) and a flash with
re-verification. Scheduled with the next flash (the rename image). Priority
lowered P1 -> P2: hygiene, not a broken build.

FIXED 2026-09-21. src/CMakeLists.txt now declares its dependencies.

REQUIRES esp_timer esp_http_server ulp
  -- reached from a header in the component's PUBLIC include dirs:
  esp_timer from hub/ValencePlatform.h (and lib/vlog), esp_http_server from
  hub/ValenceUiToken.h and hub/ValenceWsPort.h, ulp for ulp_embed_binary and
  the ulp_main.h it generates.
PRIV_REQUIRES esp_driver_parlio esp_event esp_netif esp_wifi lwip nvs_flash
              spi_flash espressif__esp_hosted espressif__esp_wifi_remote
  -- reached from .cpp only: driver/parlio_tx.h, esp_event.h, esp_netif.h,
  esp_wifi.h, lwip/sockets.h, nvs.h and nvs_flash.h, esp_flash.h,
  esp_hosted.h, and the injected esp_wifi impl headers. esp_hosted and
  esp_wifi_remote were already present, injected from idf_component.yml and
  not declared here.

DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. The include census over the app sources and headers is
50 distinct headers; everything not listed above resolves through IDF's common
requirements, which project_description.json gives as cxx newlib freertos

title: Firmware images carry a stale git label from configure time
description: Found 2026-10-10 (renumber agent): besides FIRMWARE_VERSION, each flagship_p4 image embeds a git label captured when the build was configured, not when it was built; it is stale in every image 0.1.38..0.1.42 (0.1.41 shows f4929c3-dirty). FIRMWARE_VERSION is the identity ota.py checks, but /diag and the boot log show the wrong commit. Fix: regenerate the label at build time (a pre-build step or a CMake custom target that always runs), with a check that the label matches HEAD.
close_reason: Fixed in 8941e40. Cause: IDF sets PROJECT_VER (esp_app_desc.version, the boot log's App version) from git describe at CMake configure, and pio reconfigures only on CMakeLists/sdkconfig/framework mtimes (espidf.py is_cmake_reconfigure_required), never on a HEAD move; -dirty also counted .beads/issues.jsonl. Fix: flagship_p4/git_label.py (pre: extra_script, every pio run) writes $BUILD_DIR/git_label.txt = short HEAD + -dirty for tracked changes outside .beads/issues.jsonl; on a change it deletes CMakeCache.txt so pio reconfigures; CMakeLists.txt sets PROJECT_VER from it. /diag header gains git=<label> after FIRMWARE_VERSION (ota.py parse unchanged). Proof on flagship_p4_bench, no clean between builds (2026-10-10): pre-commit image 0570cd0-dirty; after commit 8941e40 the build printed 'git label 0570cd0-dirty -> 8941e40' and the image reads 8941e40 (.beads/issues.jsonl modified, not counted); README edit -> 8941e40-dirty; revert -> 8941e40. A label change recompiles only esp_app_desc.c plus link (32 s); an unchanged label is a 6 s no-op. valencesim embeds no git label. canon_lint 0 findings; pio test -e native exit 0, 26 suites PASSED.

title: force_home's asserted stroke is replaced by max_rail at the next config push
description: MotionArbiter::forceHome sets _rail = stroke (at most the rail before it) and leaves _max_rail; any later changing config-set write runs pushConfigToMotion -> motionSetWindow(window, max_rail) -> takeWindow, which sets _rail = _max_rail = the pushed max_rail. So a force_home {stroke} shorter than max_rail holds only until the next jog_speed / window / input write; homed stays true and the arbiter then plans across max_rail. Found by reading during val-cem (54d20a8 mirrors the flipped window about the max_rail the write leaves, which is the rail after the push either way). Not reproduced on hardware. Question for triage: should force_home's stroke become max_rail (as a completed cycle's measurement does through adoptMeasuredRail), or should the push keep an asserted stroke? force_home is the RFC-025 hazard op, motorless-rig only.

title: Generators send each half-stroke at its due time, so every stroke plans from rest with zero acceleration
description: val-hnq (167a12d, 186a382) times strokes at least Kinetic's time-optimal rest-to-rest move x kRenderSlack 1.2, because a stroke submitted when the previous one ends is planned from a reset engine at (p, 0, 0): the Bezier needs its start acceleration ramped in at jmax, which costs up to 1.12 of the time-optimal profile. Sending each half-stroke ahead (anchor_us at its start, a lead over react_us) would solve consecutive crests together with continuous acceleration and drop the slack; a feel change across every pattern, so it needs an operator ruling and a bench A/B.

title: plan-strip norms are u16 x 10000: a plan outside the travel window saturates at 6.5535 and a negative share cannot be encoded
description:
Found by the Neutrino fleet soak (Phosphor ph-ode2). 0x1110 plan-strip carries start_norm, end_norm and cur_norm as u16 with scale 10000 (ValenceCatalog.h), so a plan position outside the travel window cannot be told: above it saturates at 6.5535, below it (a negative share) has no encoding at all. Both happen in ordinary use: override jogs outside the window (SPEC 11.1), and a window write that leaves the carriage outside it.
Seen: `node test/fleet/fleet.mjs --replay 388 --minutes 10` (Phosphor lane lp/fleet): carriage parked at 149.74 mm under a window of 3.5..23.0 mm reads cur_norm 6.5535 (true share 7.5) for minutes.
A client drawing the strip (Phosphor's rail, the funscript twin) then shows the plan at a wrong place. Options: a signed type (i16 or i32 at the same scale) for the three fields, or the window-share clamp stated in the catalog desc so a client knows the value is clamped. Wire-layout change: before the v1.0 tag it is an etag move.
notes:
Ruling (Valence RFC agent, 2026-10-09): a Nucleus encoding bug, not a spec defect; no RFC. The spec and registry fix no type, scale or range for plan positions: registry field_roles plan.start, plan.end and plan.current say only "normalized ... position" (SPEC 8.8 lists the roles), and the plan-strip fields do not declare unit_id 4. The u16 x 10000 encoding is Nucleus's own: ValenceCatalog.h addPlanStrip (start_norm, end_norm, cur_norm as PackedFieldType::u16, scale 10000) and ValenceDevice.cpp publishPlanStrip (wireU16 saturates). Fix here: a signed type wide enough for the shares the hub produces. i16 at scale 10000 still clips at 3.2767 (the soak's 7.5 share would read 3.2767), so i32 at scale 10000 (layout 19 -> 25 B, well under 242) or i16 at a coarser scale; same field order. Before the v1.0 tag that is an etag move (SPEC 5.4's tail-only rule binds released layouts). Side note, not this bug: the role notes do not say what "normalized" is relative to (travel window or measured travel); Nucleus and Phosphor both read it as a window share. Pinning that would be an editorial registry note by RFC, not a wire change.

Final 0.1.39 image is 105e6fb (fix commits 167a12d + 186a382), sha256 92316e9eaa0fb251122301f3748bb929d44076a3dd29f7e5639054ed7d453f21; catalog etag 83f67d8b16f12749.
close_reason: 167a12d (fw 0.1.39): 0x1110 start_norm, end_norm, cur_norm are i32 at scale 10000, declared so in the catalog (layout 19 -> 25 B); etag 99c7be4f31c520c4 -> 83f67d8b16f12749. [verified 2026-10-10 -- test_valence_device VD-PLAN-1: -0.25, 7.5 and 6.6 shares on the wire as -2500, 75000, 66000; Phosphor lp/neutrino test/plan-strip.test.mjs decodes them through valence-js by the declared type] Phosphor's readers (PlanStrip, LinkBar, the player's planShare, the fleet client) read decoded values; no hard-coded u16 found. title: cfg_gen wraps through 0; a cfg blob persisted while it sits at 0 is refused whole on the next boot
description: Valence Hub::_cfgGen is a u16 that starts at 1 and advances with a bare ++ (hub.hpp:863, hub_impl.hpp:1763 and 3728 at valence.pin a88c6bf), and SPEC 4.2 does not reserve 0, so after 65,535 effective changes it passes through 0. ValenceHub.cpp persistDue() writes cfgGen() as it stands, and StoredState.h decodeConfig() refuses a stored cfg_gen of 0 whole (NoGeneration since 3f3653e): that machine boots on factory config, uncommissioned. Rare per write, reachable over a machine's life because every changed value is a bump (a slider drag is many). Fix options: accept 0 in decodeConfig (hubBegin's restore loop terminates for any stored value), or have the library skip 0 on wrap, which is a Valence RFC. Found during val-mz7 by code reading, not observed.
close_reason: 277a3e5: decodeConfig accepts stored cfg_gen 0 (hub u16 wraps through it, SPEC 4.2 reserves none); NoGeneration removed; test covers 65535 and 0

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text:
2026-10-02, af4510b. Per operator ruling 2026-10-02. (1) No fan fitted: a kick that ends with no tach pulse latches "no fan fitted" for the boot (duty 0, mode off, no more kicks, logged once); a fan that showed a tach once and later shows none stays a stall. The open-loop tach-less branch is deleted (unreachable). (2) Sanity window plus the pull direction: the divider's 10k pull-up goes to the rail (Hardware SPEC 2026-09-22 sensing row), so an open J7 reads full scale = the table's cold end; colder than kSaneMinC = -10 C is NaN. The hot side keeps the table's end so a real overheat is never discarded. (3) kOffsetC untouched.
What this does NOT do, stated plainly: a floating G16 on a bare devkit still reads a plausible temperature (61 C on the bench): S/H residue from the other ADC1 channels, indistinguishable from a real NTC by the voltage alone. The no-fan verdict is what keeps the fan off there; the therm= number on the liveness line stays meaningless on a devkit.
RECORDED AS VETO-ABLE: a two-wire fan on J6 now reads as absent and is not driven (the board fan is non-critical by the operator's cooling model, Hardware SPEC 2026-09-23 heatsink row); a reboot re-probes.

title: Ruling: persist source.background_run across reboot?
description: Split from val-wcm (2026-09-25); held RAM-only on board and sim by the dispatching agent's instruction pending this ruling. What persisting it would and would not do: the generator's running flag is NEVER persisted, so a reboot alone cannot start motion. What survives is the POLICY: after a power cycle, the next pattern start whose session then drops keeps running unattended without anyone having re-chosen that, possibly on a different operator's session. Options: (a) persist it (the catalog calls it a standing policy); (b) keep it volatile, so every boot returns to stop-when-orphaned. If (a), it goes in its own blob or the presets blob, NOT the cfg blob, because it does not move cfg_gen. Code sites: ValenceDevice::applyPattern key 7; ValenceCatalog.h comment on 0x3200 key 7.
close_reason: Operator ruling 2026-10-03: no. A reboot never resumes a generator by itself; source.background_run is not persisted.

comments.text: DEFERRED 2026-10-01 (scope, not design). This bead asks for ONE implementation: lift ValenceUiTokenMinter's slot table, rate gate and HMAC derivation into a hardware-free core both hosts compile. A sim-only HMAC copy was considered and refused: it is the T20 hand-copy class (val-sf7.1 found the last one already drifted), and the wire cannot tell HMAC from random bytes, so it buys nothing a test can see. DESIGN: flagship_p4/src/hub/UiTokenTable.h, header-only, no IDF include. State: slots[4], secret[32], counter, lastMintMs. Methods called WITH THE HOST'S LOCK HELD: std::optional<uint32_t> claimMint(nowMs) (rate gate + ++counter), install(token, nowMs) (oldest-expiring victim, used first), bool consume(token, nowMs) (wrap-safe expiry, constant-time compare, single use). One unlocked static: derive(secret, counter, nowMs) = hmacSha256(secret, counter LE || now LE)[0..15]. The lock stays in each host because it is the only platform difference: the board keeps its file-scope portMUX (internal RAM, T4) and the two-pass mint with the HMAC outside the critical section; SimUiToken keeps std::mutex and IXWebSocket's HTTP server. The SoftwareCrypto comparator stays at namespace scope (T4). New native suite test_ui_token: rate gate at 249/250 ms, single use, expiry across the u32 wrap, victim choice, derive() determinism. title: Upstream: WELCOME limits.retained_pending is unstable across sessions (0 or 4 for the same four retained STATE pushes)
description: Measured 2026-09-20 during the SlopDeck LIVE check on the P4 hub (val-091.3): four consecutive browser sessions against an unchanged 0.1.0-p4hub all received the same four retained STATE channels (0x0003, 0x0004, 0x0006, 0x1000), but WELCOME reported retained_pending=0 on three of them and 4 on the other. registry.yaml:247 defines it as the count of retained STATE pushes that will follow WELCOME, and the JS client uses it as the snapshot-complete gate (SlopSync/clients/js/session.js:849, 912-917: LIVE once adoptedChannels.size >= retained_pending). At 0 the gate passes trivially, so a client cannot rely on it to know the snapshot is complete. Also unobserved in all four sessions: retained pushes for 0x000A pending-pairing and 0x000D paired-devices-roster, both advertised STATE and both seeded per the port notes. The value is computed by the pinned hub library (hub_impl.hpp builds WELCOME), not by Valence code, so the fix is upstream in SlopSync, not in flagship_p4. Never blocked LIVE; recorded so it is not rediscovered.
close_reason: Fixed client-side per operator ruling 2026-10-01: Valence fa70b0d (feat/rfc-050-blob-done). session.js carries opts.subscriptions in HELLO key 10, LIVE gate counts only WELCOME-granted STATE. [verified 2026-10-01 -- clients/js/test/valence-retained-sim.test.mjs vs valencesim :8482]: before fresh=0 reattach=3; after fresh=3 reattach=3, same session_id, gate 3/3 both. Phosphor's own session passes no HELLO wishes (subscribes catalog-resolved after the catalog), so its fresh WELCOME still promises 0 by definition. 0x000A/0x000D pushes not addressed.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE MEASURED, hub is consistent with its definition; the fix is client-side or spec text, so DEFERRED. [verified 2026-10-01 -- scripted session against valencesim (port 8282), probe helpers]: fresh HELLO with no subscription wishes -> retained_pending=0; abrupt socket drop then re-HELLO with the SAME instance_id (RFC-042 reattach) -> retained_pending=4; fresh HELLO carrying the 4 wishes -> 4. Mechanism: Valence lib/valence/include/valence/hub/hub_impl.hpp counts retained_pending over WELCOME's own grants only, which on a fresh session are built from HELLO's wishes (handleHello ~:642) and on a reattach from the session's migrated subscriptions (handleReattach ~:891). Valence clients/js/session.js never puts wishes in HELLO; it SUBSCRIBEs after WELCOME (:1271), so a fresh session reads 0 and its SYNCING->LIVE gate (adoptedChannels.size >= retained_pending, :1211/checkLiveTransition) passes trivially, while an autoReconnect that reattaches reads 4. That is the 3x0 / 1x4 split. Fix candidates, none in Nucleus and none a hub change: (a) session.js sends its subscription wishes in HELLO (then fresh and reattach agree), or (b) its LIVE gate also counts STATE grants from its own SUBSCRIBE's GRANT, or (c) an RFC clarifying that retained_pending covers only WELCOME's grants and naming the completeness signal for a mid-session SUBSCRIBE. session.js holds uncommitted operator work today, so it was not touched. The missing 0x000A/0x000D pushes are a separate question (likely access-gated grants for a watch-tier browser session), not measured here.

title: Upstream: slopsync_probe.py hardcodes SlopDrive's motion/pattern channels; gate device-channel steps on catalog presence
description: Measured 2026-09-20 against the P4 hub (val-091.3): '27 passed, 12 failed, 7 skipped', identical on two back-to-back runs, and all 12 failures are steps 4/4b (SlopSync/tools/slopsync_probe.py:2035, :2079-2147) subscribing to and asserting on 0x1100/0x1110/0x1111/0x1020/0x1200/0x4100 plus motion_state/motion_raw/plan_strip/motion_diag/odometer/pattern_mask UNCONDITIONALLY. Only power (0x1010) is catalog-conditional and SKIPs correctly. SPEC section 6.3: a feature exists iff its channels exist, so a conformance verifier must gate device-channel steps on the catalog the hub actually advertises, the way it already does for power. This is a SlopSync tool fix, made THERE (the sibling is read-only from this repo; the RFC-QUEUE door is for spec text, this is a tool). Until it lands, the honest stamp for a motionless hub is 27/12/7 with this reason attached; flipping has_motion=true to go green is the dead-gauge lie the SPEC forbids. Operator memory: SlopSync work waits for the firmware to settle; this is recorded so it is not rediscovered.
notes:
SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-09-21 (val-091.10): step 5.9 safety_modes, and it needs a
DIFFERENT fix from the twelve channel steps.

EXACT FAILURE TEXT [verified 2026-09-21 -- slopsync_probe.py --ip 192.168.1.118
--port 82 against the P4 hub, reproduced on three separate runs across two
images]
  == Step 5.9: safety ops -- override/bypass on 0x0005 (RFC-025c) ==
    x override_on NACKed: UNSUPPORTED_OP
  x  safety_modes           FAIL
  28 passed, 13 failed, 5 skipped

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THE 27/12/7 vs 28/13/5 CONFUSION: it is the --no-motion
FLAG, not a regression. slopsync_probe.py:2394 gates step 5.9 on skip_intent =
args.no_motion or args.listen_only (:1529), so with --no-motion safety_modes is
SKIPped and never runs. Both counts were reproduced back to back on ONE image
before any change: --no-motion gives 27/12/7 (safety_modes SKIP, byte-identical
to this bead original measurement) and a full run gives 28/13/5. Nothing in the
hub changed between val-091.3 and val-091.9 to cause it.

THE HUB IS CONFORMANT AND THE SPEC SAYS SO DIRECTLY.
  SPEC.md 11.1 (line 914): "a hub whose application does not implement a level
  MUST NACK UNSUPPORTED_OP and latch nothing. That is discoverable and honest
  -- without it, a generic client could not know whether sending HOLD to an
  arbitrary hub did anything at all."
  registry.yaml:609, 0x0303 UNSUPPORTED_OP: "intent op not implemented on this
  hub".
The P4 hub has no drive, so there is no manual override to engage. Its delegate
NACKs UNSUPPORTED_OP and latches nothing, which is the letter of 11.1. estop
and estop_clear are hub-owned and never reach the delegate, so the red button
is unaffected. NO HUB CHANGE WAS MADE.

WHY THIS ONE CANNOT BE FIXED THE WAY power (0x1010) IS. The twelve channel
failures are gateable on catalog presence because a missing channel IS the
capability answer (SPEC 6.3). 0x0005 is a CORE channel that every hub carries,
and the catalog option_access list (key 17) declares each op TIER, not whether
it is implemented. The SPEC discovery mechanism for an unimplemented op is the
NACK itself. So the fix here is an extra arm, not an extra condition:
UNSUPPORTED_OP on a safety op must read as a conformant PASS ("this hub does
not implement override/bypass") and only a MALFORMED/ACCESS_DENIED/silence, or
an ECHO whose snapshot does not follow, is a real failure. The ground-truth
assertion (ECHO must be followed by a 9-byte snapshot with the bit set) stays
exactly as it is for a hub that DOES implement it.

Honest stamp for a motionless hub is now 28 passed / 13 failed / 5 skipped on a
full run, 27/12/7 with --no-motion, with this reason attached to all thirteen.

title: Force feedback by admittance: INA228 + drive current + encoder fused into a position yield in the oscillator slot; toy profiles with soft window zones; firmware autotune
description:
Design home, operator 2026-10-08, parked until the Flagship board exists (RS485 to the drive on the hub, INA228 on the 36 V bus). Nothing here is designed in detail before the bench measures what the bus current looks like during a stroke with a toy mounted.

The idea: the hub reads force and yields position, so a toy can be soft where it needs to be (slack around its knot) without starving the motor.

1. Why not motor-side torque. The drive is a pulse follower: a lower torque limit means the encoder falls behind the hub's count, position truth desyncs, the fence lies, and a Modbus write per zone crossing costs milliseconds in a 1 ms loop. Softness comes from moving the commanded position (admittance: force in, position out), never from the drive's torque.

2. Where it lives. An additive stage in the arbiter in the oscillator's slot (RFC-103, planTick's PLANNED CHANGE after the planner sample, before the window clamp): in a marked window zone, when the measured force exceeds the toy's threshold, add a yield to the planned position, bounded by the ceilings and the window, relax it when the force drops; yields first, census flags, the planner never learns about toys. Strip, steer and LP core unchanged.

3. Sensors, three bandwidths. INA228 bus current: fast, loud, sees regen too, the edge detector. Drive current register (0x0F) over RS485: cleaner, Modbus-rate, calibrates what a bus current means for this toy. Encoder (0x16/0x17) vs the hub's count: slowest, the only direct compliance read. Good for a knot-zone yield at tens of hertz; not a 1 kHz haptic loop until an encoder line reaches the P4.

4. Autotune. The 2026-10-07/08 ladder (docs/drive-bench-2026-10-07.md, tools/aim/) moved into firmware: drive the rail, read encoder and current, step accel until following error or current crosses the toy's line, store. The hub as the one Modbus master retires the COM2 single-master rule.

5. Toy profiles (the protocol piece, a Valence RFC when it is time): a toy is a setting bundle (accel ceiling, window zones with force thresholds, oscillator cap); the hub stores and renders it, any client picks it by role. Draft the wire shape early because it outlives the sensing.

Related: val-dzf (oscillator wiring), kin-4d0, val-3kd (max_rail), feedback-machine-not-cnc, Hardware/flagship design-considerations.md.
notes: NAME RESERVED (operator 2026-10-08): Muon for the characterization/autotune tool (muon tomography: probing through the machine): tools/aim ladder, firmware autotune, admittance calibration.
